docs.title: Rook
docs.text:
Restart operator to re-invoke cluster init:

kubectl -n rook-ceph delete pod -l app=rook-ceph-operator

Get into a place you can use the regular commands:

kubectl --namespace rook-ceph exec -it deploy/rook-ceph-operator -- bash

TODO Move this

kubectl --namespace rook-ceph exec -it deploy/rook-ceph-operator -- bash
rook multus validation run --public-network=network/multus-public --cluster-network=network/multus-ceph -n rook-ceph
This leaves a MESS so you need to run:

rook multus validation cleanup --namespace rook-ceph

Then the next validation:

rook multus validation config converged

Example:

thaynes@HaynesHyperion:~$ kubectl --namespace rook-ceph exec -it deploy/rook-ceph-operator -- bash
Defaulted container "rook-ceph-operator" out of: rook-ceph-operator, k8tz (init)
[rook@rook-ceph-operator-69745fc466-pc95r /]$ rook multus validation run --help
2024/10/26 10:59:57 maxprocs: Leaving GOMAXPROCS=20: CPU quota undefined

Run a validation test that determines whether the current Multus and system
configurations will support Rook with Multus.

This should be run BEFORE Rook is installed.

This is a fairly long-running test. It starts up a web server and many
clients to verify that Multus network communication works properly.

It does *not* perform any load testing. Networks that cannot support high
volumes of Ceph traffic may still encounter runtime issues. This may be
particularly noticeable with high I/O load or during OSD rebalancing
(see: https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/architecture/#rebalancing).
For example, during Rook or Ceph cluster upgrade.

Override the kube config file location by setting the KUBECONFIG environment variable.

Usage:
  rook multus validation run [--public-network=<nad-name>] [--cluster-network=<nad-name>] [flags]

Flags:
      --cluster-network string                   The name of the Network Attachment Definition (NAD) that will be used for Ceph's cluster network. This should be a namespaced name in the form <namespace>/<name> if the NAD is defined in a different namespace from the cluster namespace.
  -c, --config string                            The validation test config file to use. This cannot be used with other flags except --host-check-only.
      --daemons-per-node int                     The number of validation test daemons to run per node. It is recommended to set this to the maximum number of Ceph daemons that can run on any node in the worst case of node failure(s). The default value is set to the worst-case value for a Rook Ceph cluster with 3 portable OSDs, 3 portable monitors, and where all optional child resources have been created with 1 daemon such that they all might run on a single node in a failure scenario. If you aren't sure what to choose for this value, add 1 for each additional OSD beyond 3. (default 19)
      --flaky-threshold-seconds timeoutSeconds   This is the time window in which validation clients are all expected to become 'Ready' together. Validation clients are all started at approximately the same time, and they should all stabilize at approximately the same time. Once the first validation client becomes 'Ready', the tool checks that all of the remaining clients become 'Ready' before this threshold duration elapses. In networks that have connectivity issues, limited bandwidth, or high latency, clients will contend for network traffic with each other, causing some clients to randomly fail and become 'Ready' later than others. These randomly-failing clients are considered 'flaky.' Adjust this value to reflect expectations for the underlying network. For fast and reliable networks, this can be set to a smaller value. For networks that are intended to be slow, this can be set to a larger value. Additionally, for very large Kubernetes clusters, it may take longer for all clients to start, and it therefore may take longer for all clients to become 'Ready'; in that case, this value can be set slightly higher. (default 30s)
  -h, --help                                     help for run
      --host-check-only                          Only check that hosts can connect to the server via the public network. Do not start clients. This mode is recommended when a Rook cluster is already running and consuming the public network specified.
  -n, --namespace string                         The namespace for validation test resources. It is recommended to set this to the namespace in which Rook's Ceph cluster will be installed. (default "rook-ceph")
      --nginx-image string                       The Nginx image used for the validation server and clients. (default "quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:stable-alpine")
      --public-network string                    The name of the Network Attachment Definition (NAD) that will be used for Ceph's public network. This should be a namespaced name in the form <namespace>/<name> if the NAD is defined in a different namespace from the cluster namespace.
      --service-account string                   The name of the service account that will be used for test resources. (default "rook-ceph-system")
      --timeout-minutes timeoutMinutes           The time to wait for resources to change to the expected state. For example, for the test web server to start, for test clients to become ready, or for test resources to be deleted. At longest, this may need to reflect the time it takes for client pods to to pull images, get address assignments, and then for each client to determine that its network connection is stable. Minimum: 1 minute. Recommended: 2 minutes or more. (default 3m0s)

Global Flags:
      --log-level string   logging level for logging/tracing output (valid values: ERROR,WARNING,INFO,DEBUG) (default "INFO")
[rook@rook-ceph-operator-69745fc466-pc95r /]$ rook multus validation config --help
2024/10/26 11:00:16 maxprocs: Leaving GOMAXPROCS=20: CPU quota undefined
Generate a validation test config file for different default scenarios to stdout.

Usage:
  rook multus validation config [command]

Available Commands:
  converged               Example config for a cluster that runs storage and user workloads on all nodes.
  dedicated-storage-nodes Example config file for a cluster that uses dedicated storage nodes.
  stretch-cluster         Example config file for a stretch cluster with dedicated storage nodes.

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for config

Global Flags:
      --log-level string   logging level for logging/tracing output (valid values: ERROR,WARNING,INFO,DEBUG) (default "INFO")

Use "rook multus validation config [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: Cluseter Finalizer
docs.text:
kubectl patch cephcluster rook-ceph -n rook-ceph --type=json -p='[{"op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/finalizers"}]'

for CRD in $(kubectl get crd -n rook-ceph | awk '/ceph.rook.io/ {print $1}'); do
    kubectl get -n rook-ceph "$CRD" -o name | \
    xargs -I {} kubectl patch -n rook-ceph {} --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers": []}}'
done

kubectl -n rook-ceph patch configmap rook-ceph-mon-endpoints --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers": []}}'
kubectl -n rook-ceph patch secrets rook-ceph-mon --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers": []}}'

docs.title: Finish off metadata
docs.text:
Talos may need some massaging:

$ cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: disk-clean
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: <storage-node-name>
  volumes:
  - name: rook-data-dir
    hostPath:
      path: <dataDirHostPath>
  containers:
  - name: disk-clean
    image: busybox
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: rook-data-dir
      mountPath: /node/rook-data
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "rm -rf /node/rook-data/*"]
EOF
pod/disk-clean created

$ kubectl wait --timeout=900s --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}=Succeeded' pod disk-clean
pod/disk-clean condition met

$ kubectl delete pod disk-clean
pod "disk-clean" deleted

And wipe the disks:

cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: disk-wipe
  namespace: rook-ceph
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: talosm03
  containers:
  - name: disk-wipe
    image: busybox
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=100 oflag=direct of=/dev/nvme1n1"]
EOF
pod/disk-wipe created

$ kubectl wait --timeout=900s --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}=Succeeded' pod disk-wipe
pod/disk-wipe condition met

$ kubectl delete pod disk-wipe
pod "disk-wipe" deleted

docs.title: Retries Exceeded
docs.text:
I see this when things take a while because something else is broken (like a csi) but there is no reason to fix the thing that is stuck. First force helmrelease to get fixed:

flux reconcile helmrelease -n home-automation home-assistant --force

Then get the kustomization in a good state again (if the helmrelease was OK):

flux reconcile kustomization -n flux-system zigbee2mqtt

Here are some commands for managing Kubernetes.

docs.title: Clean Mess
docs.text:
Check what you are deleting:

kubectl get pod --field-selector=status.phase==Succeeded -A
kubectl get pod --field-selector=status.phase==Failed -A

If nothing to debug go ahead and kill em:

kubectl delete pod --field-selector=status.phase==Succeeded -A
kubectl delete pod --field-selector=status.phase==Failed -A

Rebooting sometimes creates a mess and this will clean it but I thing they go away after a bit.

docs.title: Namespace w/ Spec Finalizer
docs.text:
This was super hard to get rid of vs. a regular namespace! 

kubectl get ns rook-ceph -o json | jq '.spec.finalizers = []' | kubectl replace --raw "/api/v1/namespaces/rook-ceph/finalize" -f -

  • Delete kubernetes finalizer in tmp.json (leave empty array "finalizers": [])
  • Run kubectl proxy in another terminal for auth purposes and run following curl request to returned port
kubectl proxy &
curl -k -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X PUT --data-binary @tmp.json 127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/namespaces/rook-ceph/finalize

docs.title: Omni
docs.text: For this cluster I am taking advantage of omni from Sidero Labs to manage my Talos installation. The home-ops clusters I've reviewed rely heavily on talosctl to manage their clusters but I wanted to skip a few steps and for $10/month I figured it was worth a shot. After getting more familiar with Talos and Omni I do think you can live with out it but I am enjoying the auth and VPN access that comes out of the box.

docs.title: The Journey Begins
docs.text:
At this point I've gotten started but documenting as I go endes up being a mess so here's the goods:

I'll recap how the story went so far but first some TODOs:

  • Bootstraping flux sets those limits but I'm not sure why

Try:

WARNING Wiping disks is for ceph. They wipe /dev/nvme# which happens to change all the time when talos re-images the OS. Make sure these paths are correct before running this!!!

TODO Devcontainer needs helm plugin install https://github.com/databus23/helm-diff because helm plugin list is missing diff and if the initial apps fail they complain the second time that you need this diff thing! 

task omni:validate                # schema-check the cluster template first
task omni:sync                    # provision/assign the nodes
task flux:install-helm-apps       # cilium + coredns + csr-approver + spegel (pre-Flux core)
task rook:wipe-disks-talosm01     # each of these prompts before it erases anything
task rook:wipe-disks-talosm02
task rook:wipe-disks-talosm03
task rook:wipe-disks-talosm04
task rook:wipe-disks-talosm05
task flux:bootstrap               # needs age.key — run from the workstation

The helm-apps step used to be task talos:install-helm-apps. The whole talos: namespace was talhelper-based and was removed in the 2026-09-22 taskfile audit — Omni owns the machine config, so a raw talosctl upgrade would fight it. Upgrades go through task omni:sync; see .agents/runbooks/talos-version-upgrade.md.

docs.title: PVE
docs.text:
Once nothing is running on the node we can follow these steps to remove nodes from proxmox.

Delete the node with:

pvecm delnode <NODE>

Then clean it out here:

root@pve01:/etc/pve/nodes# cd /etc/pve/nodes
root@pve01:/etc/pve/nodes# rm -R pve05/

You can also clean the node itself out by deleting:

systemctl stop pve-cluster corosync
pmxcfs -l
rm /etc/corosync/*
rm /etc/pve/corosync.conf
killall pmxcfs
systemctl start pve-cluster

And rm -R /etc/pve/nodes but I didn't get that far.

docs.title: Clean Drives
docs.text:
Boot using Gparted and delete any data on the drives we will be using. This is especially important for Ceph as that is picky and hard to fix up the drives from Talos.

Once you add the node to the cluster, before configurign Ceph, run this to wipe the partition table:

$ cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: disk-wipe
  namespace: rook-ceph
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: talosm01
  containers:
  - name: disk-wipe
    image: busybox
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=100 oflag=direct of=/dev/nvme0n1"]
EOF

docs.title: Apply pikvm.yaml in one paste
docs.text:
pikvm.yaml on main is the source of truth. On the PiKVM web terminal run su - (enter the root password), then paste this single line. It backs up the current override, downloads the repo copy to a temp file (a failed download changes nothing), validates it with kvmd -m, restarts kvmd, and on any failure restores the old file and restarts kvmd again. It prints APPLIED or ROLLED_BACK:

rw; cp /etc/kvmd/override.yaml /etc/kvmd/override.yaml.bak && curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thaynes43/haynes-ops/main/pikvm.yaml -o /tmp/pikvm.yaml && cp /tmp/pikvm.yaml /etc/kvmd/override.yaml && { kvmd -m >/dev/null && systemctl restart kvmd && echo APPLIED || { cp /etc/kvmd/override.yaml.bak /etc/kvmd/override.yaml; systemctl restart kvmd; echo ROLLED_BACK; }; }; ro

TESmart mapping: kvmd serverN / pin N is switch input PCN+1 (server0 = PC1 ... server15 = PC16, the switch is 16-port). Edit pikvm.yaml in git, never on the device.

docs.title: fstrim
docs.text:
See Bernd-home-ops, has fstrim service runing

fstrim is a command-line utility in Linux used to discard (or "trim") unused blocks on a mounted filesystem. When files are deleted or moved, the filesystem updates its metadata to mark those blocks as free. However, the underlying storage device may not be aware that these blocks are no longer in use. Running fstrim informs the storage device about the unused blocks, allowing it to manage its storage space more efficiently.

docs.title: OpenProject — deployment and acceptance
docs.text: Status: proposed, not deployed or ready. No source work is imported. The separately requested haynesnetwork migration follows only after login, API and persistence acceptance. The disposable proof namespace was deleted without starting a Pod.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
OpenProject Community 17.9.2, digest-pinned official slim image, bjw-s app-template 5.3.0. One web replica (Recreate) runs vendor migration/seeding as an init container; a separate vendor background worker waits for the database schema. Stock Memcached supplies the shared cache. A stock NGINX sidecar runs documented auth_request configuration; no custom authentication service or application patch.

A dedicated CNPG PostgreSQL 17 singleton uses 20Gi Ceph RBD; attachments use a 20Gi CephFS RWX claim. Both stateful inventories carry prune protection. Do not rename/move the Flux Kustomization or database/PVC without an explicit retention cutover: inventory pruning can otherwise remove the claim and leave Pods Pending. The singleton tolerates node-recovery downtime; backups are the recovery path, not a claim of database HA. Capacity inspection found approximately 14TiB raw Ceph free, with 3.8TiB maximum available in the relevant replicated pools.

frontend/openproject is the reconcile target. Merge only after the approved identity/credential prerequisites below exist, required CI passes and relevant review findings are resolved. Never deploy reachable admin/admin; the seeded administrator has a generated password and is locked from creation.

docs.title: Authenticated browser access and private API
docs.text:
https://work.haynesnetwork.com follows the established external ingress pattern: external-dns creates the proxied hostname toward ingress-ext.haynesnetwork.com, the existing tunnel's domain rule delivers to external Traefik, and the existing certificate-haynesnetwork covers TLS. Tom explicitly approved this Internet reachability on 2026-10-15 at 21:03 UTC so lab users can work without VPN. It supersedes the earlier LAN/VPN-only haynesops.com direction for this app. No tunnel, wildcard-route or shared gateway configuration is changed. Only this exact Host rule reaches the browser gateway, which checks Authentik before any application content. The Rails backend, database, LDAP and bot API stay private.

Humans authenticate through the existing Authentik/MFA path. The new single-app proxy provider initially admits only the existing authentik Admins group; Tom approved that exact initial group on 2026-10-15. No memberships change. NGINX captures identity only from the successful outpost response, validates the login shape, overwrites inbound assertions and appends its protected shared secret. The app's optional-header mode is disabled, login is required and user registration is disabled. Human application records come from verified LDAP lookup and do not need a separate human password.

Dedicated proxy and LDAP outposts belong only to this app. Their resources are ClusterIP, have no ingress or Kubernetes token mount, and use the internal Authentik service for control traffic with its normal browser URL. Existing outpost provider lists and human flows are unchanged. The new LDAP service bind uses an app-password-only flow and only the openproject-ldap service account may access that LDAP application. Its full-directory-search permission is scoped to this single provider. The OpenProject search filter further selects active members of authentik Admins. No LDAP attribute grants OpenProject administrator status automatically. Account rename/reassignment and application-role changes need deliberate handling; the LDAP/proxy key is the controlled username (cn).

LDAP uses verified TLS on the dedicated service DNS name. A generated certificate named OpenProject LDAP must cover ak-outpost-openproject-ldap.network.svc.cluster.local. Only its public trust certificate enters the application's 1Password item. The private key remains in Authentik's normal protected store/outpost lifecycle. Do not disable certificate verification as a shortcut. Supply givenName and sn LDAP attributes for the admitted users when absent, derived from their existing display names; this is an explicit identity-metadata prerequisite, not a change to login identifiers.

The agent API is http://openproject-web.frontend.svc.cluster.local:8082/api/v3/ inside the cluster. Cilium admits it only from the existing dev-env workload. Its stock NGINX listener preserves Bearer Authorization, strips cookies/identity headers and rejects non-API paths. OpenProject performs token authentication and project permissions. The direct application listener is bound to Pod loopback. The additive dev-env API/DNS Cilium policy changes no existing Pod/config/session and must not restart Chapter7 or modify its coordinator's resources.

Browser access tokens currently expire after five minutes. Measure cached-session behavior; do not claim directory disable or group removal immediately revokes an existing proxy/application session. Test logout, account locking, group removal, proxy invalidation and API-token revocation before declaring ready. If the owner requires a shorter revocation bound, set and verify that bound before use.

docs.title: Required action-time approvals and provisioning
docs.text:
The deployment authorization covers ordinary GitOps authoring, PRs and validation. Tom approved the following exact scope on 2026-10-15. The 1Password Connect token is read-only (item creation returned HTTP 403); populate the dedicated item securely in 1Password before merge. No other credential flow is authorized:

  1. Manually create only HaynesKube/openproject securely in 1Password. The existing Connect token cannot create items. Required fields: DB_PASSWORD, HEADER_SECRET, BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD, and LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD must each contain 64 random hex characters; SECRET_KEY_BASE must contain 128 random hex characters; LDAP_CA_CERT contains the public PEM certificate below. No raw value is printed or committed. ExternalSecrets deliver app, CNPG basic-auth and the one-time LDAP provisioning Job's dedicated bind Secret. No unrelated application credential is reused. Add API_TOKEN (opapi- followed by 64 random hex characters) in the same item. It is delivered only to the dedicated dev/openproject-agent-credentials helper, which has no service, network access, Kubernetes token or other secret. The helper lives in its own retained Flux app, kubernetes/main/apps/dev/openproject-agent/ (Kustomization dev/openproject-agent), not in the v1 dev-env app, so v1 cleanup keeps it. scripts/openproject/agent-api.py runs inside existing dev-env and captures only that token file through its existing approved pods/exec capability, in process memory, then authenticates to the fixed private API origin. It follows no redirects and never prints or stores the token. No dev-env Secret-read grant, mount/env change or restart is required. Do not exec into the application web container to obtain the bot credential.
  2. Apply only 96-openproject-private.yaml: new app/proxy/LDAP providers, dedicated service bind flow/account, provider-scoped search permission, app policies and two dedicated outposts. Generate the LDAP service app-password to match the dedicated 1Password field and its provider certificate through stock Authentik interfaces. Add only the required name attributes if absent. Do not modify existing human identities' passwords, identifiers, groups or MFA flows.
  3. Apply the exact new external browser ingress/DNS and Cilium policies in this PR, approved by Tom at 21:03 UTC. The only admitted browser source is external Traefik; the only bot source remains dev-env. The Internet path must pass Authentik/MFA and the unchanged authentik Admins policy. No anonymous app content, public bot route or general API authentication exemption is allowed.
  4. Deliver existing approved aws/volsync-hayesops backup credentials to this application's backup controllers only, writing a dedicated Barman server prefix openproject-postgres17-v1 in the existing cnpg-haynesops bucket and a distinct restic suffix /openproject-assets. No bucket/credential/retention change for other applications. Provision one named non-admin app writer and one reviewer role after startup, with API material stored through 1Password; workers cannot approve their own work. Tom approved openproject-agent, limited to the managed project, without deletion, approval or acceptance rights. Store its API token as API_TOKEN in the same dedicated item; never reuse a human credential.

After blueprint and ExternalSecret reconciliation, run the one-time in-cluster provisioning Job via KUBECONFIG=… python3 scripts/openproject/launch-ldap-bind-job.py. The Job runs scripts/openproject/provision-ldap-bind.py. It consumes only dev/openproject-ldap-bind by Secret reference, uses the existing dev-env service account's approved pods/exec capability, and supplies the password on stdin over the verified Kubernetes API to stock ak shell. It creates only the dedicated app-password, prints metadata only, and refuses mismatched tokens. Neither existing Authentik nor dev-env may read Secrets directly; no new RBAC or server restart is needed. Verify the bind before accepting human login. LDAP fails closed while the token is absent. Remove the one-time Job and its scoped API-only policy after completion:

kubectl -n dev delete job,ciliumnetworkpolicy openproject-ldap-bind-init

The Job uses the existing dev-env operator authority within the approved dedicated OpenProject provisioning scope; it creates no service account, Role or binding. Before readiness, remove openproject-ldap-externalsecret.yaml from its GitOps resources and delete the file through a reviewed follow-up PR. Reconcile dev-env and verify the ExternalSecret and its owned Secret are absent. The authoritative bind credential remains in 1Password and Authentik; do not delete either. A future explicit rotation can temporarily reintroduce the same dedicated delivery flow.

Verify the public LDAP certificate before storing it in 1Password:

openssl verify -CAfile ldap-ca-public.pem \
  -verify_hostname ak-outpost-openproject-ldap.network.svc.cluster.local \
  ldap-ca-public.pem

The private key stays in Authentik's protected certificate store. Track the certificate expiry and renew both the Authentik certificate and 1Password public trust field together before expiry; never disable verification as a workaround.

These actions are prerequisites, not permission to mark the service ready. The PR must remain unmerged until the requisite approvals and 1Password fields/certificate exist. The service must not be exposed temporarily to work around a credential or identity failure. All lasting cluster settings remain GitOps-managed.

docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text:
CNPG performs daily base backups plus WAL archiving to its dedicated Barman prefix, retaining 30 days. Attachment snapshots are sent nightly through VolSync to the app's separate restic repository, retaining ten daily versions and three days of snapshots. PVC prune protection is not a backup.

Database and attachments are separate backup streams. Recovery must choose a compatible point and verify every referenced attachment; no atomic cross-store snapshot is claimed. For the initial acceptance drill, take the backups while the unused app is quiescent, restore into isolated resources, and verify hierarchy, metadata, source mapping, attachment bytes/hash and actor history. Before user work, qualify the operating procedure for concurrent attachment deletion or use a maintenance backup window. Never declare restore verified from a backup Job's exit status alone.

docs.title: Acceptance before readiness and migration
docs.text:
• Confirm actual image/digest, no Enterprise token, generated locked bootstrap admin, healthy database/cache/web/worker and working persistent storage.
  • Fresh Authentik login → named user via real LDAP provisioning; second access reuses the record, no local password prompt, no anonymous project visibility.
  • Forged/missing/duplicate identity, Alice-to-Bob spoof, direct Pod listener, unapproved Pod and alternate/wildcard Host paths fail. Unauthenticated Internet requests get only the Authentik sign-in path, never work content. Verify logout and the documented revocation/cache boundary.
  • Named restricted bot: real HTTP create/read/update/comment/status/parent/link/ attachment/activity and stale lockVersion conflict tests. Create only a disposable fixture project; delete only those fixture items with authorized disposable scope. Worker comments and imports never count as an owner's approval decision (the old "prove a worker cannot approve itself" test is superseded, see below).
  • Configure Saga → Epic → Story, separate dependency graph, repository/source provenance, actor/conversation/revision fields and states Draft, Ungroomed, Needs answer, Needs approval, Approved, In progress, In review, Accepted, Paused. Generic parent links need an authoring/migration grammar check. Basic board dragging does not change status. Actual voice decisions use the real bot actor and conversation reference, never fabricated Tom authorship or self-approval.
  • Verify data/attachment survival across a normal restart, backup age/health and the isolated restore above. Return observed results, not a running-service claim.
  • No bulk migration here. The subsequent haynesnetwork agent pins 078–089 source commits, preserves original Markdown/IDs/dependencies/pauses/provenance and runs idempotent upserts. Imported work never authorizes execution. Preserve #991/#992 pauses and the Chapter7 boundary.

The reviewable work-model contract is scripts/openproject/work-model.json. It is not a bootstrap completion receipt.

Superseded 2026-10-19 (Tom, work model of 2026-10-16/19): no status firewall. The earlier requirement for live negative tests of worker creation/transition into Approved/Accepted, and to stop readiness if a native API bypass exists, is withdrawn. It is not a preferred permanent human-only lifecycle. Grooming and authorizing new scope stays with Tom/Meatball; an agent marking its own already-authorized story complete once its actual acceptance criteria are met is the intended path (see the opwork section). Still required: reading the real read-back state, never claiming enforcement from workflow rows or a hidden UI control, and honest reporting of what the API allows. Observed 2026-10-19: the existing native workflow denies Approved and Accepted to the agent role (HTTP 422). That is an access gap and a held decision for Tom (whether and how agents may self-accept), not something agents work around; no role or workflow change is made here.

docs.title: Initial rollout recovery
docs.text:
The first cold start left five empty application tables and an empty migration ledger. A separate empty database loaded the pinned vendor db/structure.sql successfully (217 tables, 257 migration versions, zero users/work packages). The failed original database was preserved as openproject_partial_20261015, with connections disabled; the successful vendor-loaded database was renamed to the configured openproject. No database or data was deleted. Remove that retained partial database only with explicit cleanup approval.

The worker now waits for a nonempty migration ledger using a read-only psql query before booting Rails' vendor wait script. This prevents the Rails migration checker from creating its metadata tables during initial SQL schema import. Helm gets a 15-minute initial startup window. VolSync's local cache explicitly uses ReadWriteOnce, independently of the attachment mover's CephFS RWX mode.

The LDAP provisioning Job uses the digest-pinned existing dev-env tooling image and kubectl's POST/SPDY exec transport to run stock ak shell. The Python WebSocket exec path required GET permission that the existing SA does not have; no new RBAC was granted. Verify create pods --subresource=exec, rather than the ambiguous create pods/exec command spelling, when checking this authority.

docs.title: Agent backlog CLI (opwork) — Story97 slice, 2026-10-19
docs.text:
scripts/openproject/opwork.py is the one shared tool Claude Code and Codex sessions use for the central backlog (project haynes-engineering, Saga=whole project, Epic=usable deliverable, Story=session-sized outcome). It wraps agent-api.py (same private API, same in-memory token, no delete, no new credential/role/RBAC) and adds no server, daemon or approval layer. Tom and Meatball groom scope; the routine lifecycle writes are the agent's.

opwork.py search "text" [--status S] [--type T] [--parent ID] [--source-key K] [--all] [--page N]
opwork.py show 97 --history --relations          # read-only, includes comment history
opwork.py claim 97 --note "starting" [--assignee me]  # Execution owner = this session, In progress
opwork.py comment 97 "progress"                  # attributed; `-` reads stdin
opwork.py status 97 "In review" --note "PR #1"
opwork.py complete 97 --evidence "tests ..."     # evidence + Accepted when the workflow allows
opwork.py create --epic 95 --origin 97 --source-key followup:97:topic --subject "..."   # a Story under Epic 95
opwork.py create --type Epic --epic SAGA_ID --source-key K --subject "..."   # an Epic under a Saga
opwork.py create --type Saga --source-key K --subject "..."                 # a Saga: no parent, no --epic
opwork.py move 97 --parent 95 --reason "regrouped"   # an existing Epic under another Saga, a Story under another Epic
opwork.py relate 130 97 --type relates
opwork.py checkpoint 97 "state" | pending | flush  # tracker unreachable: local record, replay
  • Session identity (Execution owner + the **[session]** comment prefix): OPWORK_SESSION, else <OPWORK_AGENT or agent> | worktree <name> | branch <branch>. All agents share the openproject-agent login, so the prefix, not the OpenProject author, says who acted. Never write as Tom. OPWORK_PROJECT overrides the project.
  • Search first: create reuses any item with the same --source-key (matched client-side, because the API offers no custom-field filter) and stops with exit 4 on a similar subject under the same parent unless --confirm-new (for a Saga, which has no parent, among the other Sagas). --type is Story (the default), Epic or Saga; --epic is the parent id (an Epic id for a Story, a Saga id for an Epic) and is refused for a Saga, which takes no parent, and required for the other two (exit 1, before any request; OP508, 2026-11-10). New items are filed Ungroomed under the parent (a Saga under none), with a relates link to the originating Story and the creator in Decision provenance. A create is never retried: if the answer is lost, the source key is searched and the result reported. The new item is then read back by id and checked exactly, with no normalization tolerance: its subject, every non-empty Markdown field it sent (description, acceptance, constraints, provenance), and its parent, type, starting status (Ungroomed), project and source key. On any difference (a changed, emptied or dropped field, a wrong parent, type, status or project, a changed or missing key) or a failed read, the result is UNCERTAIN (exit 6). Nothing is confirmed and nothing more is written: no second create and no origin relation. The message names the item, its source key and each field, and the intent is kept pending with the item's ID. Inspect it with show and correct it with an update. A re-run that finds one item by the key runs the same check against what that re-run asks for, except the status, because a reused item may have moved on since. Provenance names the creating session, so a re-run checks only that it is present. The item is reused, and the origin relation added, only when the check passes; until then every re-run exits 6 and posts nothing. Several items with one key are listed as before.
  • Move (OP681, 2026-11-11): move ID --parent NEW_PARENT_ID [--reason "text"] [--force] changes the parent of an existing Epic or Story and changes nothing else. It reads both items first and applies the same grammar as create: an Epic goes only under a Saga and a Story only under an Epic (exit 1, before any write); a Saga has no parent and cannot be moved. An item already under that parent is a no-op (exit 0, nothing written). An item in an explicit hold (Needs answer, Needs approval, Paused) is refused (exit 3) unless --force; ownership is not checked, since regrouping is not a claim. The PATCH sends only the parent link, with lockVersion. A 409 is not applied, so it alone is retried: the item is re-read, the grammar, no-op and hold checks run again, and the PATCH goes out once more with the new lock; a second 409 fails (exit 3) and overwrites nothing. The result is read back by id and checked exactly: the parent is the requested one, and the type, status, subject, source key and project are unchanged. The output is moved (read back): #ID ... parent=#NEW (was #OLD) ...; any difference or an unreadable result is NOT confirmed (exit 6), with no note written. Only after a confirmed move is the attributed note written on the item (the old and new parent as full links, the session and the reason). The note is a second step: if it cannot be recorded the item stays moved and the command exits 6 with MOVE DONE, NOTE NOT RECORDED, keeping the note locally for flush when it may have been sent. A re-run is then a no-op, so it never moves or notes twice. An Epic's Stories stay under the Epic.
  • Conflicts: every write sends lockVersion; a stale one (409), another owner, or an explicit hold or pause (Needs answer, Needs approval, Paused) is re-read and refused (exit 3), never overwritten. --force is a takeover/override for an explicitly authorized case only.
  • Partial updates and Formattable fields (Studio #423, 2026-11-05): an update sends only the fields given, with lockVersion; nothing else is sent, so it asks for no other change. The description and the acceptance, constraints and provenance fields are Formattable, and every write sends them as {"raw": markdown}. Before this fix Tracker.patch sent a description as a bare string (MARKDOWN omitted it); on #423 (journal 5819) such an update from a direct Tracker.patch caller left the description empty; a later {"raw": ...} update restored it. No opwork command sends a description on update: claim, status and complete change only the owner, the status and (claim --assignee) the assignee, and create already wrapped it. create sends the description, acceptance, constraints and provenance as {"raw": markdown} and the repositories as plain text (a String field). It always sends the description, as {"raw": ""} when --description is not given (a new item has nothing to clear), and leaves out an unset or empty --acceptance, --constraints or --repos. For scripts that call Tracker.patch(wp, fields, ...):
  • pass Markdown text, or exactly {"raw": text} (sent once, not double-wrapped);
  • an omitted field is not sent and keeps its value; None never means "omit";
  • None, empty or blank text would clear the field, so it is refused with exit 3 before any request, unless the call names the field in allow_clear (for example allow_clear={"description"}); then it is sent as {"raw": ""}. This opt-in is a deliberate policy: a clear has to be asked for;
  • any other value (a number, a list, bytes, another dict) is refused with exit 1 before any request; the message names the field and the type, never the value;
  • one refused field stops the whole update: nothing is sent. A conflict (409) is read back and refused (exit 3), never retried. A lost connection or answer is read back once before anything else: applied means success, not applied is exit 5, an answer whose change is missing is exit 6. The PATCH is never sent twice. Read backs compare the text exactly, with no normalization tolerance. Whether the live server rewrites Markdown (line endings, a trailing newline) is not qualified. If it does, an applied update or create reports exit 6 UNCERTAIN: that fails safe (no retry, nothing overwritten), and a tolerance waits until the server's rule is known.
  • Read back: success is printed only after a read back. A write missing on read-back is UNCONFIRMED (exit 6); an unavailable connection/read-back is exit 5. show --history marks any truncated text; --full returns it whole. claim --assignee me also sets the native assignee (opt-in; never Tom automatically; the session owner field is kept).
  • Workflow completion: complete preflights the form and records the evidence. If Accepted is not initially allowed, it moves the item to In review when permitted, re-checks the form with the read-back lock, and continues to Accepted when the workflow allows it. Otherwise, exit 7 reports the recorded evidence, actual read-back state and allowed next statuses, or the form re-check failure with instructions to inspect the item instead of repeating complete. The 2026-10-19 observation that this role could not reach Accepted was state-specific, not a permanent limit. Native workflow rules still apply.
  • Transient reads: GET retries connection refused, host/network unreachable, timeout, connection reset, a temporary DNS failure (EAI_AGAIN), an incomplete response body, and HTTP 502/503/504 on the same URL, origin and credential. The retry budget is about 120 seconds including attempts (each timeout is at most 30 seconds and bounded by the remaining budget; no attempt starts with less than 1 second left); backoff starts at 1 second, doubles and caps at 16. HTTP 401/403, all other 4xx and non-transient errors stop without retry. Redirects remain disabled. Each attempt that will be retried, and a call that ends as unavailable, emits one bounded stderr diagnostic with UTC time, method, fixed destination host, category and errno; an ordinary answer (including an expected 404, 409 or 422) prints none, and nothing carries exception text or request/response secrets.
  • Token-helper reads: the per-process token is read from the dedicated token-only helper (kubectl exec into deploy/openproject-agent-credentials) before any HTTP request, and that read is retried too. A GET shares the one 120 second budget (same backoff and floor) between the helper read and the request. For POST/PATCH only the helper read, which happens before anything is sent, is retried, with its own 30 second budget; the HTTP mutation is never retried, so a helper that never recovers sends nothing and opwork keeps the intent pending. Transient failures (pod not ready, container not found, upgrade-connection errors, a timeout, a failed spawn) are retried. An authorization denial (helper stderr containing forbidden or unauthorized, any case) is not retried, and neither is a token in the wrong format. Same helper, Deployment, namespace and identity; no other route, copy or environment fallback. Helper stdout/stderr is never printed, stored or logged: each attempt that will be retried, or that ends the call, emits one line with UTC time, helper, category=denied|transient|timeout|invalid and attempt=N. A failed attempt caches nothing.
  • Tracker unavailable: a clear TRACKER UNAVAILABLE error (exit 5). Bounded authorized work continues. POST/PATCH are never automatically retried, and DELETE remains forbidden. A failed mutation may have landed: its outcome is UNCONFIRMED, never invented success. Notes are saved under ~/.local/state/opwork/pending/ (OPWORK_STATE_DIR; directories 0700, files 0600, written atomically) with their exact body and original dedupe token. pending lists them with their token; a corrupt record is reported and skipped. A note whose POST returned 2xx but was not visible on read back (or whose read back failed after the 2xx) is saved UNCONFIRMED with that fact (and the activity id when the response had one). After recovery, flush checks history for the token: present means the record is removed; absent for a record with a recorded 2xx means it is kept for manual review and never reposted (inspect with show ID --history). Only a record with no recorded 2xx is posted by flush, and only when absent from complete history. flush first writes a post_started UTC marker into the record (atomic write); if that write fails nothing is posted and the result is exit 6 UNCONFIRMED naming the token. A record with the marker whose token is absent from history is kept for manual review and never reposted, like a recorded 2xx (this includes a POST that failed as tracker-unavailable, whose outcome is unknown). The POST is read back before the record is removed, and a 2xx that stays invisible is recorded so later flushes cannot repost it. A local write failure after a POST (full disk, read-only home) is exit 6 UNCONFIRMED with the note token, not a traceback. A clean 4xx answer to the flush POST (for example 403 or 422) created nothing, so the marker is cleared (the original record is written back) and the next flush posts the note again; a 3xx, whose outcome is uncertain, keeps the marker. The marker and record writes are fsynced, directory included. flush exits 6 when any record is kept for manual review (including a kept intent), so a script can tell. Resolving a manual-review record: run show ID --history and look for the note token (opwork:note=TOKEN, printed by flush and pending). If it is there, the note landed: delete the record file under the pending directory. If it is not, re-run comment for the work item (a new token), then delete the record file. Incomplete history keeps an unseen note for manual review. pending shows a record with read back unconfirmed (2xx) or POST started ..., outcome unknown. If the tracker drops during flush, that record is reported UNCONFIRMED, the lines for notes already flushed are printed, later records are not attempted, and the exit is 5. Legacy local checkpoints still use their existing deferred envelope. Failed status/create/claim/complete/relation commands retain their original command intent and any existing note key/body; flush keeps these "for manual inspection (show/search before repeating; note token T may have landed)" and never replays them. No sync daemon or additional queue.
  • Networking: v1 (dev/dev-env) reaches the API today. v2 session pods need the separate, held Cilium policy (egress + frontend ingress, TCP 8082); until applied v2 gets exit 5.
  • Tests: python3 -I -B scripts/tests/openproject/test_opwork.py -v (offline fake API: pagination, claims, conflicts, attribution, uncertain create, outage, and Formattable partial updates and the full create payload against strict synthetic fakes). These are mocked tests; the live fixture acceptance is recorded in the story result, not by CI. The strict fake models the outcome recorded on #423, not the server's mechanism.

docs.title: Studio local-model hosting
docs.text: Story 442 and profile CR-20 select Qwen3.5-9B Q5_K_M and its BF16 projector on Card A. The image uses the pinned llama.cpp b12679 CUDA 12 libraries and CPython 3.12.16. The loader reads both local GGUFs in the child under the Wan lease. It unloads before every Wan or Foley handover. The E10 benchmark and Tom's acceptance have separate gates.

docs.title: Part 2a dormant rollout
docs.text:
Proven for part 2a. The main build passed its CPU smoke, published and signed the image, and attached BuildKit provenance. The dormant rollout at 79fa01b5 recreated the Wan pod once. See comment 9924 on story 442 for the mounted code hashes and health reads. Flux updates wan-video-config. The existing Reloader annotation recreates the single Wan pod (Deployment strategy Recreate), including the app, Foley and API containers and existing provisioning init containers. Those init containers recheck their current pinned files and can fetch existing artifacts if they are missing. The new local-model Job, Cilium policy, profile and container are all under local-model-pending/, outside the applied Flux path. Local-model discovery continues to return HTTP 503 local_model_not_installed.

Run these gates as the coordinator, one Wan change in flight. Quiesce Studio queue dispatch and other direct clients. Check for no Wan or Foley job and no render hold. Check both Comfy queue lists empty and confirm the expected UUIDs and known idle ownership. Confirm the PVC is bound and the current init containers are healthy. Collect the previous revision, pod UID and code hashes. The Bash verification blocks run in their own shell. Each gate reports its result and a failed check stops the block, after collecting failure evidence where the block calls for it. Export the OP442_* inputs before running a block.

bash -s <<'BASH'
set -euo pipefail
source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
wan_exec() { kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- "$@"; }
at_wan() {
  wan_exec python -c 'import sys, urllib.request
with urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:" + sys.argv[1], timeout=15) as response:
    if response.status != 200:
        raise SystemExit("Expected HTTP 200")
    print(response.read().decode())' "$1"
}

gate='Wan health and idle state'
at_wan 8080/health | jq -e '.accepting_jobs == true and has("active_job") and .active_job == null'
gate_passed
gate='Wan product readiness and idle state'
at_wan 8080/v1/ready | jq -e '.ready == true and has("active_video_job") and has("active_foley_job") and
  .active_video_job == null and .active_foley_job == null'
gate_passed
gate='Foley readiness and idle state'
at_wan 8189/v1/ready | jq -e 'has("active_job") and .active_job == null'
gate_passed
gate='Empty ComfyUI queue'
at_wan 8188/queue | jq -e '.queue_running == [] and .queue_pending == []'
gate_passed
gate='Read rack GPU samples for operator review'
wan_exec nvidia-smi --query-gpu=uuid,memory.used,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv
wan_exec nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,pid,process_name,used_gpu_memory --format=csv
gate_passed
gate='Read mounted code hashes'
wan_exec sha256sum /config/video/api.py /config/video/product_local.py \
  /config/video/local_model_sidecar.py /config/video/openapi.json
gate_passed
BASH

Declare disruptive work with declare-activity start "Wan dormant admission update" --scope ai,talosw01,wan-video. After independent review and while the gates still pass, reconcile the approved merge with flux reconcile kustomization wan-video -n ai --with-source. Wait for the new pod UID and kubectl -n ai rollout status deploy/wan-video --timeout=35m. Confirm the watched revision and new ConfigMap and mounted code hashes. Repeat the prechecks plus GET /ready, GET /v1/profiles (I2V, S2V, Foley), a read of a known legacy /videos/<id> and GET /v1/local-model/profile (503 and local_model_not_installed). Check for a single healthy pod and release the activity declaration once settled. On failure keep dispatch quiesced, inspect the job/queue/hold and restore the previous dormant source through a GitOps revert and the same targeted reconciliation. Repeat the full health gate. Keep the PVC and existing ledgers.

The PR image smoke uses UID 1000 and a read-only filesystem with Docker network disabled. It imports the Python module, resolves the C ABI against the exact shared libraries, builds the plan and required-tool grammars from the bundled Qwen3.5-4B Jinja template and accepts one synthetic record_plan_v1 reply while rejecting an unexpected function. Production builds its grammars and parses replies with the Qwen3.5-9B GGUF's embedded template. The first live smoke proves that template, driver compatibility, GPU allocation, visual tokenization and model behavior. The Wan CPU suite covers the private protocol, request limits, recovery and fake inference. CI also renders the staged manifests and validates the projected profile with the production loader.

Expected for the startup repair. Its merge updates the same dormant ConfigMap and Reloader recreates Wan. Run the prechecks and post-rollout gate above, including one Ready Service endpoint on the new pod and the unchanged PVC UID. Keep Studio and direct producers paused across that window. The main workflow publishes a new signed digest. Leave the activation path staged.

docs.title: Part 2b activation
docs.text:
Expected. Merge A, B and C in order, after each preceding health gate. A installs the download policy. B starts a single CPU-only provisioning Job. Both leave the running Wan pod and its PVC unchanged. C retires the two temporary Flux Kustomizations and recreates the Wan pod with the sidecar and calibrated profile. Flux can pick up a merge on its interval. Do each merge with its prechecks complete and the lane quiesced, and reconcile to capture the exact revision.

A and B completed during the first attempt and their Flux references are retired. Keep their weights and read-back evidence. For the next C, start from current main and verify both temporary references stay absent from kubernetes/main/apps/ai/kustomization.yaml. Require checks on the exact activation and calibration head.

docs.title: Prepare evidence and verify the image
docs.text:
Run from the PR C checkout throughout. Export OP442_EVIDENCE with the printed directory for the commands below. Export OP442_LEGACY_ID with a known completed legacy video ID and keep its read private. Keep Studio dispatch and other direct producers quiesced from preflight through the smoke or rollback. Confirm OP410 and the queue worker are ready and no Studio dispatch is active.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  umask 077
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/state/op442"
  mktemp -d "$HOME/.local/state/op442/rollout.XXXXXXXX"
)

Use installed cosign or the pinned Linux amd64 tool below. The registry checks use an anonymous public pull token. They fetch the index, platform descriptors and attestation only. The signature binds the index, which binds the platform manifest and the provenance descriptor. In the activation patch, replace pending-op442-startup-proof with the tag@sha256:... from the signed main build. That image line also supplies the diagnostic Job and deployment health gate. The check below requires the latest image source revision on main and refuses the first activation's digest. Stop if any check fails.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?Set OP442_EVIDENCE to the private rollout directory}
  rm -f "$evidence/verified-image"
  base=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/wan-video
  gate='Image pin matches the current startup source'
  git fetch origin main
  image_inputs=(scripts/studio-local-model "$base/app"
    "$base/local-model-pending/weights/weights.json" .github/workflows/studio-local-model-build.yml)
  revision=$(git log -1 --format=%H FETCH_HEAD -- "${image_inputs[@]}")
  git grep -Fq 'STARTUP_LOG = "local-model-listening"' "$revision" -- "$base/app/local_model_sidecar.py"
  git diff --quiet "$revision" -- "${image_inputs[@]}"
  pin=$(awk '$1 == "tag:" {print $2}' "$base/local-model-pending/activation/sidecar.yaml")
  [[ $pin =~ ^b12679-([0-9a-f]{40})-[0-9]+-[0-9]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]
  [[ ${BASH_REMATCH[1]} == "$revision" ]]
  tag=${pin%@*}
  digest=${pin#*@}
  [[ $digest != sha256:e2e9b5e9b71aee89d0b8077ae47be113587b61054957b10f694cb4ab92b93f03 ]]
  gate_passed
  gate='Cosign available'
  cosign_bin=$(command -v cosign || true)
  if [[ -z "$cosign_bin" ]]; then
    [[ $(uname -m) == x86_64 ]]
    mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
    cosign_bin="$HOME/.local/bin/cosign-op442-v3.1.4"
    checksum=424e2c97d0b45fd7a6b608a87f090f35633f4c23ece5f092d48bba11aaf4bbfa
    if [[ ! -x "$cosign_bin" ]]; then
      binary=$(mktemp "$HOME/.local/bin/.cosign-op442.XXXXXXXX")
      curl -fsSL -o "$binary" \
        https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v3.1.4/cosign-linux-amd64
      printf '%s  %s\n' "$checksum" "$binary" | sha256sum -c
      chmod 0700 "$binary"
      mv -n "$binary" "$cosign_bin"
    fi
    printf '%s  %s\n' "$checksum" "$cosign_bin" | sha256sum -c
  fi
  gate_passed
  export DOCKER_CONFIG="$evidence/registry-anon"
  mkdir -p "$DOCKER_CONFIG"
  export GOMAXPROCS=2

  repo=thaynes43/studio-local-model
  image="ghcr.io/$repo@$digest"
  gate='Image signature and workflow identity'
  "$cosign_bin" verify \
    --certificate-identity https://github.com/thaynes43/haynes-ops/.github/workflows/studio-local-model-build.yml@refs/heads/main \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com "$image" > "$evidence/signature.json"
  jq -e --arg digest "$digest" 'any(.[]; .critical.image["docker-manifest-digest"] == $digest)' "$evidence/signature.json"
  gate_passed
  gate='Tag, signed digest and platform descriptor'
  token=$(curl -fsS "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:$repo:pull&service=ghcr.io" | jq -er .token)
  manifest() {
    curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" -H "Accept: $1" "https://ghcr.io/v2/$repo/manifests/$2"
  }
  check_digest() {
    printf '%s  %s\n' "${1#sha256:}" "$2" | sha256sum -c
  }
  for ref in "$digest" "$tag"; do
    manifest application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json "$ref" > "$evidence/index.json"
    check_digest "$digest" "$evidence/index.json"
  done
  platform=$(jq -er '.manifests[] | select(.platform.os == "linux" and .platform.architecture == "amd64") | .digest' "$evidence/index.json")
  attestation=$(jq -er --arg platform "$platform" '.manifests[] |
    select(.annotations["vnd.docker.reference.type"] == "attestation-manifest" and
           .annotations["vnd.docker.reference.digest"] == $platform) | .digest' "$evidence/index.json")
  gate_passed
  gate='Attestation digest, image provenance and source revision'
  manifest application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json "$attestation" > "$evidence/attestation.json"
  check_digest "$attestation" "$evidence/attestation.json"
  layer=$(jq -er '.layers[] | select(.annotations["in-toto.io/predicate-type"] == "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v0.2") | .digest' "$evidence/attestation.json")
  curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" "https://ghcr.io/v2/$repo/blobs/$layer" > "$evidence/provenance.json"
  check_digest "$layer" "$evidence/provenance.json"
  jq -e --arg platform "${platform#sha256:}" --arg revision "$revision" '
    .predicateType == "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v0.2" and
    any(.subject[]; .digest.sha256 == $platform) and
    (.predicate.metadata["https://mobyproject.org/buildkit@v1#metadata"].vcs |
      .source == "https://github.com/thaynes43/haynes-ops" and .revision == $revision)
  ' "$evidence/provenance.json"
  gate_passed
  printf '%s\n' "ghcr.io/$repo:$pin" > "$evidence/verified-image"
BASH

docs.title: A. Install only the download policy
docs.text:
Before merging A, run the dormant gate and save the Wan pod and PVC UIDs. Check both idle GPU UUIDs, utilization and process ownership, the bound PVC and node Ready. Record a known legacy read with the completed job's ID. After merging A reconcile the parent and policy. Require the Cilium policy to match the provisioner's label and its DNS and HTTPS allowlists, require no Job or Job Kustomization, and check the same Wan pod is still Ready.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  gate='Dormant Wan, Foley and engine health'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py dormant > "$evidence/before-a.health.json"
  gate_passed
  gate='Record Wan pod UID'
  kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -er '.items | select(length == 1) | .[0].metadata.uid' > "$evidence/dormant.uid"
  gate_passed
  gate='Bound PVC and UID'
  kubectl -n ai get pvc wan-video -o json |
    jq -er 'select(.status.phase == "Bound") | .metadata.uid' > "$evidence/pvc.uid"
  gate_passed
  gate='Render node Ready on amd64'
  kubectl get node talosw01 -o json |
    jq -e '.status.nodeInfo.architecture == "amd64" and any(.status.conditions[]; .type == "Ready" and .status == "True")'
  gate_passed
  gate='Read rack GPU samples for operator review'
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=uuid,memory.used,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,pid,process_name,used_gpu_memory --format=csv
  gate_passed
  gate='Known completed legacy video read'
  id=${OP442_LEGACY_ID:?}
  [[ $id =~ ^[0-9a-f]{32}$ ]]
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- python -B -c '
import json, sys
from urllib.request import urlopen
with urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:8080/videos/" + sys.argv[1], timeout=5) as response:
    job = json.load(response)
if job["id"] != sys.argv[1] or job["state"] != "succeeded":
    raise SystemExit("Expected a completed legacy video")
print(json.dumps({"id": job["id"], "state": job["state"]}))
' "$id" > "$evidence/legacy.json"
  gate_passed
BASH

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  gate='Reconcile download policy manifests'
  flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  flux reconcile kustomization wan-local-model-download-policy -n ai
  flux get kustomizations -n ai wan-local-model-download-policy | tee "$evidence/a-flux.txt"
  gate_passed
  gate='Provisioner policy label and allowed DNS and HTTPS'
  kubectl -n ai get ciliumnetworkpolicy wan-local-model-provision -o json |
    jq -e '
      .spec.endpointSelector.matchLabels["app.kubernetes.io/name"] == "wan-local-model-provision" and
      (.spec.egress[0].toPorts[0].rules.dns ==
        [{"matchName":"huggingface.co"},{"matchPattern":"**.cdn.hf.co"}]) and
      (.spec.egress[1].toFQDNs ==
        [{"matchName":"huggingface.co"},{"matchPattern":"**.cdn.hf.co"}]) and
      (.spec.egress[1].toPorts[0].ports == [{"port":"443","protocol":"TCP"}])
    '
  gate_passed
  gate='Provisioning Job and inventory are absent'
  job=$(kubectl -n ai get job wan-local-model-provision-r2 --ignore-not-found -o name)
  job_inventory=$(kubectl -n ai get kustomization wan-local-model-weights --ignore-not-found -o name)
  [[ -z "$job" && -z "$job_inventory" ]]
  gate_passed
  gate='Same Ready Wan pod UID'
  old=$(cat "$evidence/dormant.uid")
  uid=$(kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -er '.items | select(length == 1) | .[0] |
      select(any(.status.conditions[]; .type == "Ready" and .status == "True")) | .metadata.uid')
  [[ -n "$old" && "$uid" == "$old" ]]
  gate_passed
  gate='Dormant health and discovery'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py dormant
  gate_passed
BASH

Rollback A. Before B, merge a revert of A and reconcile cluster-apps. Confirm the policy Kustomization and the Cilium policy disappear through Flux inventory pruning, the Job remains absent, and the dormant gate and both UIDs still pass. If B was already applied, retire B first. If the dormant gate finds a retained local-model journal from a later activation, use the hold-clearing step before declaring recovery.

docs.title: B. Provision and read back the weights
docs.text:
Before merging B, confirm A Ready at the correct revision and repeat the dormant and storage checks. Reserve 7,499,546,400 bytes for the files, 1 MiB for writes and metadata, and 8 GiB plus 1,024 inodes free. Budget 16 additional inodes for staging. Create the PVC subdirectory as the serving UID. If the pinned revision already exists, stop and review its provenance.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  gate='Weights capacity, directory permissions and unused revision'
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- python -B -c '
import os
from pathlib import Path

if os.geteuid() != 1000:
    raise SystemExit("Expected Wan UID 1000")
workspace = Path("/workspace")
space = os.statvfs(workspace)
if space.f_bavail * space.f_frsize < 7499546400 + 1024**2 + 8 * 1024**3 or space.f_favail < 1040:
    raise SystemExit("Weights capacity gate failed")
root = workspace / "local-model-weights"
root.mkdir(mode=0o750, exist_ok=True)
if root.is_symlink() or not os.access(root, os.R_OK | os.W_OK | os.X_OK):
    raise SystemExit("Weights directory must be writable by UID 1000")
target = root / "qwen3.5-9b-q5_k_m" / "3885219b6810b007914f3a7950a8d1b469d598a5"
if os.path.lexists(target):
    raise SystemExit("Pinned revision already exists")
print({"free_bytes": space.f_bavail * space.f_frsize, "free_inodes": space.f_favail})
'
  gate_passed
BASH

B gives Flux a Job health check. The Job runs on talosw01 with the published Linux amd64 Python manifest, one attempt, a 30-minute CPU-only deadline and a mount limited to local-model-weights. It starts at the pinned Hub revision and records each redirect hostname. It follows only HTTPS redirects under **.cdn.hf.co. The first host observed in the preflight metadata was us.aws.cdn.hf.co. Byte caps, private staging, hashes and a create-only rename govern publication. On unexpected_download_redirect preserve the refused hostname and stop. A reviewed GitOps change must add only the necessary verified hostname to both the Job's HTTPS redirect allowlist and the Cilium DNS and FQDN rules, with the same file SHA-256s and caps. Require a new attempt after reviewing space and the refused Job. Keep path, query and signature values out of the evidence.

Changed: the first attempt failed and was retried under a new name. On 2026-11-25 at 05:16Z the original provisioning Job (memory limit 256Mi) was killed for memory five seconds after it started (OOMKilled, exit 137). It had logged the redirect to us.aws.cdn.hf.co and written 570,458,112 bytes of the first file to /workspace/local-model-weights/qwen3.5-9b-q5_k_m/.quarantine-rgimzg5p/. Nothing was published and the Wan pod was not restarted. The downloader wrote the file with a single fsync at the end, so its written pages stayed in the container's memory account. The retry, wan-local-model-provision-r2, flushes and drops the file's cached pages every 64 MiB and has a 1Gi limit. The quarantined partial is accounted for as described below and stays until the retry has published.

A failed or interrupted Job can leave one or more quarantined directories. After the Job's pod has stopped, list the matching entries under /workspace/local-model-weights/qwen3.5-9b-q5_k_m/. Record the Job ID, failure code, exact attempt path, allocated bytes (du -s --block-size=1) and entry count (find -xdev -printf . | wc -c). Recheck the byte and inode reserves before any retry. Keep the attempt while it is needed as evidence. For operator cleanup, select one exact .quarantine-* directory, resolve and verify its parent and name, and confirm it is a directory and has no active Job using it. As the owning UID, run chmod u+w -- "$attempt" if it was sealed, then rm -r -- "$attempt" using the verified path. Check that the path is gone and record the freed space. Leave the revision directory and other attempts in place.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  gate='Reconcile provisioning manifests'
  flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  if ! flux --timeout=34m reconcile kustomization wan-local-model-weights -n ai; then
    kubectl -n ai logs job/wan-local-model-provision-r2 > "$evidence/b-provision.log" || true
    exit 1
  fi
  gate_passed
  gate='Provisioning Job complete and logs saved'
  kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=complete job/wan-local-model-provision-r2 --timeout=30s
  kubectl -n ai logs job/wan-local-model-provision-r2 > "$evidence/b-provision.log"
  gate_passed
  gate='Successful pod ran the pinned provisioner'
  provisioner=docker.io/library/python:3.12.16-slim-bookworm@sha256:1475c4f5b6bcb7d35e57661d6f5d7429ec4041275633c15f2b49350ac898276d
  kubectl -n ai get pods -l batch.kubernetes.io/job-name=wan-local-model-provision-r2 -o json |
    jq -e --arg provisioner "$provisioner" '.items | select(length == 1) | .[0] |
      select(.status.phase == "Succeeded" and .spec.containers[0].image == $provisioner) |
      {uid: .metadata.uid, image: .spec.containers[0].image, imageID: .status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}' \
      > "$evidence/b-image.json"
  gate_passed
  gate='Provisioned manifest matches approved pins'
  weights=/workspace/local-model-weights/qwen3.5-9b-q5_k_m/3885219b6810b007914f3a7950a8d1b469d598a5
  pins=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/wan-video/local-model-pending/weights/weights.json
  wan() { kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- "$@"; }
  wan cat "$weights/manifest.json" > "$evidence/b-manifest.json"
  jq -S . "$pins" > "$evidence/b-pins.sorted.json"
  jq -S . "$evidence/b-manifest.json" > "$evidence/b-manifest.sorted.json"
  diff -u "$evidence/b-pins.sorted.json" "$evidence/b-manifest.sorted.json"
  files=$(jq -er '.files | select(length > 0) | .[] | [.name,.bytes,.sha256] | @tsv' "$pins")
  gate_passed
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r name bytes hash; do
    gate="Weight size and SHA-256 for $name"
    [[ $(wan stat -c '%s' "$weights/$name") == "$bytes" ]]
    checksum=$(wan nice -n 19 sha256sum "$weights/$name")
    read -r actual _ <<< "$checksum"
    [[ $actual == "$hash" ]]
    printf '%s %s %s\n' "$name" "$bytes" "$actual"
    gate_passed
  done <<< "$files" > "$evidence/b-weights.txt"
  gate='PVC free byte reserve'
  wan df -Pk /workspace | tee "$evidence/b-bytes.txt" |
    awk 'END { exit !(NR >= 2 && $4 >= 8 * 1024 * 1024) }'
  gate_passed
  gate='PVC free inode reserve'
  wan df -Pi /workspace | tee "$evidence/b-inodes.txt" |
    awk 'END { exit !(NR >= 2 && $4 >= 1024) }'
  gate_passed
  gate='Same Wan pod and PVC UIDs'
  old=$(cat "$evidence/dormant.uid")
  uid=$(kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -er '.items | select(length == 1) | .[0].metadata.uid')
  [[ -n "$old" && "$uid" == "$old" ]]
  pvc_uid_matches "$evidence/pvc.uid"
  gate_passed
  gate='Dormant health and discovery'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py dormant > "$evidence/b-health.json"
  gate_passed
BASH

Rollback B. Keep producers paused. Capture the wan-local-model-provision-r2 Job UID, state and logs. Merge a revert that removes the weights Kustomization from the ai inventory, then reconcile cluster-apps. Flux prunes the Job and hashed ConfigMap. Check that the Job and its pods are gone, the policy is still present, the PVC UID is the same and the dormant health gate passes. Use the hold-clearing step for a retained local-model journal if it blocks that gate. Preserve any published revision and account for the exact bytes and inodes of every .quarantine-* attempt. Require fresh capacity evidence and a reviewed new Job attempt before retry. On success leave the completed Job in desired state through the read-back and calibration. C will prune the completed Job, ConfigMap and download policy.

docs.title: C. Calibrate, activate and check ready
docs.text:
Changed: the first activation was reverted. On 2026-11-25 the calibration ran in the dormant pod (15 samples on the model's card, all 266 MiB; ceiling 270) and PR 5050 was merged at 06:15Z. The Wan pod was recreated with the sidecar at 06:17Z. Its three existing containers became Ready; the local-model container never did. It exited with status 1 immediately on every observed start. The process raised Local-model sidecar must be pinned to its configured GPU UUID, so it never bound the private socket. The pod had no Ready Service endpoint. The coordinator proved the queue and workers idle under the lease and found no residency journal. PR 5056 (0a521b75) restored the dormant path. Helm waited until the Deployment reached its 30-minute progress deadline. The Flux Kustomization health check failed two seconds later on the failed HelmRelease and the revert could reconcile. The weights and activation configuration were retained.

Proven on CPU. Anonymous GHCR extraction of the failed digest selected the Linux amd64 manifest sha256:34336c097119df5ebecad0f5d5ba58a1bd0062a07a0c1ecdd89edba217706f1b. The three Python modules matched 79fa01b5 byte for byte. Its CPython 3.12.16 ran the real serve module with the staged profile. The weights fixture used the pinned manifest and sparse regular files of the pinned sizes. Startup checks that manifest, file type and size. The provisioning Job verifies the actual file hashes. Neither the fixture nor the test loads a model. With both process variables set to the profile UUID, ready passed and residency reported no child. Setting only NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all or only CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 reproduced the original Python traceback. The archived ReplicaSet records the correct named pins, and the failed process did not log its effective values. The specific live mismatch remains unverified. The Talos NVIDIA runtime has been observed rewriting NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to void after mounting a pinned card. That could explain the failure. The diagnostic below checks the process values and driver-visible cards on talosw01. Foley starts without a startup equality check. Its leased worker verifies Card A through NVML and supplies the exact CUDA pin to its inference subprocess. Talos NVIDIA runtime observation ControlFoley worker source

The NVIDIA toolkit warning ERROR: init 250 result=11 did not occur in the extracted image runtime. The archived logs show it in the same pod's healthy ComfyUI container, immediately before normal startup output. The talosw01 extension version 580.178.04-v1.19.1 contains libnvidia-sandboxutils.so.580.178.04. Its Management::init failure branch passes init, line 250 and the driver-initialization result to the log formatter. NVIDIA defines result 11 as a missing file path. The exact path was absent from the logs. The Python pin guard ran before loading a model library or querying the GPU. NVIDIA status definitions Talos extensions issue 940

Expected after the repair. The sidecar binds its private socket after a profile, pin or weights check fails. ready checks the listener and residency reports that this instance never started a child. Local discovery and new local requests return HTTP 503 local_model_unavailable with a reason_code. The CUDA pin must be the profile UUID and the NVIDIA pin must be that UUID or void. The same bounded NVML read used for card status queries all visible device UUIDs under the existing compute lease. Exactly one must match the profile. If the lease is occupied at startup, the listener reports gpu_pin_unproven immediately. The first local request or operator probe that passes the already-held lease completes the pin check. Discovery only reads the current verdict. A terminal refusal requires a restart after correcting the cause. With no older reservation and the lease and queue guards satisfied, Wan and Foley can proceed. A retained reservation still requires its normal release proof. Use the diagnostic below before changing the Wan pod.

Check the Job succeeded, the read-back and disk/inode reserves pass and Wan is still dormant. Check node headroom for an 8 GiB request and 16 GiB limit, including other workloads. Run the Wan-pod change check before every subsequent Wan-pod change. With producers paused, confirm known card ownership, drain ordinary ComfyUI cache under the existing lease, and collect Card A readings and its engine process baseline. Round the highest drained memory reading up to the next integer if needed, add the 4 MiB release allowance, and cap the ceiling at 512 MiB. Set the marked unloaded_max_mib line in the profile to the value printed below before merging PR C. Keep Wan dormant if the readings are unstable or their rounded maximum exceeds 512 MiB. The cap can leave less than 4 MiB of headroom. Save the unedited calibration JSON with the approved profile for rollback.

Review every Card A PID and process name in calibration.json against the engine ownership checks and record its attribution privately. Refuse rows with unresolvable process names. The API container's nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps can miss processes in other containers. An empty process list proves nothing by itself. The release guard is the idle card's memory against both the load baseline plus 4 MiB and the calibrated ceiling.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  gate='Leased idle proof, calibration and memory ceiling'
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/wan-video -c api -- env PYTHONPATH=/config/video python -B - \
    > "$evidence/calibration.json" <<'PY'
import json, math, subprocess, time
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.request import urlopen
import api

card = "GPU-6ff9702a-1b2c-6094-5a85-00aa1924c55a"

def compute_apps():
    return subprocess.check_output(
        ["nvidia-smi", "--id=" + card, "--query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,pid,process_name,used_gpu_memory",
         "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"], text=True, timeout=10,
    )

lease = api.acquire_compute()
if lease is None:
    raise SystemExit("Compute is reserved")
with lease:
    with urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:8080/health", timeout=5) as response:
        health = json.load(response)
    status, foley = api.foley("/v1/ready")
    if (not health["accepting_jobs"] or health["active_job"] is not None
            or status != 200 or foley["active_job"] is not None):
        raise SystemExit("Wan or Foley is busy/unavailable")
    if api.local.load_profile(api.CONFIG) is not None:
        raise SystemExit("Expected dormant Wan")
    try:
        api.local.state_path(api.ROOT).lstat()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    else:
        raise SystemExit("Expected no local-model residency journal")
    if not api.gpus_idle(api.gpu_sample()):
        raise SystemExit("Rack GPUs are not idle")
    api.require_empty_queue()
    api.engine("/free", {"unload_models": True, "free_memory": True})
    processes = compute_apps()
    samples = []
    for _ in range(15):
        api.require_empty_queue()
        sample = api.gpu_sample()
        if not api.gpus_idle(sample):
            raise SystemExit("Unexpected GPU activity during calibration")
        sample_a = next(gpu for gpu in sample["gpus"] if gpu["uuid"] == card)
        sample_a["gpu_uuid"] = sample_a.pop("uuid")
        samples.append({"time": sample["time"], **sample_a})
        time.sleep(1)
    api.require_empty_queue()
    if compute_apps() != processes:
        raise SystemExit("Card A compute processes changed during calibration")
    rounded = math.ceil(max(sample["memory_mib"] for sample in samples))
    if rounded > api.local.MAX_UNLOADED_MIB:
        raise SystemExit("Rounded drained memory exceeds the 512 MiB cap")
    ceiling = min(api.local.MAX_UNLOADED_MIB, rounded + api.local.RELEASE_DRIFT_MIB)
    print(json.dumps({"gpu_uuid": card, "samples": samples, "compute_apps_csv": processes,
                      "boot_id": Path("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id").read_text().strip(),
                      "unloaded_max_mib": ceiling}))
PY
  jq -r '.samples[].memory_mib' "$evidence/calibration.json"
  jq -r '.compute_apps_csv' "$evidence/calibration.json"
  jq -r '"Set unloaded_max_mib to \(.unloaded_max_mib) MiB"' "$evidence/calibration.json"
  gate_passed
BASH

C keeps the ai/wan-video Kustomization identity. Its rendered PVC stays the same and retains kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/prune: disabled. The two retired Kustomizations own only the policy, Job and Job ConfigMap. Misplacing the PVC in a retiring inventory could delete the claim and leave Wan Pending. The activation initializer preserves the compute-lock inode. The sidecar mounts both weights read-only and has no second device allocation.

Save the profile from the calibrated, checked PR head before merging. The hold-clearing command needs that exact profile if the mount has been removed.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  gate='Save the approved profile JSON'
  profile=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/wan-video/local-model-pending/activation/profile.yaml
  awk 'found { sub(/^    /, ""); print } /^  local-model.json: \|$/ { found=1 }' "$profile" |
    jq -e . > "$evidence/c-approved-profile.json"
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: Run the one-shot startup diagnostic
docs.text:
Expected. The coordinator decides whether to run the staged Job. Before creating it, run the dormant Wan-pod change check with producers paused. Confirm the queue and workers are empty, both GPU owners are known and idle, and the existing compute-lock file is present. Keep dispatch paused through the check. The Job uses the same container image, GPU environment, runtime class and security context as the sidecar. The NVIDIA runtime can expose Card A by UUID before the process acquires the lease, even without a device-plugin allocation. That gives the exact image a compute-capable device. Under this reviewed command, the wrapper writes the approved profile from a Job argument to its private emptyDir and calls the same startup function as the sidecar. Startup takes the original lease by inode for the read-only NVML enumeration. The wrapper checks that the CUDA library can be mapped under the same lease.
