It calls no CUDA initialization or model operation. The private workspace has no dispatch lease path, and the Wan PVC is read-only. Keep the overlay dormant if idle ownership or the nonblocking flock cannot be proved. An authorized equivalent is an isolated maintenance test on talosw01 with Wan stopped and proven idle, using the same container spec. The CPU smoke covers the real PID 1 listener and the void case off the NVIDIA runtime. The CPU runner bind-mounts a stand-in for the UUID query and gives only its disposable container a fixture PATH. The published image has no stand-in or test switch.

Keep the Job and profile outside Flux. Use only the verified image from the step above. One Job create carries the approved profile and gets a unique attempt suffix. The 10-minute Job deadline includes scheduling and the image pull. Poll for either terminal condition and save the Job, pod termination state and logs for each attempt. Kubernetes cleans up the finished Job after 24 hours. Repeat the dormant health gate after collecting evidence. A failure keeps C on hold.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  attempt=$(mktemp -d "$evidence/start-check.XXXXXXXX")
  base=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/wan-video/local-model-pending
  gate='Verified image and approved profile'
  pin=$(awk '$1 == "tag:" {print $2}' "$base/activation/sidecar.yaml")
  image=$(cat "$evidence/verified-image")
  [[ $image == "ghcr.io/thaynes43/studio-local-model:$pin" ]]
  profile=$(jq -ce . "$evidence/c-approved-profile.json")
  card=$(jq -er .gpu_uuid <<< "$profile")
  gate_passed
  gate='Existing Wan compute lock'
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- test -f /workspace/compute.lock
  gate_passed
  gate='Create diagnostic Job'
  yq -o=json '.' "$base/diagnostic/job.yaml" |
    jq -e --arg image "$image" --arg profile "$profile" '
      .spec.template.spec.containers[0] |= (.image = $image | .args[1] = $profile)
    ' > "$attempt/spec.json"
  kubectl -n ai create -f "$attempt/spec.json" -o json > "$attempt/created.json"
  name=$(jq -er '.metadata.name | select(test("^wan-local-model-start-check-[a-z0-9]+$"))' "$attempt/created.json")
  printf 'Diagnostic evidence directory %s, Job %s\n' "$attempt" "$name"
  gate_passed
  gate='Read diagnostic Job condition'
  deadline=$((SECONDS + 660))
  condition=''
  while :; do
    # One failed read must not end the block before the logs are saved: a
    # re-run would create a second Job. Keep the last good read and poll on.
    if kubectl -n ai get "job/$name" -o json --request-timeout=10s > "$attempt/job.json.next"; then
      mv "$attempt/job.json.next" "$attempt/job.json"
      condition=$(jq -r '[.status.conditions[]? | select(.status == "True") | .type] |
        if index("Failed") then "Failed" elif index("Complete") then "Complete" else "" end
      ' "$attempt/job.json")
    fi
    if [[ -n $condition ]] || (( SECONDS >= deadline )); then
      break
    fi
    sleep 2
  done
  gate_passed
  gate='Capture pod termination state'
  kubectl -n ai get pods -l "batch.kubernetes.io/job-name=$name" -o json |
    jq '{pods: [.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, status: .status}]}' > "$attempt/pods.json"
  gate_passed
  result=0
  gate='Diagnostic Job completed'
  if [[ $condition == Complete ]]; then
    gate_passed
  else
    printf '%s failed (%s)\n' "$gate" "${condition:-deadline}" >&2
    result=1
  fi
  gate='Capture diagnostic logs'
  kubectl -n ai logs "job/$name" --pod-running-timeout=5s --request-timeout=15s \
    > "$attempt/start-check.log" 2> "$attempt/logs.stderr"
  gate_passed
  gate='Diagnostic startup verdict and listener'
  if sed -n 's/^[^{]*\({".*}\)$/\1/p' "$attempt/start-check.log" |
    jq -se --arg card "$card" '
      any(.[]; .event == "local-model-listening" and .verdict == "ready" and .reason_code == null and
        .gpu_uuid == $card and (.pins.NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES == $card or .pins.NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES == "void") and
        .pins.CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES == $card and .visible_gpu_count == 1 and .visible_gpu_uuids == [$card]) and
      any(.[]; .ready == true and .residency.resident == false and .residency.receipt == null and
        (.residency | has("startup_error") | not)) and
      any(.[]; .cuda_library_loaded == true)
    '; then
    gate_passed
  else
    printf '%s failed\n' "$gate" >&2
    result=1
  fi
  gate=''
  exit "$result"
BASH

docs.title: Activate and verify the Service
docs.text:
After the diagnostic and calibrated PR checks pass, declare activity with agent-run declare-activity start "Wan local model activation" --scope ai,talosw01,wan-video. In the Wan Flux Kustomization, change the path to the reviewed activation overlay. Keep wait: false, the 5-minute apply timeout, and the absence of healthChecks. The activation overlay sets HelmRelease upgrade.disableWait: true so its upgrade can finish applying resources while an image pull, init container or listener is still unhealthy. This allows the reviewed revert to reconcile without waiting for the Deployment progress deadline. Use the Deployment, EndpointSlice and discovery gates below as the workload proof. The dormant HelmRelease keeps its existing upgrade settings.

Merge C and reconcile the parent and existing Wan Kustomization. Require four Ready containers on the new pod, completed init containers, a Ready Service endpoint, and healthy local discovery. The private probe remains Ready in the served failure state. Any complete listener outage can briefly remove Wan from the Service. While the listener is unavailable, an otherwise admissible legacy Wan, typed I2V, S2V or Foley request fails before engine work. Keep producers paused until the applicable gate passes. Use the activity ID to end the declaration once settled.

The leased startup proof below resolves gpu_pin_unproven before discovery if the sidecar started while the API held the lease. The probe cannot dispatch model work.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  gate='Reconcile activation manifests'
  flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  flux reconcile kustomization wan-video -n ai
  gate_passed
  gate='Deployment rollout'
  kubectl -n ai rollout status deploy/wan-video --timeout=35m
  gate_passed
  gate='New Ready pod, init containers and image'
  image=$(cat "$evidence/verified-image")
  old=$(cat "$evidence/dormant.uid")
  [[ -n $old && -n $image ]]
  kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -e --arg old "$old" --arg image "$image" '
      .items | select(length == 1) | .[0] |
      select(.metadata.uid != $old and .spec.nodeName == "talosw01") |
      select(any(.spec.containers[]; .name == "local-model" and .image == $image)) |
      select(any(.status.initContainerStatuses[]; .name == "prepare-local-model")) |
      select(([.status.containerStatuses[].name] | sort) == ["api","app","foley","local-model"]) |
      select(all(.status.containerStatuses[]; .ready and .restartCount == 0)) |
      select(all(.status.initContainerStatuses[]; .state.terminated.exitCode == 0)) |
      {uid:.metadata.uid, containers:[.status.containerStatuses[] | {name,image,imageID,ready}]}
    ' > "$evidence/c-pod.json"
  gate_passed
  gate='Same nonempty PVC UID'
  pvc_uid_matches "$evidence/pvc.uid"
  gate_passed
  gate='New pod is a Ready Service endpoint'
  uid=$(jq -er .uid "$evidence/c-pod.json")
  kubectl -n ai get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -e --arg uid "$uid" '
      any(.items[].endpoints[]; .targetRef.uid == $uid and .conditions.ready == true)'
  gate_passed
  for name in wan-local-model-weights wan-local-model-download-policy; do
    gate="Retired inventory $name is absent"
    retired=$(kubectl -n ai get "kustomization/$name" --ignore-not-found -o name)
    [[ -z "$retired" ]]
    gate_passed
  done
  gate='Retired provisioning Job, policy and ConfigMap are absent'
  job=$(kubectl -n ai get job wan-local-model-provision-r2 --ignore-not-found -o name)
  policy=$(kubectl -n ai get ciliumnetworkpolicy wan-local-model-provision --ignore-not-found -o name)
  [[ -z "$job" && -z "$policy" ]]
  kubectl -n ai get configmaps -o name |
    awk '/^configmap\/wan-local-model-provision-/ { found=1 } END { exit found }'
  gate_passed
  gate='Local-model startup proof under the compute lease'
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/wan-video -c api -- env PYTHONPATH=/config/video python -B - <<'PY'
import api

lease = api.acquire_compute()
if lease is None:
    raise SystemExit("Compute is reserved")
with lease:
    lane = api.local.enabled_lane(api.ROOT, api.CONFIG)
    if lane is None:
        raise SystemExit("Expected an active local-model lane")
    api.local.require_started(lane.status(residency_only=True, allow_unbound=True, lease=lease))
PY
  gate_passed
  gate='Wan, Foley, queue and local discovery health'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py active > "$evidence/c-health.json"
  gate_passed
  gate='Discovery matches the approved ceiling'
  ceiling=$(jq -er .unloaded_max_mib "$evidence/c-approved-profile.json")
  jq -e --argjson ceiling "$ceiling" '.discovery.unloaded_max_mib == $ceiling' "$evidence/c-health.json"
  gate_passed
  gate='Sidecar log proves the GPU pin'
  kubectl -n ai logs deploy/wan-video -c local-model > "$evidence/c-local-model.log"
  card=$(jq -er .gpu_uuid "$evidence/c-approved-profile.json")
  sed -n 's/^[^{]*\({".*}\)$/\1/p' "$evidence/c-local-model.log" |
    jq -se --arg card "$card" '
      any(.[]; (.event == "local-model-listening" or .event == "local-model-pin-proof") and
        .reason_code == null and .gpu_uuid == $card and
        (.pins.NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES == $card or .pins.NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES == "void") and
        .pins.CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES == $card and .visible_gpu_count == 1 and .visible_gpu_uuids == [$card])
    '
  gate_passed
  gate='GPU plugin allocation remains on ComfyUI'
  kubectl -n ai get deployment wan-video -o json |
    jq -e '[.spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.resources.limits["nvidia.com/gpu"] != null) |
      {name, limit:.resources.limits["nvidia.com/gpu"]}] == [{"name":"app","limit":"2"}]'
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: Wan-pod change check
docs.text:
Before every later Wan-pod change, pause the Studio worker and direct producers. Confirm there is one Ready Wan pod, four Ready containers if active, and a Ready Service endpoint for that pod. Save the pod UID, image, restart counts and listener status. Run the active health command below and review the empty queue, cleared residency and idle ownership before proceeding. Set OP442_WAN_MODE=dormant to check a dormant deployment. Allow for a Service outage in the change window and repeat these checks after the replacement pod starts.

After a recreate of an active pod, prove the pin first. The API holds the compute lease while it recovers, so the sidecar normally starts with gpu_pin_unproven and serves a refusal. Local discovery then answers 503 and the active health command below fails closed, although nothing is wrong. Run the gate "Local-model startup proof under the compute lease" from Activate and verify the Service on the replacement pod before this check. A submit proves the pin as well; discovery only reads it. (Found in the delta review of PR 5060.)

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  mode=${OP442_WAN_MODE:-active}
  case "$mode" in
    active) containers='["api","app","foley","local-model"]' ;;
    dormant) containers='["api","app","foley"]' ;;
    *) printf 'Expected OP442_WAN_MODE=active or dormant\n' >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  gate='One Ready Wan pod with the expected containers'
  uid=$(kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -er --argjson containers "$containers" '.items | select(length == 1) | .[0] |
      select(any(.status.conditions[]; .type == "Ready" and .status == "True")) |
      select(([.status.containerStatuses[].name] | sort) == $containers) |
      select(all(.status.containerStatuses[]; .ready)) | .metadata.uid')
  printf 'Wan pod UID %s\n' "$uid"
  gate_passed
  gate='Wan pod is a Ready Service endpoint'
  kubectl -n ai get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -e --arg uid "$uid" 'any(.items[].endpoints[]; .targetRef.uid == $uid and .conditions.ready == true)'
  gate_passed
  gate='Read container status and image IDs'
  kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=wan-video -o json |
    jq '.items[].status.containerStatuses[] | {name, imageID, ready, restartCount}'
  gate_passed
  gate='Wan, Foley, queue and model health'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py "$mode"
  gate_passed
  gate='Read rack process ownership for operator review'
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- nvidia-smi \
    --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,pid,process_name,used_gpu_memory --format=csv
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: Clear a local-model hold
docs.text:
Keep all producers quiesced. Run the reviewed helper in the API container when a release latched local_model_held, or when a retained journal blocks the dormant path. The guard is three idle Card A memory readings at or below both the calibrated ceiling and the recorded memory baseline plus 4 MiB. The journal's load baseline takes precedence. For a hold that predates a load baseline, use the highest recorded dormant calibration sample.

With the profile mounted, the helper requires the matching sidecar to report no child. With the profile removed, it checks sidecar.sock under the compute lease. A live listener, a non-socket path or an inconclusive probe is a refusal. If the socket refuses a connection, the helper moves it in the same directory to sidecar.stale.<UTC timestamp>-<id>.sock. It records the name in the receipt and requires the original path to stay absent through the rest of the proof. Keep the moved socket as evidence even if a later check fails.

The dormant path checks three compute-process lists against the engine PIDs and names reviewed in the calibration for that boot, within their recorded memory. The API container may miss processes in other containers. An empty list proves nothing by itself. A row with an unresolvable process name causes refusal. The helper also refuses an occupied lease, a nonempty or unreadable queue, an active Wan or Foley job, or a separate render hold. For a Wan render hold, use the existing Wan recovery procedure first.

Use the original reviewed calibration and save the exact approved C profile. The helper accepts ceilings from the rounded-up drained maximum through that maximum plus 4 MiB, within 1–512 MiB. If the original ceiling was too low, calculate the corrected ceiling from the original samples using the same formula and review it through GitOps. Keep both profile artifacts. For a mounted profile the helper reads the corrected mount and requires the sidecar to match. For dormant recovery, point OP442_RECOVERY_PROFILE to the private copy of the reviewed corrected JSON. The helper reconstructs the earlier digest from the corrected profile and accepts the journal only when a lower ceiling in the same range reproduces that digest exactly. It records both digests and the ceiling change. The journal's load baseline still applies.

Keep the receipt and archived journal on the original PVC. Link the receipt ID and state hash in the private operator note with the operator, pod UID and reason for recovery. The helper writes its proof before renaming state.json in place to state.<UTC timestamp>-<id>.json. On refusal, preserve the files and resolve the stated proof failure. On interruption, check the receipt, archived journal and any moved socket before another attempt. Keep the local request receipts and avoid reusing an unresolved request ID. Start new work only after the health gate for the resulting active or dormant state.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  receipt=$(mktemp "$evidence/hold-clear.XXXXXXXX")
  profile=${OP442_RECOVERY_PROFILE:-"$evidence/c-approved-profile.json"}
  gate='Leased hold-clear proof and receipt'
  jq -en --slurpfile calibration "$evidence/calibration.json" \
    --slurpfile profile "$profile" \
    '{calibration: $calibration[0], profile: $profile[0]}' |
    kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/wan-video -c api -- python -B /config/video/clear_local_model_hold.py |
    tee "$receipt"
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: Rollback C after a served startup refusal
docs.text:
A Ready listener and HTTP 503 with a startup reason trigger this gate. Keep producers paused. Under the existing lease, confirm the queue and workers are idle, the journal path is absent, and the listener attests to a startup refusal with no child. Save that evidence and proceed to the GitOps revert. An existing journal or uncertain evidence requires the tracked rollback or hold-clearing path and the original release proof.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  gate='Leased idle proof, no journal and served refusal with no child'
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/wan-video -c api -- env PYTHONPATH=/config/video python -B - \
    > "$evidence/start-refusal-rollback.json" <<'PYTHON'
import json
import api
from clear_local_model_hold import check_idle, path_present

lease = api.acquire_compute()
if lease is None:
    raise SystemExit("Compute is reserved")
with lease:
    check_idle()
    if path_present(api.local.state_path(api.ROOT)):
        raise SystemExit("Residency journal exists. Use tracked rollback or hold clearing.")
    lane = api.local.enabled_lane(api.ROOT, api.CONFIG)
    if lane is None:
        raise SystemExit("Expected an active local-model lane")
    status = lane.status(residency_only=True, allow_unbound=True)
    if not status.get("startup_error") or status["resident"]:
        raise SystemExit("The listener did not report a startup refusal with no model child")
    print(json.dumps(status))
PYTHON
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: Rollback C after the sidecar served
docs.text:
Quiesce producers and check Wan, Foley, queue and sidecar listener health. Restore listener readiness if needed for release inspection. If the lane has a local-model hold, run hold clearing first. If it has ordinary residency, the rollback helper submits the tracked unload, validates its receipt and proves no child, reservation or pending operation remains under the lease. It drains ordinary ComfyUI cache only after proving residency is clear. If release latches a hold, preserve the journal and return to hold clearing before continuing to the GitOps revert. If the ceiling lacks the calibrated headroom, preserve the original profile and review the ceiling-only correction against the original calibration. If the listener is unavailable, a stale socket becomes eligible to move only after the profile has been removed through the reviewed dormant revert. Follow the dormant recovery gate for any retained journal before resuming dispatch.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  gate='Tracked rollback and residency release'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py rollback --evidence "${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}"
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: Rollback C when the sidecar never became Ready
docs.text:
An image that cannot run or a listener it cannot bind can leave the Service without a Ready endpoint. For a served startup refusal, use its leased no-child gate above. If rollout observation from pod creation shows the sidecar never became Ready, and the API container confirms state.json is absent, proceed directly to the GitOps revert. Every model load writes state before it starts a child. This path works without a sidecar listener or a local-model request. Current ready: false alone cannot establish that readiness was never reached. Cross-check the observed rollout with the pod's container states, events, current and previous sidecar logs, and EndpointSlices. A previous successful listener, a state file, or uncertain history requires the tracked rollback and, if held, the hold-clearing step. A stale socket can survive a crash. Use rollout history and journal absence for the direct revert and leave the socket in place. If a retained journal is found, keep dispatch paused and use the applicable hold-clearing path with the original calibration and approved profile or reviewed ceiling correction.

Keep dispatch paused. Copy the exact failed pod name from the first command into OP442_FAILED_POD. A container that never started has no logs. When Kubernetes reports an exit, read the previous container logs. Keep these records private. Require the inside-container proof to succeed on the same pod.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  gate='Read current Wan pod names'
  kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=wan-video -o wide
  gate_passed
  gate='Read failed sidecar status and pod events'
  pod=${OP442_FAILED_POD:?Set OP442_FAILED_POD to the failed Wan pod name}
  kubectl -n ai get pod "$pod" -o json |
    jq -e '.status.containerStatuses[] | select(.name == "local-model" and .ready == false) |
      {ready, started, restartCount, state, lastState}'
  kubectl -n ai describe pod "$pod"
  gate_passed
  gate='No Ready Service endpoint'
  kubectl -n ai get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -e 'all(.items[].endpoints[]; .conditions.ready != true)'
  gate_passed
  gate='Read status and applicable sidecar logs'
  status=$(kubectl -n ai get pod "$pod" -o json |
    jq -ce '.status.containerStatuses[] | select(.name == "local-model")')
  if jq -e '.state.running or .state.terminated' <<< "$status" > /dev/null; then
    kubectl -n ai logs "$pod" -c local-model --tail=80
  fi
  if jq -e '.lastState.terminated' <<< "$status" > /dev/null; then
    kubectl -n ai logs "$pod" -c local-model --previous --tail=80
  fi
  gate_passed
BASH

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  pod=${OP442_FAILED_POD:?}
  gate='Leased idle proof, activated profile and no residency journal'
  kubectl -n ai exec -i "$pod" -c api -- env PYTHONPATH=/config/video python -B - <<'PY'
import api
from clear_local_model_hold import check_idle, path_present

lease = api.acquire_compute()
if lease is None:
    raise SystemExit("Compute is reserved")
with lease:
    check_idle()
    if api.local.load_profile(api.CONFIG) is None:
        raise SystemExit("Expected the activated profile on the failed pod")
    if path_present(api.local.state_path(api.ROOT)):
        raise SystemExit("Residency journal exists. Use the tracked rollback or hold clearing.")
PY
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: GitOps revert and dormant gate
docs.text:
After the applicable rollback proof, merge a reviewed revert of C's activation settings in wan-video/ks.yaml. Restore the dormant ./kubernetes/main/apps/ai/wan-video/app path. Keep the 5-minute timeout and operator readiness gate. Retain the Wan app ConfigMap helper and keep both completed provisioning inventories retired. Reconcile the parent and existing Wan Kustomization. Set OP442_ACTIVE_POD_UID to the UID of the pod being replaced. Require a new three-container Ready pod with a Ready Service endpoint, the same PVC UID, empty queues, idle workers, and local_model_not_installed. Repeat the private legacy read from the dormant gate and verify rack ownership before resuming dispatch. If an already-dormant pod still has a journal, run hold clearing before resuming. Supply the original calibration and approved profile or reviewed ceiling correction. The dormant helper moves only a refused socket under the lease, then requires the memory proof and the remaining gates. End the activity declaration once settled.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  old=${OP442_ACTIVE_POD_UID:?Set OP442_ACTIVE_POD_UID to the pod being replaced}
  gate='Reconcile dormant manifests'
  flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  flux reconcile kustomization wan-video -n ai
  gate_passed
  gate='Dormant Deployment rollout'
  kubectl -n ai rollout status deploy/wan-video --timeout=35m
  flux get kustomizations -n ai wan-video > "$evidence/rollback-flux.txt"
  gate_passed
  gate='New Ready dormant pod and successful init containers'
  uid=$(kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -er --arg old "$old" '.items | select(length == 1) | .[0] |
      select(.metadata.uid != $old) |
      select(([.status.containerStatuses[].name] | sort) == ["api","app","foley"]) |
      select(all(.status.containerStatuses[]; .ready)) |
      select(all(.status.initContainerStatuses[]; .state.terminated.exitCode == 0)) | .metadata.uid')
  gate_passed
  gate='Same nonempty PVC UID'
  pvc_uid_matches "$evidence/pvc.uid"
  gate_passed
  gate='New pod is a Ready Service endpoint'
  kubectl -n ai get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=wan-video -o json |
    jq -e --arg uid "$uid" 'any(.items[].endpoints[]; .targetRef.uid == $uid and .conditions.ready == true)'
  gate_passed
  gate='Local-model profile mount is absent'
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/wan-video -c api -- test ! -e /config/video/local-model.json
  gate_passed
  gate='Dormant health and discovery'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py dormant > "$evidence/rollback-health.json"
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: Two private smoke windows
docs.text:
Expected. Run both windows with the active health gate, known idle ownership, the same private evidence directory and all other producers paused. The driver stages only synthetic inputs generated by smoke-inputs.py before the first window. Each admitted operation uses the Wan compute lease. Each 30-minute clock starts immediately before its first leased load. Keep the terminal open through cleanup and hold dispatch paused between windows.

bash -s <<'BASH'
  set -euo pipefail
  source scripts/wan-video/op442_gate.sh
  umask 077
  evidence=${OP442_EVIDENCE:?}
  gate='Window 1 cold load, text, vision, handover and final unload'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py window-1 --evidence "$evidence"
  gate_passed
  gate='Window 2 paired memory drift and final unload'
  python3 -B scripts/wan-video/op442_smoke.py window-2 --evidence "$evidence"
  gate_passed
BASH

docs.title: Window 1. Cold load, text, vision and S2V
docs.text: Step Budget and evidence Cold load Up to 120 s with a 60 s target. Record the load ID, baseline and wall time. The PVC cache may already be warm. Text and vision 30 s for one plan_v1 answer at 256 tokens and 55 s for one frame_check_v1 answer at 512 tokens. Keep the token counts, schema results and all four ordered synthetic frame hashes. Allow 10 s for the model peak check. Handover precheck and S2V Allow 30 s for the leased readiness and ledger precheck. Submit by 4m 15s elapsed with 1,280 s for the render and admission, and keep 265 s for read-back, reload and final cleanup. S2V evidence read-back Allow 40 s to verify the internal unload receipt predates engine dispatch, read the empty queue, and save the prompt ID and receipt. Use the per-UUID process samples to confirm S2V ownership. Return load Up to 120 s with a 60 s target. Record the warm load ID, baseline and wall time. Final tracked unload and idle proof Reserve 100 s. Verify the unload receipt against its paired baseline, then prove the queue, workers and card idle under the lease. Record the final receipt and idle proof.

docs.title: Window 2. Five paired drift cycles
docs.text:
Start only after window 1 writes passed.json. The driver checks the profile and unloaded host again. Budget 120 s per load and 25 s for each unload and its receipt, for 725 s total. Keep the 100 s final cleanup reserve throughout. Each cycle records the load baseline, verified post-exit sample and signed difference. Require post-exit memory at or below the calibrated ceiling and at most 4 MiB above the corresponding baseline. The fifth tracked unload supplies the final release receipt. The driver then verifies idle ownership under the lease. A stopped window with a safely unloadable child still uses its final cleanup reserve. A failure preserves the receipts and evidence.

Rely on the 4 MiB allowance for unattended use only after window 2 passes. A release exceeding that limit already latches a hold during the pilot. Review the evidence before changing any allowance. The absolute profile ceiling also applies.

Keep both windows' GPU and process samples, observed local-model VRAM peaks against 12,288 MiB, sidecar cgroup memory peaks against 16 GiB, request IDs and timings private. A sampled peak is an observation at the sampling interval. The driver retries the exact original PUT at most once, after a transport failure and a definitive absent response for that ID. At a polling deadline, follow the same original ID through cleanup. If work settles with a live child and a known owner, submit the tracked unload within the cleanup reserve. A failed or unverified release, unknown owner, access denial or unresolved original ID stops further requests. Keep any hold and use the recovery route below. A skipped, cut-off or unverified step leaves the window incomplete.

docs.title: Stops and evidence
docs.text:
Stop Hold state and next action Release exceeds the load baseline plus 4 MiB or the calibrated ceiling and fails the API's memory proof, or the API reports local_model_held Save the receipt, journal and memory readings. Use hold clearing. If the ceiling was set too low, preserve the original profile and review a ceiling-only correction within the original calibration range. Dormant recovery finds a socket, an unresolvable process name or an unavailable process query The helper archives a socket only after a refused connection under the lease. A live listener, non-socket, ambiguous probe or process proof failure stops recovery. Keep dispatch paused and preserve any moved socket. An empty process list still requires all three memory readings to pass. Release receipt missing, failed or inconsistent without a confirmed hold Hold status unknown. Preserve the request and journal, and inspect under the lease. Use hold clearing if held, or resume tracked cleanup only after ownership and residency are known. Unknown ownership, malformed queue, unsettled request or failed lease proof Foreign work or lease contention alone does not latch the local-model hold. A malformed queue may latch a separate render hold or a local-model hold after dispatch. Resolve ownership and any Wan render hold first. Use hold clearing for a latched local-model hold. Startup refusal, reserve failure or unavailable listener The startup refusal creates no hold. With a listening but unavailable process, verify prior residency under the lease before reverting. Use the direct rollback only with evidence of no Ready transition and no state file. With state present, use the tracked rollback and hold clearing if held. Access denial The denial does not itself latch a hold. The state of any earlier request may be unknown. Stop without retrying through another route. An authorized operator can inspect and follow hold clearing if held. Output check, cap or budget failure No hold from the stop itself. Finish verified cleanup within the reserve if safe. If the API latches a hold during release, use hold clearing.

Keep dispatch paused through verified cleanup or recovery. Resume once the applicable Service, health, queue, rack and residency gates pass. Preserve failed attempts, weights and journals. Publish only IDs, states, hashes, measured times and memory samples to the tracker. Keep service logs, full model outputs, prompts, staged media and engine ledgers in the private evidence directory. Record source, built image, tested checks, installation, usable smoke and Tom's acceptance separately. The E10 model quality verdict comes from its own benchmark.

docs.title: Studio database on postgres16
docs.text: OP431 adds a retained CNPG Database named studio on database/postgres16. PostgreSQL's postgres role owns the database. studio_migrator owns the studio schema, and studio_app is the API runtime role. Both logins require TLS and SCRAM from the IPv4 pod network. Their other TCP connections hit explicit HBA rejects.

docs.title: Consumer contract
docs.text:
The ai/studio-database Flux Kustomization projects the two CNPG passwords into separate libpq connection strings for the primary service. Have the OP434 deployment depend on this Kustomization. Wire individual secretKeyRef entries as follows.

Consumer Secret in ai Key and environment variable API studio-runtime-db STUDIO_DATABASE_URL Migration and worker registration Jobs studio-migrator-db STUDIO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL

Set STUDIO_DATABASE_SCHEMA=studio for all three consumers. The web, MCP and render workers use the API and need no database Secret. Run each consumer with its own service account. The projection readers are for ESO's TokenRequest calls only.

ESO generates each CNPG basic-auth Secret once in database. The two namespaced stores each authenticate as a different ai service account. Each account can get its own named source Secret. Kubernetes' default system:basic-user binding provides the store permission review. The projection reads the username and password by property and refreshes every minute. Both DSNs require TLS with SCRAM channel binding. The project uses the cluster's Postgres TLS setup without distributing the CNPG CA Secret. If a source Secret is regenerated, verify CNPG and the projection have converged. Reloader rolls the API when its projected Secret changes. The completed migration Job stays complete. A new Job pod reads the current value from its own projection. ESO 2.15.0 permission validation PostgreSQL 16 connection options

docs.title: Reconciliation and owner bootstrap
docs.text:
The following commands are for the authorized coordinator. On an initial installation, check for name collisions from the current primary before reconciling. Use the primary lookup and peer connection below with -d postgres and expect no rows from both queries. Investigate any existing database or role before proceeding.

SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'studio';
SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname IN ('studio_app', 'studio_migrator');

Capture PostgreSQL pod UIDs and restart counts before and after reconciliation. Require all three instances ready. Wait for the CNPG Database generation to be applied, both roles to be reconciled and all four ExternalSecrets to be ready. Capture statuses only.

kubectl -n database get pods -l cnpg.io/cluster=postgres16 \
  -o 'custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,UID:.metadata.uid,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount'
kubectl -n database get cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io postgres16 \
  -o 'custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,READY:.status.readyInstances,ROLES:.status.managedRolesStatus.byStatus.reconciled'
kubectl -n database get databases.postgresql.cnpg.io studio \
  -o 'custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GEN:.metadata.generation,OBSERVED:.status.observedGeneration,APPLIED:.status.applied'
for namespace in database ai; do
  kubectl -n "$namespace" wait --for=condition=Ready --timeout=2m \
    externalsecret/studio-runtime-db externalsecret/studio-migrator-db
done

CNPG creates the database and schema. Its Database spec has no ACL fields. Before OP434 starts the migration or starts using the database, run the following once through the existing local postgres peer path. The guard requires the expected database, owners and unprivileged roles. The changes are restricted to the new database and can be retried.

primary=$(kubectl -n database get cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io postgres16 \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.currentPrimary}')
kubectl -n database exec -i "$primary" -c postgres -- \
  psql -X -w -h /controller/run -U postgres -d studio -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
BEGIN;
SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '30s';
DO $guard$
BEGIN
  IF current_database() <> 'studio' OR current_user <> 'postgres'
     OR pg_is_in_recovery()
     OR (SELECT datdba FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'studio')
        IS DISTINCT FROM 'postgres'::regrole::oid
     OR (SELECT nspowner FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname = 'studio')
        IS DISTINCT FROM 'studio_migrator'::regrole::oid THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Studio database, owner, or primary mismatch';
  END IF;
  IF (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_roles
      WHERE rolname IN ('studio_app', 'studio_migrator')
        AND rolcanlogin AND NOT (rolsuper OR rolcreatedb OR rolcreaterole
                                OR rolreplication OR rolbypassrls OR rolinherit)) <> 2
     OR EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_auth_members
                WHERE member IN ('studio_app'::regrole, 'studio_migrator'::regrole)
                   OR roleid IN ('studio_app'::regrole, 'studio_migrator'::regrole)) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Studio role privileges mismatch';
  END IF;
END
$guard$;
REVOKE ALL ON DATABASE studio FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE studio TO studio_app, studio_migrator;
REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public, studio FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA studio TO studio_app;
COMMIT;
SQL

docs.title: Migration and grants
docs.text:
Follow the Studio LAN rollout for Flux ordering.

Run studio-api-migrate upgrade head once in the Job under studio_migrator using the pinned Studio API image. The command holds a database advisory transaction lock. A second connection slot lets a retry connect while a previous Job's backend lingers. The lock still serializes schema writes. The Job verifies the migrator role and its HBA rules before upgrading. STUDIO_RUNTIME_ROLE=studio_app applies schema, table and column grants in the Alembic revision transaction. The owner bootstrap above grants database CONNECT. After migration, the one-shot registration Job uses the migration identity to register the worker token digest. The API runtime role can read credential rows for authentication. It has no credential writes, create, temporary table, sequence or Alembic history privileges. Studio API runtime grants

The initial OP434 install applied 0002_active_agent_grants. OP956 pins 0003_studio_run_queue, which adds the queue tables and reapplies the initial grants while adding the queue-specific ones. Use the migration identity to check the applied Alembic revision.

SELECT version_num FROM studio.alembic_version;

docs.title: Credential-free access evidence
docs.text:
Review the rendered HBA rules on the Postgres instances using the peer path above. Expect zero syntax errors and the three Studio rules in order on each instance. Compare the pod UIDs and restart counts with the pre-change capture.

SELECT count(*) AS hba_errors FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE error IS NOT NULL;
SELECT type, database, address, auth_method
FROM pg_hba_file_rules
WHERE user_name @> ARRAY['studio_app', 'studio_migrator']
ORDER BY rule_number;
SELECT pg_postmaster_start_time(), pg_conf_load_time();

From a permitted ai workload with the chosen key injected via secretKeyRef, run the following with the role argument set to studio_app or studio_migrator. The migration Job runs the migrator checks and prints the revision before it exits. Read its results from the completed Job logs. Run the runtime checks in the API container after the grants. The checks print role and outcome only.

kubectl -n ai exec -i "$verification_pod" -c "$verification_container" -- python - studio_app <<'PY'
import os
import sys

import psycopg

role = sys.argv[1]
key = {
    "studio_app": "STUDIO_DATABASE_URL",
    "studio_migrator": "STUDIO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL",
}[role]
dsn = os.environ[key]
with psycopg.connect(dsn) as connection:
    actual = connection.execute(
        "SELECT current_user, current_database(), ssl "
        "FROM pg_stat_ssl WHERE pid = pg_backend_pid()"
    ).fetchone()
    assert actual == (role, "studio", True)
    if role == "studio_app":
        privileges = connection.execute("""
            SELECT has_schema_privilege(current_user, 'studio', 'USAGE'),
                   has_schema_privilege(current_user, 'studio', 'CREATE'),
                   has_database_privilege(current_user, 'studio', 'TEMP'),
                   has_table_privilege(current_user, 'studio.productions', 'UPDATE'),
                   has_column_privilege(current_user, 'studio.productions', 'document', 'UPDATE'),
                   has_column_privilege(current_user, 'studio.productions', 'id', 'UPDATE'),
                   has_table_privilege(current_user, 'studio.agent_keys', 'INSERT'),
                   has_table_privilege(current_user, 'studio.worker_tokens', 'SELECT'),
                   has_table_privilege(current_user, 'studio.worker_tokens', 'INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE'),
                   has_column_privilege(current_user, 'studio.runs', 'document', 'UPDATE'),
                   has_column_privilege(current_user, 'studio.runs', 'snapshot', 'UPDATE'),
                   has_column_privilege(current_user, 'studio.run_wan_attempts', 'request', 'UPDATE'),
                   has_column_privilege(current_user, 'studio.run_wan_attempts', 'job_id', 'UPDATE')
        """).fetchone()
        assert privileges == (
            True, False, False, False, True, False, False,
            True, False, True, False, False, False,
        )
        print("studio_app schema, draft, worker and queue privileges passed")
    else:
        version = connection.execute(
            "SELECT version_num FROM studio.alembic_version"
        ).fetchone()[0]
        print("Alembic revision:", version)
print(role, "connected to studio over TLS")

for target, override in (
    ("other database", {"dbname": "postgres"}),
    ("plaintext", {"sslmode": "disable", "channel_binding": "disable"}),
):
    try:
        connection = psycopg.connect(dsn, **override)
    except psycopg.OperationalError as error:
        if "pg_hba.conf rejects connection" not in str(error):
            raise SystemExit(f"{role}: expected HBA rejection for {target}") from None
    else:
        connection.close()
        raise SystemExit(f"{role}: unexpectedly allowed {target}")
    print(role, "HBA rejected", target)
PY

docs.title: Backup and rollback
docs.text:
D47 relies on the existing postgres16 daily Barman physical base backups and archived WAL, which include the Studio database and its role catalog. Check a completed backup after provisioning. The NFS media share is outside that coverage. CNPG 1.30 backup scope

For rollback, stop Studio clients and the Job first. Keep the Database and its schema, and keep both managed roles. In a GitOps commit change the roles to login: false and disablePassword: true, remove their passwordSecret references and remove the Studio hostssl allow. Keep the Studio rejects ahead of CNPG's default rule. Verify both logins disabled and Studio sessions drained before removing the projections, readers and generators in a follow-up. Preserve the database, schema owners, ACLs, tables and migration revision. The Flux prune exemption and CNPG reclaim policy retain the database. Restore via an isolated target or recover forward. Removing inline role definitions leaves their PostgreSQL roles unmanaged, including their LOGIN settings. Use the staged rollback above. CNPG 1.30 managed roles

docs.title: Studio LAN deployment
docs.text:
OP434 installed Studio in ai. OP956 adds the queue worker and its credential registration. OP957 installed the f30445f app pin and imported One More Meeting and The Winter Menu. Its scoped playback proof and key revocation are Proven in OP957 comment 9914 and OP944 comment 9915. OP959 pins the next app images and retires those one-shot stages. The OP959 rollout and checks below are Expected until the coordinator records the results.

https://studio.haynesops.com uses the internal Traefik tier, the internal.haynesops DNS target and the namespace's wildcard certificate. Traefik sends /v1/ and /auth/ to the API and UI paths to nginx. The probes, worker paths and MCP paths have no ingress route. A NetworkPolicy allows internal Traefik pods to reach the API and web ClusterIP Services. The auth route allows a burst of 30 requests and refills at 120 per minute per observed peer address on each Traefik replica. The internal LoadBalancer may combine clients behind a shared peer address.

MCP exposes /mcp and /mcp/upload on the same TCP listener at http://studio-mcp.ai.svc.cluster.local:8001. The existing NetworkPolicy allows port 8001 from dev-agents and Studio API pods in ai, subject to caller egress policy. The internal Traefik route excludes the entire /mcp path family and Traefik has no network access to MCP (CR-21). MCP forwards requests to http://studio-api.ai.svc.cluster.local:8000 using the caller's agent key. Upload requires an active assets:upload grant. Studio MCP transport contract

The API, MCP and static web each run two replicas, with required hostname anti-affinity and a PodDisruptionBudget of one available replica. Updates allow one surge pod and zero unavailable replicas. Plan for a third eligible node during a rollout. The migration Job has its own account and Secret reference. API pods use the runtime DB and OIDC projections. Reloader handles changes to those two projections with the Deployment's rolling strategy. A completed Job remains complete after password rotation. A new Job pod reads the current migration projection.

The product store is gasha01.haynesnetwork:/hdd-nfs-repl/data/studio/api-store-v1, mounted at /studio read-write on the API and read-only on the worker. The API runs as 1000:1000, the existing NFS writer's IDs. Its startup command checks exclusive create, fsync, hard-link no-clobber and read-back under .probe/ before serving. Kubernetes uses /healthz for process liveness. The readiness probe tolerates the first /readyz response of 503 while the store check runs. It also checks PostgreSQL. Web probes read /index.html. MCP probes check its TCP listener. The LAN route check runs from Gatus.

The worker runs one studio-worker replica on talosw01 with Recreate and the dev-env-agent priority class. It shares the API's UID and GID. Both processes mount data/studio/build-stage-v1 from the same export at /build-stage, read-write, as STUDIO_BUILD_STAGE_ROOT. The worker builds there and the API validates and publishes the resulting delivery. Both use the same STUDIO_BUILD_REVISION=git:<commit>. The worker records the API image digest as STUDIO_BUILD_IMAGE_DIGEST. The API and worker load the model licence register from their image's installed Python package. The API inherits /opt/studio from the image's WORKDIR.

The immutable studio-model-licences-1aa9b4736da9 ConfigMap is exempt from pruning and falls out of every Flux inventory at OP959. Keep it through the rollback window. Once f30445f is retired as a rollback candidate and no pod or workload mounts the ConfigMap, remove it in a follow-up GitOps cleanup. Render the identical immutable ConfigMap without its prune exemption in a cleanup Kustomization with pruning enabled. Confirm Flux owns the exact ConfigMap again, its live prune exemption is gone and the inventory contains only that ConfigMap. Then retire the cleanup Kustomization and verify the ConfigMap is gone. Recover the original contents from OP957's merged tree.

The worker records main-thread progress under /run/studio on a pod-local emptyDir. Startup waits for the marker. Liveness checks its age every 30 seconds and restarts the container after three consecutive failures. The 1,500-second age budget gives a 20-minute Wan clip five minutes of margin. Wan polling refreshes the marker, as do claim polls and build steps. The probe works without network calls. After a liveness kill, the 90-second claim expires. The replacement reclaims the FIFO head with a new fence or keeps it held pending reconciliation. It reconciles by the recorded Wan job ID and may re-send the same ID and body at most once per claim if Wan reports the ID absent after an ambiguous submission. Wan deduplicates that request, so the pending attempt causes no second engine submission. Progress probe Claim recovery

Worker egress allows cluster DNS, the Studio API on TCP 8000, the Wan product Service on TCP 8080 and Wyoming Whisper on TCP 10300. The API admits the worker pod to port 8000. On that port the application enforces the worker-only /internal/v1/work/* boundary. The pod has no inbound listener, service account token or database credential. ESO generates the 64-character alphanumeric token with CreatedOnce. The registration Job mounts it as a file and uses the migration identity to register worker ID studio-worker. The worker uses the same Secret key as an environment reference. Re-running registration with the same value is idempotent. Studio queue configuration Token administration

D47 excludes NFS media from backups. The NFS server is outside the cluster and remains a shared dependency of all API replicas. PostgreSQL uses the existing CNPG backup coverage.

For the CPU matting release sequence and dormant sidecar, see the Studio matting deployment.

docs.title: Gatus and backup coverage
docs.text:
OP435 verified the Gatus endpoint installed by OP434. The ai/studio Flux Kustomization renders studio-gatus-ep from the shared common/gatus/guarded component. The Gatus ConfigMap sidecar in observability watches the gatus.io/enabled label and loads the endpoint into the internal group. Gatus requests https://studio.haynesops.com/v1/me through internal Traefik once a minute. It sends no credential. The expected anonymous response is 401, within the installed 200–401 success range. A timeout, too-many-requests response, missing route or server error fails. The process and database/store probes remain on the API pod. The Studio Deployments do not mount the Gatus ConfigMap, so its installation or update requires no Studio pod rollout.

The Gatus ConfigMap reconciles with the app. Verify its configuration and check the internal/studio result in Gatus. Use a result timestamp following the reconcile and within two probe intervals of verification. The first history entry can take one interval.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  kubectl -n ai get configmap studio-gatus-ep -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}'
)

OP435 saw passing Gatus checks at 01:59, 02:00 and 02:01 UTC on 2026-11-25. It also observed 401 at /v1/me, 200 at / and 404 at /healthz from the Gatus pod. It found direct NFS mounts and no Studio claim in ai. VolSync has no Studio claim to snapshot.

docs.title: Initial resource settings
docs.text:
OP434 measured the API, MCP, web and migration images in a disposable smoke using the packaged executables and PostgreSQL 16. The smoke sampled process RSS and CPU with a small number of serial probes. The queue worker and registration Job use provisional settings.

Workload Measured RSS Mean CPU in smoke CPU request Memory request / limit API 127.5 MiB 1.5m 100m 160 MiB / 640 MiB MCP 63.1 MiB 1.5m 50m 96 MiB / 320 MiB Web 9.4 MiB below sampling resolution 25m 16 MiB / 32 MiB Migration Job 74.3 MiB 1.14 CPU-seconds in 9.99 s 100m 96 MiB / 192 MiB Registration Job Pending Pending 50m 64 MiB / 192 MiB Queue worker Pending Pending 250m 2 GiB / 8 GiB

The API and MCP memory limits include headroom for the maximum photo upload measured on Studio PR 102 at 346 MiB in the API (640 MiB limit) and 173 MiB in MCP (320 MiB limit). The measurements are process RSS from the local test. The ai namespace had no ResourceQuota at OP957 preflight. Its default-cpu-request LimitRange set a default CPU request of 50m.

CR-22 divides D18's 24 vCPU limit into 20 for studio-render and 4 for studio-worker. Both use the same low priority. The worker runs one build at a time with two media threads. The Deployment serves the run lane. Its CPU request matches the render pod's 250m scheduling share. At preflight the idle render pod used 3m CPU and 16 MiB. The existing serial mix reported 195 MB peak memory. The worker request and limit are provisional allowances for the Python process, decoded frame buffers and media subprocesses. Sample worker CPU, memory and restarts during the first authorized build. Studio mix measurements

docs.title: Voice and image queues before consumers are installed
docs.text:
OP959 opens the media-job and lane routes. A signed-in person who presses Generate voice sees Queued in voice lane (or Queued · voice lane paused). Voice and image jobs stay queued indefinitely at this pin. The run worker posts an empty claim body and can claim only the run lane. There is no media-job cancel route, purge or automatic retry. Tom can pause the voice and image lanes from his signed-in session to hold future claims. Only a person can change lane pauses. Paused lanes still accept new jobs.

OP961 adds separate consumers with their own worker IDs, tokens, writable store mounts and Kokoro or ComfyUI settings. The first consumer for each lane would take any stale jobs in queue order and submit them to the shared image engine or voice service. Repeat the media queue count before enabling either consumer. If either count is nonzero, stop for backlog review.

docs.title: OP959 release
docs.text:
Use the digest pair in release.yaml. Studio main commit 393fe1d66070ac726739b4cdb001a9e6b2c467db contains dccfc9b and was the newest successful Studio images publish at selection. The API, MCP, worker, migration and worker-registration Jobs share the Python digest. Web uses its matching nginx digest. Both tags, digests and Linux/amd64 revision labels were verified anonymously. Studio images run

STUDIO_GO_LIVE_APPROVER_SUBJECTS stays [] and the sign-in freshness window defaults to 900 seconds. STUDIO_ESCALATION_AUTHORIZATION=person leaves authorization with a signed-in person. API and MCP use the default 90-second upload body deadline and 15-second idle deadline. The existing database, store, OIDC, staging and service settings supply the required startup values for these entry points. Worker registration reuses the registered worker token. The release provisions zero agent keys.

docs.title: Before reconciliation
docs.text:
This upgrade assumes the existing NFS store and build-stage directories. For a fresh installation, prepare api-store-v1 and build-stage-v1 as UID/GID 1000 on the Studio export before rolling the app. Check the existing store mount and the database and OIDC prerequisites.

Run the checks before merging the GitOps change. Flux can reconcile as soon as it sees the merged commit. Ask Studio users to keep Studio idle until postflight completes. The previous pin has no queue-pause routes, so check the queue again immediately before merge. Require ready database and OIDC projections, all three database instances ready, the worker idle and at least three nodes eligible for the rolling app replicas. Use the normal database readiness checks. Confirm OP957's successful proof and key revocations before retiring the stages.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  flux get kustomization cloudnative-pg-cluster -n database
  kubectl -n database get cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io postgres16 \
    -o 'custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,DESIRED:.spec.instances,READY:.status.readyInstances'
  for stage in studio-database studio-oidc studio studio-worker; do
    kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=Ready --timeout=1m "kustomization/$stage"
  done
  kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=Ready --timeout=1m \
    externalsecret/studio-runtime-db externalsecret/studio-migrator-db \
    externalsecret/studio-oidc-client externalsecret/studio-worker-token \
    helmrelease/studio-render
  kubectl get nodes
  kubectl -n ai get ingressroute studio
  kubectl -n ai get svc studio-api studio-web studio-mcp
  kubectl -n ai get networkpolicy studio-api-ingress studio-web-ingress studio-mcp-ingress
  kubectl -n ai get job studio-revoke-playback-1aa9b4736da9 \
    -o 'custom-columns=JOB:.metadata.name,SUCCEEDED:.status.succeeded'
  kubectl -n ai logs deploy/studio-worker -c worker --since=2m | grep -c 'work/claim "HTTP/1.1 204'
)

Run this block as a Bash script with preflight as its first argument and keep the baseline file on the coordinator's machine. After verifying the new pod pins, run it again with postflight and the same baseline path. It requires an exact match for each film's production, story, run, delivery and playback index counts and the durable store's file count and total bytes. The store count excludes .probe. Use compare for the counts alone on a rollback, against a fresh preflight baseline taken immediately before rollback at a separate path. Save this block as a Bash script to call it with a phase, baseline path and API pod target during the OP437 recovery check.

Every mode uses the API's runtime database connection in a read-only transaction. Postflight also calls the pinned application's _check_approval in preview mode, _stored_snapshot, and drafts.get_draft followed by Draft.summary, which loads the canonical model with Story.from_document. The probe needs no browser session or agent key and outputs only IDs, codes, counts and hashes. It exits unsuccessfully on any difference.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  phase=${1:-preflight}
  baseline=${2:-"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:?}/studio-op959-baseline.json"}
  target=${3:-deploy/studio-api}
  expected=
  if [[ $phase != preflight && $phase != recovery-baseline ]]; then
    expected=$(<"$baseline")
    test -n "$expected"
  fi
  report=$(kubectl -n ai exec -i "$target" -c api -- python -I -B - "$phase" "$expected" <<'PY'
import json
import os
import sys
from hashlib import sha256

from haynes_studio.db.engine import connect_engine, snapshot

films = (
    ("prd_01M7ZGYNHFET1GKR4304FVD4PE",
     "sty_01M7ZGYNHFET1GKR4304FVD4PF", "run_01M7ZHNZJ2PWA8XR8K7KKWP17V",
     "dlv_01M7ZHP1QS82QGK196ZPCM7MQS", True, 1),
    ("prd_01M79V9FC00000000000000001",
     "sty_01M79V9FC00000000000000001", "run_01M7C5CJA7XKBCRPM0ZRP2P5RS",
     "dlv_01M7C5D3KFX3MFVWCXBCVJHMG7", False, 0),
)


def check_import(conn, production, story, run, delivery, has_snapshot, expected_boards):
    from haynes_studio.api.approval_routes import _check_approval, _delivery
    from haynes_studio.api.errors import APIError
    from haynes_studio.api.run_routes import _stored_snapshot
    from haynes_studio.db import drafts, runs
    from haynes_studio.golive import records
    from haynes_studio.store.local import LocalStore

    row = runs.get(conn, run)
    assert (row["production_id"], row["story_id"]) == (production, story), run
    delivered = _delivery(conn, run)
    assert delivered is not None and delivered["id"] == delivery, (run, delivery)
    active = conn.scalar(records.active_id(run))
    _, refusal = _check_approval(row["document"], delivered, delivered["master"]["sha256"],
                                 True, active, preview=True)
    code = refusal.details["code"] if refusal is not None else None
    assert code == "approval.legacy_run", (run, code)
    print(run, code)

    try:
        response = _stored_snapshot(LocalStore(os.environ["STUDIO_STORE_ROOT"]), row)
    except APIError as error:
        code = error.details["code"]
        assert not has_snapshot and (error.status_code, code) == (404, "run.snapshot_missing"), (
            run, error.status_code, code)
        print(run, error.status_code, code)
    else:
        assert has_snapshot and response.status_code == 200, (run, response.status_code)
        digest = sha256(response.body).hexdigest()
        recorded = row["document"]["snapshot"]["sha256"]
        assert digest == recorded, (run, digest, recorded)
        print(run, response.status_code, digest)

    draft = drafts.get_draft(conn, story)
    assert all("created_by" not in board for board in draft.boards.values()), story
    summary = draft.summary(conn)
    assert (summary["id"], summary["production_id"]) == (story, production), story
    board_count = summary["derived"]["board_count"]
    assert board_count == len(draft.boards) == expected_boards, (story, board_count, len(draft.boards))
    print(story, "boards", board_count)


def recovery_reads(conn):
    from haynes_studio.store.local import LocalStore

    store = LocalStore(os.environ["STUDIO_STORE_ROOT"])
    selections, selection_rows = sha256(), 0
    for (row,) in conn.exec_driver_sql("SELECT to_jsonb(s)::text FROM studio.selections s ORDER BY iss, sub"):
        selections.update(row.encode() + b"\n")
        selection_rows += 1

    proxies = {}
    for _, _, run, delivery, _, _ in films:
        proxy = conn.exec_driver_sql(
            "SELECT document->'proxy' FROM studio.deliveries WHERE id = %s AND run_id = %s",
            (delivery, run),
        ).scalar_one()
        with store.open(proxy["locator"]) as handle:
            digest = sha256()
            size = 0
            while chunk := handle.read(1024 * 1024):
                digest.update(chunk)
                size += len(chunk)
        assert (digest.hexdigest(), size) == (proxy["sha256"], proxy["bytes"]), (run, size)
        proxies[run] = [digest.hexdigest(), size]

    queued = {}
    for run, pin in conn.exec_driver_sql(
        "SELECT id, document->'snapshot' FROM studio.runs WHERE document->>'status' = 'queued' ORDER BY id"
    ):
        limit = 16 * 1024 * 1024
        with store.open(pin["locator"]) as handle:
            data = handle.read(limit + 1)
        digest = sha256(data).hexdigest()
        assert len(data) <= limit and digest == pin["sha256"], run
        queued[run] = digest
    return {"proxy SHA-256/bytes": proxies, "selection rows/SHA-256": [selection_rows, selections.hexdigest()],
            "queued snapshot SHA-256": queued}


phase, expected = sys.argv[1:]
assert phase in {"preflight", "postflight", "compare", "recovery-baseline", "recovery-compare"}, phase
recovery = phase.startswith("recovery-")
if phase == "postflight":
    assert os.environ["STUDIO_BUILD_REVISION"] == "git:393fe1d66070ac726739b4cdb001a9e6b2c467db"
engine = connect_engine(os.environ["STUDIO_DATABASE_URL"], os.getenv("STUDIO_DATABASE_SCHEMA", "studio"))
imports = {}
with snapshot(engine) as conn:
    conn.exec_driver_sql("SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY")
    assert conn.exec_driver_sql("SELECT current_user, current_database(), ssl "
                               "FROM pg_stat_ssl WHERE pid = pg_backend_pid()").one() == (
                                   "studio_app", "studio", True)
    statuses = dict(conn.exec_driver_sql(
        "SELECT document->>'status', count(*) FROM studio.runs GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1"
    ).tuples().all())
    forbidden_run_states = {"running", "held"} if recovery else {"queued", "running", "held"}
    assert not forbidden_run_states.intersection(statuses), statuses
    if recovery:
        media_counts = conn.exec_driver_sql(
            "SELECT lane, document->>'status', count(*) FROM studio.media_jobs "
            "WHERE document->>'status' IN ('queued', 'running') GROUP BY 1, 2"
        ).all()
        assert not any(status == "running" for _, status, _ in media_counts), media_counts
        waiting = {lane for lane, _, _ in media_counts}
        if "queued" in statuses:
            waiting.add("run")
        paused = set(conn.exec_driver_sql(
            "SELECT lane FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (lane) lane, paused FROM studio.queue_lane_events "
            "ORDER BY lane, sequence DESC) latest WHERE paused"
        ).scalars())
        assert waiting <= paused, ("queued work in unpaused lanes", sorted(waiting - paused))
    for production, story, run, delivery, has_snapshot, expected_boards in films:
        counts = list(conn.exec_driver_sql("""
            SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.productions WHERE id = %s),
                   (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.stories WHERE id = %s),
                   (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.runs WHERE id = %s),
                   (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.deliveries WHERE id = %s AND run_id = %s),
                   (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.delivery_media WHERE run_id = %s)
        """, (production, story, run, delivery, run, run)).one())
        assert counts[:4] == [1, 1, 1, 1] and counts[4] >= 2, (run, counts)
        imports[run] = counts
        if phase == "postflight":
            check_import(conn, production, story, run, delivery, has_snapshot, expected_boards)
    recovered = recovery_reads(conn) if recovery else {}


def fail_walk(error):
    raise error


store = os.environ["STUDIO_STORE_ROOT"]
files = size = 0
for directory, subdirs, names in os.walk(store, onerror=fail_walk):
    if directory == store and ".probe" in subdirs:
        subdirs.remove(".probe")
    for name in names:
        size += os.stat(os.path.join(directory, name), follow_symlinks=False).st_size
        files += 1
report = {"production/story/run/delivery/index counts": imports, "store files/bytes": [files, size], **recovered}
if phase not in {"preflight", "recovery-baseline"}:
    baseline = json.loads(expected)
    assert report == baseline, {"expected": baseline, "actual": report}
    print("runs by status", statuses)
print(json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True))
PY
  )
  printf '%s\n' "$report"
  if [[ $phase == preflight || $phase == recovery-baseline ]]; then
    (umask 077; set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$report" > "$baseline")
  fi
)

docs.title: Migration and application rollout
docs.text:
The source gate chain is cluster-apps → studio-migration → studio and studio-worker-registration → studio-worker. Registration also waits on the existing studio-render Kustomization and its HelmRelease health. The final worker gate requires both the healthy app and registration. All four Studio Kustomizations must be Ready at the same Git artifact revision. Keep render and the database components at their current configuration. The old app can keep serving if the migration fails. Investigate the Job and use a forward fix. For a changed or exhausted Job at the same digest, change its name and Flux health check together using the next -rN suffix.

The old API f30445f serves while the migration Job moves from 0004_go_live_approvals to 0007_escalation_packages. Revision 0005 creates the media job tables, lane events and promotions, and grants privileges to the runtime role on the new tables. Revision 0006 adds the formats tables and a nullable stories.format_version_id with a foreign key and a check that permits NULL. Existing story rows and old inserts therefore pass. The old code uses its declared columns and updates the story document, so pre-existing drafts with no relational pin remain writable. Revision 0007 creates the three escalation tables and adds their runtime grants. The three revisions leave the existing runtime grants, including asset_versions, in place. The old API checks the store and its database connection at readiness. It does not resolve the Alembic head. PostgreSQL still needs a schema lock for the new stories column and constraint. Keep writes idle and check the LAN during the migration. Studio migration source

From a LAN-capable terminal, record 200 at the root and 401 at /v1/me before, during and after the migration. docs.title: Postflight
docs.text:
Verify pod readiness and pins against the release record. Expect two pods of each app on distinct nodes and one worker on talosw01. The status imageID may be qualified by the runtime. Verify its digest and the configured image for each pod. Repeat the baseline snapshot. Use phase=postflight to check the pinned read paths on both imports. Both must return approval.legacy_run in the approval preview. The Winter Menu's recovered run must return 404 run.snapshot_missing. One More Meeting must return snapshot bytes that hash to its recorded SHA-256. Both draft summaries must load. One More Meeting has one board without created_by. The Winter Menu's recovered draft has zero boards.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  root=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio
  api="ghcr.io/thaynes43/haynes-studio@$(yq -e '.apiDigest' "$root/release.yaml")"
  web="ghcr.io/thaynes43/haynes-studio-web@$(yq -e '.webDigest' "$root/release.yaml")"
  for workload in api mcp web worker; do
    expected=$api
    replicas=2
    node=""
    if [[ $workload == web ]]; then expected=$web; fi
    if [[ $workload == worker ]]; then
      replicas=1
      node=talosw01
    fi
    kubectl -n ai get pod -l "app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-$workload" -o json |
      jq -er --arg image "$expected" --arg digest "${expected##*@}" \
        --arg node "$node" --argjson replicas "$replicas" '
        [.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)] |
        select(length == $replicas and
          ([.[].spec.nodeName] | unique | length) == $replicas and
          all(.[];
            ($node == "" or .spec.nodeName == $node) and
            .spec.containers[0].image == $image and .status.containerStatuses[0].ready and
            (.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID | endswith($digest)))) |
        .[] | [.metadata.name, .spec.nodeName, .spec.containers[0].image,
               .status.containerStatuses[0].imageID] | @tsv
      '
  done
  kubectl -n ai get pdb studio-api studio-mcp studio-web
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/studio-worker -c worker -- studio-worker --check-progress 1500
  kubectl -n ai logs deploy/studio-worker -c worker --since=2m | grep -c 'work/claim "HTTP/1.1 204'
)

No Studio-built run on this installation has exercised the 1,500-second liveness budget. Watch the worker's restart count throughout the first authorized build. If the count increases, check the pod events for a liveness kill and follow the recorded Wan job ID through recovery.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-worker --watch \
    -o 'custom-columns=POD:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount'

From an API pod, check the effective runtime grants. A table described as insert-only below also permits reads. The guard checks both table-level and column-level UPDATE grants, including inherited privileges. The only job updates are to the mutable worker columns. In particular, the requester stays fixed at insertion.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/studio-api -c api -- python - <<'PY'
import os

import psycopg

append_only = (
    "asset_versions", "asset_promotions", "queue_lane_events", "formats",
    "format_versions", "escalation_check_failures", "escalation_packages",
    "escalation_events", "go_live_approvals", "go_live_withdrawals",
)
mutable = {
    "media_job_lanes": {"next_position"},
    "media_jobs": {"document", "worker_id", "fence", "claim_until", "dispatched"},
    "stories": {"document", "format_version_id"},
}
with psycopg.connect(os.environ["STUDIO_DATABASE_URL"]) as conn:
    conn.read_only = True
    assert conn.execute("SELECT current_user").fetchone() == ("studio_app",)
    for table in (*append_only, *mutable):
        name = f"studio.{table}"
        privileges = conn.execute("""
            SELECT has_table_privilege(%s, 'SELECT'), has_table_privilege(%s, 'INSERT'),
                   has_table_privilege(%s, 'UPDATE'), has_table_privilege(%s, 'DELETE'),
                   has_table_privilege(%s, 'TRUNCATE')
        """, (name,) * 5).fetchone()
        assert privileges == (True, table != "media_job_lanes", False, False, False), (table, privileges)
        updates = {column for column, in conn.execute("""
            SELECT attname FROM pg_attribute
            WHERE attrelid = %s::regclass AND attnum > 0 AND NOT attisdropped
              AND has_column_privilege(attrelid, attnum, 'UPDATE')
        """, (name,))}
        assert updates == mutable.get(table, set()), (table, updates)
        print(table, "SELECT", "INSERT" if privileges[1] else "",
              "UPDATE columns", sorted(updates), "DELETE/TRUNCATE denied")
PY
)

import os

PY

from urllib.error import HTTPError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

from haynes_studio.queue.worker_tokens import worker_bearer

base = os.environ["STUDIO_API_URL"]
for label, token, expected in (
