docs.title: Roll back while keeping the new schema
docs.text:
Stop new submissions and let existing runs settle before changing the build revision. Require empty queues across all three lanes. Use the baseline's run-status guard and the media queue count before rollback. The old build lacks the lane-pause table and ignores pauses. If a queued OP959 run slips through, the old worker claims it and fails prebuild with work.revision_mismatch, before any engine submission. Voice and image jobs have no consumer at this pin. A nonempty media queue requires a backlog review before proceeding.

Revoke any provisioned escalation responder key before rollback. None is provisioned here. The older API lacks the route confinement for that key.

A corrective GitOps PR can restore the API, MCP, worker and web images from f30445f, along with their environment, build revision, worker provenance digest, old register generator and mounts. Recover those from OP957's merged tree. Remove the new worker probes with the worker rollback because that CLI lacks --check-progress. Keep the OP959 migration and worker-registration Jobs and their Flux gates, the existing worker token, the store and the inputs. The corrective PR's release check must enforce the previous app image pair and separately enforce the retained OP959 Job digest and names. Restoring the whole OP957 deployment would reintroduce the retired stages and the older migration Job, whose Alembic cannot resolve the new head.

The same additive schema reasoning allows f30445f to serve pre-upgrade data and imported playback at 0007_escalation_packages. Prefer fixing forward after the new app begins writing. The older API validates the whole story on each write and at enqueue. A single board stamped created_by by the new build blocks every old-build write and enqueue on that story. An old edit of a story's JSON format pin cannot update the new relational column and can fail its consistency check. Keep affected drafts and recipe changes paused during a rollback. Leave the database at the new head and keep the retained Jobs Complete. Reconcile the app and worker in the same dependency order. Repeat the baseline counts, ready pod and digest checks for the restored images, the pre-existing LAN routes, and signed-in imported playback. Use the retained migration Job's head evidence and rerun the runtime privilege check. The new routes and liveness check apply only while OP959 is installed.

docs.title: OP961 voice and image workers
docs.text:
Expected. OP961 uses the installed OP959 image digests (Studio 393fe1d) and schema (0007_escalation_packages). The licence register comes from the Python package in the image. Each media Deployment has one replica with Recreate, the existing low priority class and a 1-vCPU limit. Both are eligible off talosw01 (CR-37). The engines are remote, and layered compositing is one local still. The 20+4 vCPU budget on talosw01 is unchanged. Voice's provisional memory request/limit is 128/384 MiB. Image's is 192 MiB/1 GiB. Record memory and restarts during the authorized jobs.

Both lanes run as the NFS writer UID/GID. They need the writable canonical /studio store to read source blobs and publish results create-only. The voice lane reads reusable takes and writes WAV takes and the assembled track. The image lane reads reference and layer inputs and writes the PNG. Neither uses build staging or a separate scratch directory. The only other mount holds the main-thread progress marker. The 120-second voice budget covers a 45-second Wyoming exchange plus local assembly, store I/O and 15-second API calls. The 300-second image budget covers the 60-second ComfyUI HTTP inactivity timeout and gives reference preparation, single-still compositing and store I/O room. The worker touches progress before each queue and history request during long engine waits. Media worker source and progress contract

The API rolls both replicas with an nginx sidecar from the already pinned web image. A ConfigMap supplies its configuration. Media NetworkPolicies allow DNS, API port 8002 and each lane's engine: Kokoro Wyoming 10210 or ComfyUI TCP 8188 on the comfyui pod. There is no engine ingress policy to extend. API port 8002 accepts traffic from the two media Deployments. The listener forwards only the five media-work POSTs to the API over loopback, with no request retry or access logging. The API authenticates them. Traefik, MCP and the run worker keep using 8000. The new workers have no port 8000 grant. The dedicated listener enforces the HTTP path boundary without putting worker bearer headers into Cilium HTTP flow logging. Cilium HTTP policy Cilium header redaction settings

Each media lane has its own worker ID and ESO-generated token. Its registration Job uses the migration projection and --replace. The generator and ExternalSecret are prune-exempt. CreatedOnce plus creationPolicy: Orphan keep the same value across reconciles and ExternalSecret removal. A lost or revoked token cannot be fixed by re-registering the old value. The API associates the bearer with a worker ID and uses that ID in claim fences. It does not bind the ID to a lane. A registered worker token can claim any lane on the shared claim route. A source follow-up should bind explicit lane grants to worker identities, migrate the run identity, and reject out-of-lane claims before queue access. Worker administration

docs.title: Before enabling either consumer
docs.text: Run the read-only queued media jobs check immediately before merging this GitOps change. Flux can enable the consumers as soon as their dependencies are ready. Require a successful check with both counts zero. If either count is nonzero, stop for backlog review. The first consumer could otherwise drain stale requests in queue order against ComfyUI or Kokoro. Keep Studio users from submitting media jobs between the count and the start of both consumers.

docs.title: Reconcile and check health
docs.text:
The coordinator runs this after the GitOps PR has merged. Registration depends on the completed OP959 migration. The media worker stage depends on both registrations and the API sidecar being ready in the app stage. The existing run registration and worker stages have their own gates.

(
  set -uo pipefail
  failed=0
  check() {
    local label=$1
    shift
    if "$@"; then
      printf 'PASS %s\n' "$label"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$label" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  }
  stop_on_failure() {
    if (( failed )); then
      printf 'FAIL OP961 rollout verification\n' >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  }

  root=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio
  read_digest() {
    local value
    value=$(yq -er "$1" "$root/release.yaml") &&
      [[ $value =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] &&
      printf -v "$2" '%s' "$value"
  }
  pinned() {
    kubectl -n ai get deploy "$1" -o json |
      jq -e --arg name "$2" --arg image "$expected" '
        any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .name == $name and .image == $image)'
  }
  listener_ready() {
    kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-api -o json |
      jq -e --arg digest "$web_digest" '
        [.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)] |
        length == 2 and all(.[]; any(.status.containerStatuses[]?;
          .name == "media-worker-routes" and .ready and (.imageID | endswith($digest))))'
  }
  same_revision() {
    kubectl -n ai get kustomization studio-migration studio studio-media-worker-registration studio-media-workers \
      -o json | jq -e '
        [.items[].status.lastAppliedRevision] | select(length == 4) |
        unique | select(length == 1 and .[0] != null)'
  }
  worker_ready() {
    kubectl -n ai get pod -l "app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-$1-worker" -o json |
      jq -er --arg image "$expected" --arg digest "$digest" --arg lane "$1" '
        [.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)] | select(length == 1) | .[0] |
        select(.spec.nodeName != null and .spec.nodeName != "talosw01" and
          .spec.containers[0].args == ["--lane", $lane] and
          .spec.containers[0].image == $image and
          .status.containerStatuses[0].ready and
          (.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID | endswith($digest))) |
        [.metadata.name, .spec.nodeName, .status.containerStatuses[0].imageID,
          .status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount] | @tsv'
  }

  check 'release API digest' read_digest .apiDigest digest
  check 'release web digest' read_digest .webDigest web_digest
  stop_on_failure
  expected="ghcr.io/thaynes43/haynes-studio@$digest"
  check 'installed API pin' pinned studio-api api
  check 'installed run worker pin' pinned studio-worker worker
  check 'engine and migration readiness' kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=Ready --timeout=1m \
    helmrelease/kokoro helmrelease/comfyui kustomization/studio-migration
  stop_on_failure
  check 'reconcile parent' flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  stop_on_failure
  check 'reconcile Studio API' flux reconcile kustomization studio -n ai
  check 'API rollout' kubectl -n ai rollout status deploy/studio-api --timeout=5m
  check 'two ready API listeners at the web digest' listener_ready
  stop_on_failure
  check 'reconcile media registration' flux reconcile kustomization studio-media-worker-registration -n ai
  for lane in voice image; do
    check "$lane token projection" kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=Ready --timeout=2m \
      "externalsecret/studio-$lane-worker-token"
    if job=$(yq -er 'select(.kind == "Job") | .metadata.name' "$root/media-worker-registration/$lane-job.yaml"); then
      printf 'PASS %s registration Job name (%s)\n' "$lane" "$job"
      check "$lane registration completion" kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=complete --timeout=5m "job/$job"
      check "$lane registration logs" kubectl -n ai logs "job/$job" -c register
    else
      printf 'FAIL %s registration Job name\n' "$lane" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  done
  stop_on_failure
  check 'reconcile media workers' flux reconcile kustomization studio-media-workers -n ai
  check 'Studio and media stage readiness' kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=Ready --timeout=5m \
    kustomization/studio kustomization/studio-media-worker-registration kustomization/studio-media-workers
  check 'matching applied revisions' same_revision
  for lane in voice image; do
    check "$lane rollout" kubectl -n ai rollout status "deploy/studio-$lane-worker" --timeout=5m
    check "$lane pod placement, args and pin" worker_ready "$lane"
  done
  stop_on_failure
  printf 'PASS OP961 rollout verification\n'
)

In a quiet window expect at least one idle 204 from each consumer. Allow two 5-second poll intervals after rollout on an empty queue. Record progress and log counts together with the live launch arguments. For the run worker the command has no lane argument, so the pinned client sends the empty run claim. The two media clients send their configured lane in the claim body. Logs record status and path only. They do not record the body, so retain the launch argument check and the targeted 200s during the two real jobs as lane evidence.

(
  set -uo pipefail
  failed=0

docs.title: Two real jobs and people-only pause proof
docs.text:
Expected, with Tom. Pause and resume require his signed-in browser and X-Studio-CSRF. The coordinator can capture pod evidence while Tom makes these requests. The coordinator has no people's session or agent key, and the pinned studio-api-admin can administer credentials and import verified finished archives. It cannot create a draft production or request a job. The migration role is for those operator commands only. A future approved key could use read, draft:write and assets:generate on the single eligible production with 60-minute expiry and revocation after the check. Even that key could not pause the lane, create a production, or open an unselected result's people-only media routes. Use Tom's session for this proof.

Both imported stories are protected and their recorded asset versions lack media. Keep their boards and selections intact. Use a fresh Short draft in the existing production that owns the stock Kokoro voice. A read-only catalog check before OP961 found one promoted Kokoro-82M v1.0 voice definition (af_heart) scoped to a production, with no story or board scope. A stock definition supplies an engine voice ID and needs no recorded audio. Confirm the definition still appears through the API. Use no pinned photos, cast or set stills.

Tom can issue the API requests below in his signed-in Studio browser. This helper is for a same-origin console at https://studio.haynesops.com. Run one step at a time. Keep the session cookie in the browser and record only statuses, IDs, timings and hashes.

const studio = await (async () => {
  if (location.origin !== "https://studio.haynesops.com") throw Error("Open Studio first");
  const me = await fetch("/v1/me").then((response) => response.json());
  if (me.principal?.kind !== "human" || !me.csrf_token) throw Error("Sign in to Studio");
  return async (method, path, body, extra = {}, expected = 200) => {
    const headers = new Headers(extra);
    if (method !== "GET") headers.set("X-Studio-CSRF", me.csrf_token);
    if (body !== undefined) headers.set("Content-Type", "application/json");
    const response = await fetch(path, {method, headers, body: JSON.stringify(body)});
    const result = await response.json();
    if (response.status !== expected) throw Error(`${response.status} ${result.error?.code ?? ""}`);
    return result;
  };
})();
  1. Read GET /v1/assets?kind=voice and choose the promoted Kokoro definition with scope.production_id set and both scope.story_id and scope.board_id empty. Use its production and version IDs. The production already has Short enabled. Create a new story and board through the browser:
const voices = await studio("GET", "/v1/assets?kind=voice");
const stock = voices.items.find((v) => v.state === "promoted" &&
  v.scope.production_id && !v.scope.story_id && !v.scope.board_id &&
  v.attributes.voice_id === "af_heart" && v.provenance.generator?.model === "Kokoro-82M v1.0");
if (!stock) throw Error("No eligible stock voice");
const story = await studio("POST", `/v1/productions/${stock.scope.production_id}/media-types/short/stories`,
  {title: "OP961 media proof", narrator_voice_version_id: stock.id}, {}, 201);
const board = await studio("POST", `/v1/stories/${story.id}/boards`, {
  lines: [{speaker: "narrator", text: "The tiny kettle is ready.", gap_before_ms: null}],
  method: {layer: "whole_frame", motion: "i2v"},
  photo: {current_version_id: null, prompt: "A tiny yellow kettle on a blue table",
    input_asset_version_ids: []},
}, {"If-Match": String(story.revision)}, 201);

  1. Voice first. GET /v1/queue/lanes must show the voice lane open before starting. Send PUT /v1/queue/lanes/voice with {"paused":true}. With the lane paused, send POST /v1/boards/<board.id>/voice-jobs with {} and a unique Idempotency-Key. Expect 202. Observe its job still queued after at least two idle poll intervals through GET /v1/jobs/<id> and worker 204s. Send PUT /v1/queue/lanes/voice with {"paused":false}. Poll the same job to succeeded and check result_is_current: true. This board has one uncached line, so it requires one Kokoro take.

  2. Image next. Begin with the image lane open and verify no other Studio image job is active. The coordinator observes ComfyUI with the GET-only probe below. If household work is present, let it finish and observe the worker's backoff if the two overlap. Do not create household load to force that condition. Tom pauses image with PUT /v1/queue/lanes/image and {"paused":true}. Send POST /v1/boards/<board.id>/photo-jobs with {"seed":0} and its own unique Idempotency-Key. Expect 202 while paused and confirm that job remains queued through two poll intervals. It is a whole-frame text-to-image request with no reference images. Read GET /v1/boards/<board.id> and use its revision as If-Match for PATCH /v1/boards/<board.id>. Send only photo, preserving its fields and changing prompt to "A tiny yellow kettle on a green table". Resume image with PUT /v1/queue/lanes/image and {"paused":false}. Expect the single original job to succeed with result_is_current: false. Confirm the board's photo.current_version_id is still null. Keep the draft and both results as private evidence. Restore any lane paused by the procedure before ending the window, including on a failed check.

  3. For each successful job, use GET /v1/jobs/<id>/result. Take the WAV hash from voice.track.sha256 and the PNG hash from content.sha256. Fetch the corresponding /v1/jobs/<id>/media/<sha256> through Tom's browser. Check 200, audio/wav or image/png, and SHA-256 of the returned bytes. The same version is readable through /v1/asset-versions/<version-id>/media/<sha256> for a signed-in person. The generic media route is not the proof path for the unselected PNG. Keep file bytes, request bodies, cookie and CSRF out of evidence. Record Tom's Inspector/Composer review and acceptance separately. The pinned web client does not expose a photo-job button, so this procedure uses the authenticated API for the photo.

Use a fresh key for each of the two job requests. In a transport ambiguity reuse that request's exact body and key to find the same job. Do not submit an additional job to compensate for a failed inference. API requests, results and queue controls

docs.title: Shared engine evidence
docs.text:
The image worker checks both queue lists before starting and checks again immediately before marking dispatch and submitting the prompt. A busy engine causes a ten-second backoff, up to 30 minutes. An unreadable queue stops that job. The last idle check and POST are separate requests, so household work can arrive in between. Studio submits one prompt and polls its specific history before it can move to another job. With an uncertain dispatch it does not retry the prompt, interrupt, or clear any queue entry. Image edits can upload an input before the second idle check. Layered stills compose locally. For this proof the photo has no input upload. Queue ordering and busy/unknown fixtures

Before the image lane resumes, take this read-only sample through the image pod's permitted engine connection. Repeat it during the wait only if needed to observe existing household work.

(
  set -uo pipefail
  if kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/studio-image-worker -c worker -- python - <<'PY'
import os
from datetime import UTC, datetime

import httpx

with httpx.Client(base_url=os.environ["STUDIO_COMFYUI_URL"], trust_env=False, timeout=5) as client:
    try:
        response = client.get("/queue")
        response.raise_for_status()
    except httpx.HTTPError as error:
        raise SystemExit(f"FAIL GET /queue ({type(error).__name__})") from None
    print("PASS GET /queue", response.status_code)
    try:
        queue = response.json()
    except ValueError:
        raise SystemExit("FAIL /queue JSON") from None
    results = []
    for key in ("queue_running", "queue_pending"):
        entries = queue.get(key) if isinstance(queue, dict) else None
        passed = isinstance(entries, list)
        results.append(passed)
        print(datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(), "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", key,
              len(entries) if passed else "expected list")
raise SystemExit(0 if all(results) else 1)
PY
  then
    printf 'PASS ComfyUI queue sample\n'
  else
    printf 'FAIL ComfyUI queue sample\n' >&2
    exit 1
  fi
)

Capture a UTC timestamp just before the first job is enqueued. After both finish, substitute that timestamp below. For the two isolated jobs the expected successful claim counts are zero run, one voice, one image. For image, read the final GET /queue, the successful API POST /publish, the single POST /prompt and the resulting history fetch in order. Compare any household busy interval with the completed job's waited_s and the image engine job ID in its result provenance. If the household queue was idle throughout, mark live busy backoff unobserved and link the source fixture instead. Preserve only aggregate counts, statuses and the IDs for this proof.

  since='<UTC RFC3339 start time>'

    if ! logs=$(kubectl -n ai logs "deploy/$worker" -c worker --since-time="$since" --timestamps); then

    if count=$(awk '/\/work\/claim "HTTP\/1.1 200/ {n++} END {print n+0}' <<< "$logs") &&
       [[ $count == "$expected" ]]; then
      printf 'PASS %s successful claims (%s)\n' "$worker" "$count"
    else

    if [[ $worker == studio-image-worker ]]; then

         prompts=$(awk '/POST .*\/prompt "HTTP\/1.1/ {n++} END {print n+0}' <<< "$logs") &&
         [[ $prompts == 1 ]]; then
        printf 'PASS image worker prompt count (1)\n'
      else
        printf 'FAIL image worker prompt count (expected 1)\n' >&2
        failed=1
      fi
    fi
  done
  if (( failed )); then
    printf 'FAIL worker log verification\n' >&2

docs.title: Rotation and rollback
docs.text:
For planned rotation, drain the lane in an idle maintenance window. Add a new digest-independent, versioned token generator and Orphan ExternalSecret. Use the new token reference in the lane Deployment and registration Job and keep the same worker ID. Add --replace to the rotation Job's arguments. Bump that Job's digest-suffixed name and Flux health check to the next -rN (start at -r1). Reconcile registration before the workers. The existing pod's old bearer is revoked as soon as --replace commits. Expect a brief interruption until the new pod starts. Verify internal 422 and idle 204 with the replacement before resuming. For a retry with the same secret, use a fresh Job suffix and leave the credential references alone. An already revoked digest needs a fresh token.

For rollback, drain both lanes where possible. Revert just the OP961 source through GitOps and keep OP959's app pin. Flux prunes the media worker Deployments, their policies and Jobs. The API rolls back to its 8000-only pod template. Keep both tokens registered and their prune-exempt projections so reinstalling adopts the same tokens. If a token is ever compromised, revoke that ID with the migration role and rotate before reinstalling. Completed or queued jobs, catalog entries and result blobs remain in place. A paused lane can be left paused while the workers are absent.

(
  set -uo pipefail
  failed=0
  check() {
    local label=$1
    shift
    if "$@"; then
      printf 'PASS %s\n' "$label"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$label" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  }
  absent() {
    local found
    found=$(kubectl -n ai get "deployment/studio-$1-worker" --ignore-not-found -o name) &&
      [[ -z $found ]]
  }
  api_port() {
    kubectl -n ai get svc studio-api -o json | jq -e '[.spec.ports[].port] == [8000]'
  }
  check 'reconcile parent after revert' flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  if (( failed == 0 )); then
    check 'reconcile Studio API' flux reconcile kustomization studio -n ai
    check 'API rollout' kubectl -n ai rollout status deploy/studio-api --timeout=5m
    check 'run worker rollout' kubectl -n ai rollout status deploy/studio-worker --timeout=5m
    for lane in voice image; do
      check "$lane Deployment pruned" absent "$lane"
      check "$lane token projection retained" kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=Ready --timeout=1m \
        "externalsecret/studio-$lane-worker-token"
    done
    check 'API service exposes only port 8000' api_port
  fi
  if (( failed )); then
    printf 'FAIL OP961 rollback verification\n' >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  printf 'PASS OP961 rollback verification\n'
)

docs.title: OP964 third release
docs.text:
Proven (2026-11-25, 11:14Z to 11:18Z): this pin is installed. Evidence: OP964, comment 10061. Changed: the postflight probe at first asserted that The Winter Menu's run document carries no snapshot reference. It does; only the stored snapshot is absent. The assertion below is corrected, and the probe passed in full with it. The anonymous ingress block was run from inside the cluster through the internal ingress with the certificate verified, since the coordinator's pod has no LAN route.

OP964 promotes feedback and iterations, the reference-photo composer, private release packages, the Assets page, the staging archive and worker lane grants. The coordinator reviews, merges and rolls out the pin. All checks below are expected until the coordinator records installed evidence.

Use release.yaml for the revision, digest pair and successful Studio images run ID. The Python digest covers the API, MCP, three workers, migration and three registration Jobs. The web digest covers the web pods and the API's media-worker listener.

The selected pair (Studio 80975a9) includes Studio PRs 116, 118, 120, 121, 123, 125, 127, 128 and 131. Its Alembic head is 0012_release_constraints. OP437 is outside this pin. PR 128 is the matting adapter's source (OP451): nothing calls it yet, and the matting sidecar is not part of this pin. The coordinator repinned from b182c1d with the command below after PRs 131 and 128 merged. For a repin, select a successful main publish containing all nine PRs. Run the following from haynes-ops with the selected full SHA and publish run ID. It verifies both Linux/amd64 tags, immutable manifests and revision labels anonymously, then updates the release record, workload references and digest-named Job gates together. Update the recorded PR ancestry and migration head. Studio images

uv run --no-project --with PyYAML==6.0.3 -- python -I -B scripts/tests/studio-release/check.py \
  --pin "$studio_revision" "$studio_publish_run"

Drain on termination (added with this pin). The API container, its media-worker listener, MCP and web each sleep 8 seconds in preStop before they receive the stop signal, inside the default 30-second grace period. A terminating pod stays in the ingress's rotation for a moment; without the drain the next request to it is a 502, on a pod delete and on every roll. The release check requires the sleep on all four containers. The first roll to this pin still terminates pods of the previous pin, which have no drain, so a brief 502 is possible during this roll only. Once this pin is installed, the one-app-pod recovery check can require zero failed requests.

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
Before merging, arrange an idle window and keep submissions stopped until postflight passes. Flux can pick up the merge before a manual reconcile. Require all three postgres16 instances Ready, ready Studio stages and existing projections, ready Kokoro and ComfyUI, and room for the extra API pod on a separate eligible node. Check database readiness and OP961 installed evidence (comments 9993, 9997 and 10002). Review the current shared ComfyUI queue using the image worker and submit nothing.

docs.title: Imported productions and queue counts
docs.text:
Run this block in preflight on the old API and retain the baseline. All modes call the running build's publication and approval filters and check both imported story IDs. Run postflight only after the pod check on the new pair. Use compare after an image rollback with a fresh preflight baseline taken immediately before rollback. Choose a different path for that baseline via STUDIO_OP964_BASELINE. Use the same path for each preflight and its follow-up.

Run preflight immediately before merge. The probe counts queued and running work in each of the run, voice and image lanes. A held run also stops the roll for review. With maxUnavailable: 0, the old API serves while the new API becomes Ready. Old API pods can authenticate existing worker tokens without enforcing the lane grants until the last old pod is gone.

Every mode uses a read-only snapshot as studio_app over TLS. Postflight calls the same database and validation helpers as the new read routes. Both imports must have empty feedback, no active iteration, no frozen release target or package, and an empty staging archive. Each is unpublished and unapproved. Release eligibility must report approval.legacy_run. A package list represents only prepared packages, so the legacy case has no package row to display as held. Its eligibility refusal is the held reason that the release view would use. The catalog must expose One More Meeting's recorded-only versions by their frozen IDs. The recovered Winter Menu run has no frozen catalog pins. Shared catalog entries can appear for either production and are separate from those pins. The snapshot and draft results follow OP959. See the Studio references for feedback, release and archive.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  phase=${STUDIO_OP964_PHASE:-preflight}
  baseline=${STUDIO_OP964_BASELINE:-"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:?}/studio-op964-baseline.json"}
  revision=$(yq -er '.revision' kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio/release.yaml)
  expected=
  if [[ $phase != preflight ]]; then
    expected=$(<"$baseline")
    test -n "$expected"
  fi
  report=$(kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/studio-api -c api -- python -I -B - \
      "$phase" "$expected" "$revision" <<'PY'
import json
import os
import sys
from hashlib import sha256

from haynes_studio.db import drafts, runs
from haynes_studio.db.engine import connect_engine, snapshot


films = (
    ("One More Meeting", "prd_01M7ZGYNHFET1GKR4304FVD4PE",
     "sty_01M7ZGYNHFET1GKR4304FVD4PF", "run_01M7ZHNZJ2PWA8XR8K7KKWP17V",
     "dlv_01M7ZHP1QS82QGK196ZPCM7MQS", True, 1),
    ("The Winter Menu", "prd_01M79V9FC00000000000000001",
     "sty_01M79V9FC00000000000000001", "run_01M7C5CJA7XKBCRPM0ZRP2P5RS",
     "dlv_01M7C5D3KFX3MFVWCXBCVJHMG7", False, 0),
)


def check(label, operation, *args):
    try:
        result = operation(*args)
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"FAIL {label} ({type(error).__name__})", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    print(f"PASS {label}: {result}", file=sys.stderr)
    return True


def queue_counts(conn):
    queued, running, held = conn.exec_driver_sql("""
        SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE document->>'status' = 'queued'),
               count(*) FILTER (WHERE document->>'status' = 'running'),
               count(*) FILTER (WHERE document->>'status' = 'held')
        FROM studio.runs
    """).one()
    media = conn.exec_driver_sql("""
        SELECT lanes.lane,
               count(jobs.id) FILTER (WHERE jobs.document->>'status' = 'queued'),
               count(jobs.id) FILTER (WHERE jobs.document->>'status' = 'running')
        FROM studio.media_job_lanes AS lanes
        LEFT JOIN studio.media_jobs AS jobs ON jobs.lane = lanes.lane
        GROUP BY lanes.lane ORDER BY lanes.lane
    """).tuples().all()
    print("run queued/running/held", queued, running, held, file=sys.stderr)
    for lane, queued_media, running_media in media:
        print(f"{lane} queued/running", queued_media, running_media, file=sys.stderr)
    assert (queued, running, held) == (0, 0, 0)
    assert media == [("image", 0, 0), ("voice", 0, 0)]
    return "all three lanes idle"


def unpack_import(conn, production, story, run, delivery):
    row = runs.get(conn, run)
    assert (row["production_id"], row["story_id"]) == (production, story)
    assert row["document"]["delivery_id"] == delivery
    return row


def check_draft(conn, production, story, expected_boards):
    draft = drafts.get_draft(conn, story)
    assert all("created_by" not in board for board in draft.boards.values())
    summary = draft.summary(conn)
    assert (summary["id"], summary["production_id"]) == (story, production)
    assert summary["derived"]["board_count"] == len(draft.boards) == expected_boards

    # This calls the installed build's real publication and approval filters.
    def listed(published, approved):
        return {
            item["id"] for item in drafts.list_stories(
                conn, production, summary["media_kind"], None, 50, published=published, approved=approved,
            )
        }

    assert story in listed(False, False)
    assert story not in listed(True, None) and story not in listed(None, True)
    return f"{expected_boards} boards, unpublished, unapproved"


def check_approval(conn, row, delivery):
    from haynes_studio.api.approval_routes import _check_approval, _delivery
    from haynes_studio.golive import packages, records

    delivered = _delivery(conn, row["id"])
    assert delivered is not None and delivered["id"] == delivery
    active = conn.scalar(records.active_id(row["id"]))
    _, refusal, _ = _check_approval(
        row["document"], delivered, delivered["master"]["sha256"], True, active,
        lambda: packages.for_run(conn, row["id"]), preview=True,
    )
    assert active is None and refusal is not None and refusal.details["code"] == "approval.legacy_run"
    return refusal.details["code"]


def check_snapshot(conn, row, has_snapshot):
    from haynes_studio.api.errors import APIError
    from haynes_studio.api.run_routes import _stored_snapshot
    from haynes_studio.store.local import LocalStore

    try:
        pin = runs.get(conn, row["id"], snapshot_pin_only=True)
        response = _stored_snapshot(LocalStore(os.environ["STUDIO_STORE_ROOT"]), pin, None)
    except APIError as error:
        # A recovered run has no stored snapshot (the column is null). Its document still
        # names the snapshot it was built from, so that reference is not null.
        assert not has_snapshot and row["snapshot"] is None
        assert (error.status_code, error.details["code"]) == (404, "run.snapshot_missing")
        return "404 run.snapshot_missing (recovered run)"
    digest = sha256(response.body).hexdigest()
    assert has_snapshot and response.status_code == 200 and digest == row["document"]["snapshot"]["sha256"]
    return f"200 SHA-256 {digest}"


def check_feedback(conn, story, run):
    from haynes_studio.feedback import records

    assert records.list_candidates(conn, story, run, None, 51) == []
    assert records.draft_iteration(conn, story) is None
    return "zero candidates and no active iteration"


def check_packages(conn, row):
    from haynes_studio.api.errors import APIError
    from haynes_studio.api.release_routes import _require_releasable, _review_evidence
    from haynes_studio.golive import packages

    assert packages.targets(row["snapshot"]) == []
    assert packages.for_run(conn, row["id"]) == []
    current, refusal = _review_evidence(conn, row)
    assert current is None and refusal is not None
    try:
        _require_releasable(None, None, refusal)
    except APIError as error:
        assert (error.status_code, error.details["code"]) == (422, "approval.legacy_run")
        return "zero targets and packages, eligibility refused (approval.legacy_run)"
    raise AssertionError("legacy release unexpectedly allowed")


def check_catalog(conn, production, row, has_snapshot):
    from haynes_studio.db import catalog

    frozen = {version["id"] for version in row["frozen_library"]}
    assert bool(frozen) == has_snapshot
    visible = catalog.find_assets(
        conn, {production}, kind=None, labels=[], production_id=production,
        version_ids=frozen, after=None, limit=len(frozen) + 1,
    )
    assert {version["id"] for version in visible} == frozen
    assert all(version["recorded_without_media"] and version["scope"]["production_id"] == production
               for version in visible)
    # Exercise the unfiltered first page as the catalog does; shared results are permitted.
    page = catalog.find_assets(
        conn, {production}, kind=None, labels=[], production_id=production,
        version_ids=None, after=None, limit=51,
    )
    assert all(version["scope"]["production_id"] in (None, production) for version in page)
    return f"{len(visible)} recorded-only frozen versions, {min(50, len(page))} first-page entries"


def check_archive(conn, production):
    from haynes_studio.db import staging_archive

    drafts.production(conn, production)
    assert staging_archive.production_records(conn, production, None, 51) == []
    return "zero staging archive records"


def import_counts(conn, production, story, run, delivery):
    return list(conn.exec_driver_sql("""
        SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.productions WHERE id = %s),
               (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.stories WHERE id = %s AND production_id = %s),
               (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.runs WHERE id = %s AND story_id = %s),
               (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.deliveries WHERE id = %s AND run_id = %s),
               (SELECT count(*) FROM studio.delivery_media WHERE run_id = %s)
    """, (production, story, production, run, story, delivery, run, run)).one())


def fail_walk(error):
    raise error


def store_counts():
    store = os.environ["STUDIO_STORE_ROOT"]
    files = size = 0
    for directory, subdirs, names in os.walk(store, onerror=fail_walk):
        if directory == store and ".probe" in subdirs:
            subdirs.remove(".probe")
        for name in names:
            size += os.stat(os.path.join(directory, name), follow_symlinks=False).st_size
            files += 1
    return [files, size]


phase, expected, revision = sys.argv[1:]

    results.append(check("queue counts", db_check, queue_counts))

docs.title: Migration and rollout
docs.text:
The installed starting point is Studio 393fe1d at 0007_escalation_packages. Migrate to the head shipped in the selected Python image. The old API reads named columns, checks database and store readiness, and continues serving after the schema transaction commits. Changes to existing tables can take locks. The whole upgrade is one transaction: the ALTER TABLE stories and the index on runs in 0008 and the SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock on stories in 0009 are held until the single commit after 0012, so the old API's story reads wait for the entire run (seconds on this data, against its 30-second statement timeout), and a failure in any revision rolls the schema back to 0007 with 393fe1d still serving. Sample old API availability before, during and after migration. Migration source

Revision Schema change Effect on the serving 393fe1d build 0008_candidate_feedback Creates append-only candidates, notes and iterations, adds nullable stories.feedback_iteration_id and a partial expression index on run answers, and grants scoped runtime access. Old story inserts omit the nullable reference and old edits update named columns. The partial index applies only to run documents with answers. 0009_release_packages Adds append-only package, publication and iteration-clear tables. Locks stories in SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE mode, installs a constraint trigger on story insert/update for a non-null feedback iteration, and validates existing references against the candidate's run story. Old inserts and existing drafts without an active iteration pass the trigger condition. The previous API's published status, list filters and story insert default still use stories.published. This migration preserves the Boolean column and its default. 0010_staging_archive Creates production-scoped archive records and immutable version chains and grants runtime SELECT and INSERT. Old API and workers never query these tables. The production foreign key uses existing IDs. 0011_worker_lane_grants Creates a SELECT-only runtime grant table and seeds studio-worker → run, studio-voice-worker → voice and studio-image-worker → image. The new API joins the binding to the active worker identity. Old API ignores the table. The migration changes neither token rows nor token projections. Lane enforcement starts on a per-pod basis at the API rollout. 0012_release_constraints (OP963) Backfills publications.target_id from the package, rejects duplicate run/target publications, constrains the package byte count and composite publication/package identity, and requires archive version parents and roots to be contiguous (the root FK is deferred). These release and archive tables were introduced after the old build. At a first upgrade from 0007 they have no rows to backfill or validate. If an intermediate pin has already written records, resolve any data-integrity failure through a reviewed forward fix.

The selected publish has one Alembic head, 0012, whose parents in order are 0011, 0010, 0009 and 0008. Read the migration Job output for the actual revisions and head. Expect the migrator to use TLS and the configured role policies to refuse the other connections. Record a missed active window explicitly if the Job finishes before a sample. Use the following during the change from a LAN-capable terminal.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  root=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio
  job=$(yq -er 'select(.kind == "Job") | .metadata.name' "$root/migration/job.yaml")
  date -u
  kubectl -n ai get "job/$job" --ignore-not-found
  kubectl -n ai get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-api \
    -o 'custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,READY:.status.containerStatuses[0].ready,IMAGE:.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID'
  base=https://studio.haynesops.com
  status() { curl -sS --max-time 15 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$1"; }
  test "$(status "$base/")" = 200
  test "$(status "$base/v1/me")" = 401
  printf 'PASS LAN root=200 v1/me=401\n'
)

Registration follows migration. Each digest-named Job mounts the existing projection for its worker. In the token administration code a matching active token exits successfully with audit status 200 before writing anything. For this release the Job arguments omit --replace so a different token for an existing ID fails with a conflict. An audit 201 would mean a first registration and is unexpected on this installed cluster. Stop and look at that worker's state before resuming submissions.

After merge, from the coordinator session, follow the existing Flux dependencies. Controllers can start dependent stages as soon as their gates pass. A failed migration leaves the previous app available. Use a forward fix and change the Job name and health check together for a retry at the same digest (-rN). Keep the existing projections, storage and engine configuration.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  root=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio
  job_name() { yq -er 'select(.kind == "Job") | .metadata.name' "$root/$1"; }

  flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  flux reconcile kustomization studio-migration -n ai
  job=$(job_name migration/job.yaml)
  kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=complete --timeout=5m "job/$job"
  kubectl -n ai logs "job/$job" -c migrate

  flux reconcile kustomization studio -n ai
  for workload in api mcp web; do
    kubectl -n ai rollout status "deploy/studio-$workload" --timeout=5m
  done
  flux reconcile kustomization studio-worker-registration -n ai
  flux reconcile kustomization studio-media-worker-registration -n ai
  for worker in worker voice-worker image-worker; do
    case "$worker" in
      worker) job=$(job_name worker-registration/job.yaml) ;;
      *) job=$(job_name "media-worker-registration/${worker%-worker}-job.yaml") ;;
    esac
    kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=complete --timeout=5m "job/$job"
    kubectl -n ai logs "job/$job" -c register | jq -ser --arg worker "studio-$worker" '
      map(select(.worker_id == $worker and .status != null) | .status)
      | select(. == [200]) | .[0]'
    printf 'PASS %s existing registration\n' "$worker"
  done
  for stage in studio-worker studio-media-workers; do
    flux reconcile kustomization "$stage" -n ai
  done
  for worker in worker voice-worker image-worker; do
    kubectl -n ai rollout status "deploy/studio-$worker" --timeout=5m
  done
  kubectl -n ai get kustomization studio-migration studio studio-worker-registration \
    studio-worker studio-media-worker-registration studio-media-workers -o json |
    jq -er '
      [.items[] | select(any(.status.conditions[]?; .type == "Ready" and .status == "True"))] |
      select(length == 6) | [.[].status.lastAppliedRevision] | unique |
      select(length == 1 and .[0] != null) | .[0]'
)

docs.title: Postflight
docs.text:
Run each block before allowing submissions. Require both API containers on the pair, two Ready API, MCP and web replicas on distinct nodes within each Deployment, and one Ready worker per lane. The run worker stays on talosw01 and both media workers stay off it. Require zero restarts on every container. The check includes terminating pods so a terminating old API fails the gate for worker claim probes. Expect each worker's progress check and idle-claim log check from OP961 to pass again.

(
  set -uo pipefail
  root=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio
  api_digest=$(yq -er '.apiDigest' "$root/release.yaml") || exit 1
  web_digest=$(yq -er '.webDigest' "$root/release.yaml") || exit 1
  api="ghcr.io/thaynes43/haynes-studio@$api_digest"
  web="ghcr.io/thaynes43/haynes-studio-web@$web_digest"
  failed=0
  for workload in api mcp web worker voice-worker image-worker; do
    replicas=2
    placement=any
    case "$workload" in
      api) containers=$(jq -cn --arg api "$api" --arg web "$web" \
             '{api:$api, "media-worker-routes":$web}') ;;
      mcp) containers=$(jq -cn --arg api "$api" '{mcp:$api}') ;;
      web) containers=$(jq -cn --arg web "$web" '{nginx:$web}') ;;
      *)
        replicas=1
        placement=off-talosw01
        if [[ $workload == worker ]]; then placement=talosw01; fi
        containers=$(jq -cn --arg api "$api" '{worker:$api}') ;;
    esac
    if kubectl -n ai get pods -l "app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-$workload" -o json |
      jq -er --argjson containers "$containers" --argjson replicas "$replicas" \
        --arg placement "$placement" '
        .items | select(length == $replicas and
          ([.[].spec.nodeName] | unique | length) == $replicas and
          all(.[];
            .metadata.deletionTimestamp == null and .spec.nodeName != null and
            ($placement == "any" or
             ($placement == "talosw01" and .spec.nodeName == "talosw01") or
             ($placement == "off-talosw01" and .spec.nodeName != "talosw01")) and
            any(.status.conditions[]?; .type == "Ready" and .status == "True") and
            ([.spec.containers[] | {key:.name,value:.image}] | from_entries) == $containers and
            (.status.containerStatuses | length) == ($containers | length) and
            all(.status.containerStatuses[]; . as $c |
              ($containers[$c.name] // "" | split("@") | .[1]) as $digest |
              $digest != null and .ready and .restartCount == 0 and (.imageID | endswith($digest))))) |
        .[] | [.metadata.name, .spec.nodeName, (.status.containerStatuses[].imageID)] | @tsv'
    then
      printf 'PASS studio-%s pods, pins and restarts\n' "$workload"
    else
      printf 'FAIL studio-%s pods, pins or restarts\n' "$workload" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  done
  if (( failed )); then
    printf 'FAIL OP964 pod verification\n' >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  printf 'PASS OP964 pod verification\n'
)

Run the import and queue probe with STUDIO_OP964_PHASE=postflight and the original baseline. Run the OP961 engine block from the voice and image pods. It opens a Kokoro connection and reads GET /queue from shared ComfyUI. From the run pod, open and close one TCP connection to its configured Wan service. This establishes reachability for all three workers without requesting engine work.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/studio-worker -c worker -- python -I -B - <<'PY'
import os
import socket
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

service = urlsplit(os.environ["STUDIO_WAN_URL"])
try:
    socket.create_connection((service.hostname, service.port), timeout=5).close()
except OSError as error:
    raise SystemExit(f"FAIL run worker reaches its engine ({type(error).__name__})") from None
print("PASS run worker reaches its engine")
PY
)

Check internal/studio in Gatus using the existing Gatus procedure. Record a passing timestamp after reconcile and within two one-minute probe intervals. Confirm the anonymous /v1/me response on the LAN is 401. A passing health result alone does not verify any signed-in feature.

docs.title: Worker lane grants
docs.text:
Run this block only after the pin, registration and queue checks pass. It repeats the API pin and endpoint gates before sending a well-formed claim for another lane. The grants query checks the three seeded IDs, and the worker Deployment checks bind each probe to the same existing projection used by its successful registration Job. The probes use the workers' own API addresses and read the token within each worker process. They never send a well-formed claim for the caller's lane. Authenticated invalid JSON gets 422 and cannot reach the claim handler. Each well-formed cross-lane request must return 403 work.lane_forbidden before the claim transaction starts.

(

  root=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio

  digest=$(yq -er '.apiDigest' "$root/release.yaml")

  endpoints=$(kubectl -n ai get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=studio-api -o json)
  if jq -e --arg digest "$digest" --argjson endpoints "$endpoints" '
    .items as $pods |
    ($pods | length) == 2 and
    all($pods[];
      .metadata.deletionTimestamp == null and
      any(.status.containerStatuses[]?; .name == "api" and .ready and (.imageID | endswith($digest)))) and
    ([$endpoints.items[].endpoints[] | select(.conditions.ready == true) | .targetRef.uid] | unique)
    == ([$pods[].metadata.uid] | unique)
  ' <<< "$pods" >/dev/null; then
    printf 'PASS both API endpoints use the selected pin\n'
  else
    printf 'FAIL API pin or endpoints, skip all cross-lane claims\n' >&2
    exit 1

docs.title: Anonymous ingress and MCP
docs.text:
Verify the internal ingress uses the API's public HTTP port and serves the web root. Requests use the existing certificate validation. All listed API reads and writes must return 401 without an identity. Worker and MCP paths must return 404 at the ingress. Also repeat the existing route and playback checks for the older routes and both delivery proxies.

(
  set -uo pipefail
  base=https://studio.haynesops.com
  production=prd_01M7ZGYNHFET1GKR4304FVD4PE
  story=sty_01M7ZGYNHFET1GKR4304FVD4PF
  run=run_01M7ZHNZJ2PWA8XR8K7KKWP17V
  printf -v absent_digest '%064d' 0
  failed=0
  check() {
    local expected=$1 method=$2 path=$3 status=transport-error
    local -a body=()
    if [[ $method == POST || $method == DELETE ]]; then
      body=(-H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary '{')
    fi
    if status=$(curl -q -sS --max-time 15 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
        -X "$method" "${body[@]}" "$base$path") && [[ $status == "$expected" ]]; then
      printf 'PASS %s %s %s\n' "$method" "$path" "$status"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %s %s got %s expected %s\n' "$method" "$path" "$status" "$expected" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  }

  check 200 GET /
  for path in /v1/me "/v1/stories/$story/candidates?run_id=$run" \
    "/v1/runs/$run/release-packages" "/v1/runs/$run/release-packages/$absent_digest/download" \
    "/v1/assets?production=$production" \
    "/v1/productions/$production/archive-records" \
    /v1/archive-records/arc_00000000000000000000000001 \
    /v1/archive-versions/arv_00000000000000000000000001; do
    check 401 GET "$path"
  done
  for path in "/v1/runs/$run/candidates" "/v1/runs/$run/release-packages" \
    "/v1/runs/$run/go-live-approvals" \
    "/v1/runs/$run/publications" "/v1/productions/$production/archive-records" \
    /v1/archive-records/arc_00000000000000000000000001/versions \
    /v1/archive-versions/arv_00000000000000000000000001/apply \
    /v1/candidates/cnd_00000000000000000000000001/feedback \
    /v1/candidates/cnd_00000000000000000000000001/iterations \
    /v1/asset-jobs; do
    check 401 POST "$path"
  done
  check 401 DELETE "/v1/stories/$story/feedback-iteration"
  for path in /healthz /readyz /mcp /mcp/upload /internal/v1/work/claim; do
    check 404 GET "$path"
  done
  if (( failed )); then
    printf 'FAIL OP964 anonymous ingress\n' >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  printf 'PASS OP964 anonymous ingress\n'
)

Cluster MCP checks the bearer before reading the request body or applying tool-specific byte limits. A small ordinary call and a bounded request just over 256 KiB must both return 401. The latter demonstrates auth ordering. Verifying the exceptions requires authenticated tool dispatch. The Studio source fixture test_only_archive_text_writers_get_larger_mcp_envelopes covers the 256 KiB default, the 2 MiB wire ceiling for studio_create_archive_record and studio_add_archive_version, and refusals for other tool names and non-call messages. /mcp/upload has its separate existing limit. Record the live 401s and cite the fixture for cap evidence. MCP reference and fixture.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/studio-api -c api -- python -I -B - <<'PY'
import httpx

base = "http://studio-mcp.ai.svc.cluster.local:8001"
initialize = {
    "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize",
    "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {},
               "clientInfo": {"name": "deploy-probe", "version": "1"}},
}
probe_call = {
    "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {"name": "studio_get_board", "arguments": {"board_id": "x" * (256 * 1024)}},
}
results = []
with httpx.Client(base_url=base, trust_env=False, timeout=5,
                  headers={"Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"}) as client:
    for label, path, body in (("MCP initialize", "/mcp", initialize),
                              ("MCP upload initialize", "/mcp/upload", initialize),
                              ("MCP over 256 KiB", "/mcp", probe_call)):
        try:
            response = client.post(path, json=body)
            status = response.status_code
            passed = status == 401 and response.json().get("error", {}).get("code") == "auth.required"
        except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, AttributeError) as error:
            status, passed = type(error).__name__, False
        results.append(passed)
        print("PASS" if passed else "FAIL", label, status)
print("PASS" if all(results) else "FAIL", "OP964 anonymous MCP")
raise SystemExit(0 if all(results) else 1)
PY
)

Signed-in feature use and phone playback have separate evidence. The existing imports can be reviewed privately but are permanently ineligible for go-live. A new Studio-built run and a signed-in person are required for the first real release package. See OP944 for phone playback.

docs.title: Roll back while keeping the third schema
docs.text:
Use a corrective GitOps PR that restores all six workload pins to the 393fe1d Python and web pair, including the API's listener, and restores the old API/worker build revision and worker image provenance. Recover the workload pins from the OP961/Cilium-fixed tree. Keep the new migration and registration Jobs and their health checks Complete. The old migration image cannot resolve the newer Alembic head. Review the corrective PR's release check so it verifies the restored workload pair separately from the retained Job digest. Keep the store, database, projections and existing worker IDs. Reconcile in dependency order and use the read-only compare phase against a new baseline. Repeat the restored pod, old LAN, Gatus and imported playback checks.

Before rollback, stop submissions, drain all three lanes and review any held run. Check for newer writes before restoring writer access. The old build may serve the original imports and their media at the new schema. Prefer a forward fix as soon as people have used the new features.

Revision Rollback with the upgraded schema retained 0008 Unused feedback tables and a null story reference are safe. Existing notes and iteration records stay stored but disappear from the old UI. An active feedback iteration won't be frozen into a run enqueued by the old app. Answering runs can carry answers, which the old run schema rejects. Keep affected drafts and runs out of the old editing and build flow. A full return to that flow requires no new feedback-linked work. 0009 The old app can still read stories.published. It ignores release packages, iteration-clear events and publications. New publication rows won't appear in the old column's status or filters, and the old approval path lacks the package checks. Restore old publishing and edit semantics only before new release or feedback state has been written. Preserve all package copies and records. 0010 Staged text and versions stay in the database but are unavailable in the old app. Once a storyboard is applied, its draft_application.archive_version_id stamp is outside the old board schema. Keep affected drafts out of old editing and enqueue. A full writer rollback requires no archive applies or new archive work to continue. 0011 The seeded grants and token rows survive rollback. The old API ignores lane bindings even after the new schema is in place. Keep all submissions stopped until the lane-aware app is restored. The old pin can cover private import reads in the meantime. 0012 Package, publication and archive integrity constraints remain in place. The old build uses none of those tables. Their records retain the 0009/0010 visibility and writer restrictions above. No revision (Studio PR 128) The new build's format recipe schema accepts matte_slots. A format version saved with it by the new build is outside the old build's recipe schema, so the old build would likely refuse any story or run pinned to that version. Count such versions below before an image rollback; if any exist, fix forward.

Keep any data written by the new build. An image rollback never calls alembic downgrade and never rewrites a legacy published flag to imitate a new publication record.

Count what the new build has written before deciding on an image rollback. compare covers only the import counts and the store totals. This read-only block counts every kind of row and field that only the new build writes. All zero means an image rollback strands nothing; anything else is listed by name, and the table above says what the old build does with it.

(
  set -uo pipefail
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/studio-api -c api -- python -I -B - <<'PY'
import os
import sys

import psycopg

QUERIES = {
    "run candidates": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.run_candidates",
    "feedback notes": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.candidate_feedback",
    "feedback iterations": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.feedback_iterations",
    "iteration clears": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.feedback_iteration_clears",
    "stories with an active iteration": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.stories WHERE feedback_iteration_id IS NOT NULL",
    "release packages": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.release_packages",
    "publications": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.publications",
    "archive records": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.archive_records",
    "archive versions": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.archive_versions",
    "runs with feedback answers": "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.runs WHERE document ? 'answers'",
    "boards stamped from the archive":
        "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.boards WHERE document::text LIKE '%\"archive_version_id\"%'",
    "format versions with matte slots":
        "SELECT count(*) FROM studio.format_versions WHERE recipe::text LIKE '%\"matte_slots\"%'",
}
written = 0
with psycopg.connect(os.environ["STUDIO_DATABASE_URL"]) as conn:
    conn.read_only = True
    for label, query in QUERIES.items():
        try:
            count = conn.execute(query).fetchone()[0]
        except psycopg.Error as error:
            print(f"FAIL {label}: {type(error).__name__}")
            conn.rollback()
            written = -1
            continue
        print(f"{'PASS' if count == 0 else 'NOTE'} {label}: {count}")
        if count and written >= 0:
            written += count
if written < 0:
    print("FAIL some counts could not be read; do not conclude anything from this block")
    sys.exit(2)
print("PASS nothing written by the new build" if written == 0
      else "NOTE the new build has written data: see the rollback table before an image rollback")
sys.exit(0 if written == 0 else 1)
PY
)

The block exits 0 only when every count is zero, 1 when the new build has written something (a result, not an error), and 2 when a count could not be read. Column and table names are those of the schema at the pinned build; if a count fails after a later pin, correct the query before trusting the block.

docs.title: OP437 one API pod recovery
docs.text:
Proven (2026-11-25), with two changes. Run once against the third pin, 11:35:27Z to 11:41:01Z: 32 checks passed and none failed. All 300 ingress samples answered 401 as expected, with no 502 and no transport error, while studio-api-5ccf9956c6-2cw6s was deleted and its replacement became Ready on another node. The data probe was unchanged on the replacement, and the surviving API pod and the three workers kept their identities and restart counts. Changed: the coordinator's pod has no LAN route, so each request was made from an MCP pod through the internal ingress Service, with the public host name and the certificate verified; this covers the ingress-to-pod path and not the LAN-to-ingress hop. One check was added: the pod chosen for deletion carries the drain on both containers. Still open: the baseline held no saved selection and no queued snapshot, so that preservation case is proven in the source tests only. Story 437, comments 10077 and 10078.

As written. The saga coordinator runs this check once from a LAN client with existing Studio read access to Kubernetes and authority to delete a single API pod. Use a quiet window without Studio submissions or draft or selection edits. The baseline refuses active runs or media jobs and requires any queued work to be in an already-paused lane. Record the number of selections and queued snapshots in the baseline. A zero count leaves that installed preservation case open. Do not create test records or change queue controls to fill it.

Save the OP959 read-only data probe as a local Bash file. The recovery modes read the same rows and store totals. They also fingerprint selections, verify queued snapshot hashes and read and hash both imported proxies through the API container's store mount. The comparison executes on the replacement API pod. The signed-out ingress requests establish route availability and access boundaries. Source integration tests cover authenticated draft CRUD and ranged media. This installed check cannot establish node-loss recovery, PostgreSQL failover, loss of talosw01 (simulated in the source tests), or completion of a real media job.

Declare the activity first and end it with the returned ID after the block, including after a failure. Save that ID as activity_id in your shell.

agent-run declare-activity start 'OP437 Studio API pod replacement' --scope ai,studio-api --ttl 30m

Save the block below as a Bash file and pass the path to the data probe as its first argument. It requires two Ready API, web and MCP replicas on distinct nodes per Deployment and one available replica per budget. A direct pod deletion bypasses PDB enforcement, so the block rechecks both API pods immediately before deleting the named target. Keep the printed evidence and the sample file. The loop samples at most one request per second for 300 requests, starting before deletion, with no HTTP retries. At least one expected response must arrive after the replacement Ready check. Keep every response in the log. Any unexpected status, any transport error, or any 502 fails the check. The surviving API pod's two containers and the three workers must retain their recorded restart counts and pod identities throughout the drill. On any refusal or failed check, record it and stop without a second deletion.

Changed (2026-11-25): the drain is installed, so the tolerance is zero. The third deployment pin (story 964, comment 10061) added an 8-second preStop sleep to the API container and its listener. A deleted pod keeps serving while the ingress drops its endpoint, so no request should fail, and tolerated_502s is 0 below. Before the delete, confirm the pod chosen for deletion carries the sleep on both containers. For a pod from before that pin, the earlier tolerance applies instead: at most two 502 answers within five seconds of the delete request, because the ingress can briefly route to the terminating endpoint.

(
  set -uo pipefail
  data_probe=${1:?Pass the OP959 data probe file}
  [[ -r $data_probe ]] || { printf 'FAIL data probe file is unreadable\n' >&2; exit 1; }
  evidence=$(mktemp -d "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:?}/studio-op437.XXXXXX") || exit 1
  base=https://studio.haynesops.com
  k=(kubectl -n ai --request-timeout=15s)
  workers=(studio-worker studio-voice-worker studio-image-worker)
  worker_pods=()
  routes=(/v1/me /v1/productions /v1/queue/lanes)
  samples=300
  tolerated_502s=0
  failed=0
  sampler=
  trap 'if [[ -n $sampler ]]; then kill "$sampler" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "$sampler" 2>/dev/null || true; fi' EXIT
  trap 'exit 130' INT TERM

  check() {
    local label=$1
    shift
    if "$@"; then
      printf 'PASS %s\n' "$label"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$label" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  }
  gate() {
    if (( failed )); then
      printf 'FAIL OP437 API recovery (evidence %s)\n' "$evidence" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  }
  ready_pods() {
    "${k[@]}" get pods -l "app.kubernetes.io/name=$1" -o json | jq -ce '
      [.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)
       | select(any(.status.conditions[]?; .type == "Ready" and .status == "True"))
       | {name: .metadata.name, uid: .metadata.uid, node: .spec.nodeName,
          containers: [.status.containerStatuses[]? | select(.ready) | .name]}]
      | sort_by(.name) | select(all(.[]; .node != null and .node != ""))'
  }
  ready_pair() {
    ready_pods "$1" | jq -ce 'select(length == 2 and (map(.node) | unique | length == 2))'
  }
  worker_placement() {
    local pods name
    pods=$(ready_pods "$1" | jq -ce --arg worker "$1" '
      select(length == 1 and (.[0].node == "talosw01") == ($worker == "studio-worker"))') || return 1
    name=$(jq -er '.[0].name' <<<"$pods") || return 1
    worker_pods+=("$name")
    printf '%s\n' "$pods"
  }
  record_restarts() {
    local counts
    counts=$("${k[@]}" get pod "$survivor" "${worker_pods[@]}" -o json | jq -ce --arg survivor "$survivor" '
      [.items[] | {pod: .metadata.name, uid: .metadata.uid,
        containers: ([.status.containerStatuses[]? | {name, restarts: .restartCount}] | sort_by(.name))}]
      | sort_by(.pod)
      | select(length == 4 and all(.[];
          (.uid | type == "string" and length > 0)
          and (.containers | map(.name)) == (if .pod == $survivor then ["api", "media-worker-routes"] else ["worker"] end)
          and all(.containers[]; (.restarts | type) == "number")))') || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$counts" | tee "$1"
  }
  unchanged_restarts() {
    record_restarts "$evidence/restarts-after.json" &&
      diff -u "$evidence/restarts-before.json" "$evidence/restarts-after.json"
  }
  deployment_ready() {
    "${k[@]}" get "deploy/$1" -o json | jq -e --argjson replicas "$2" '
      .status.observedGeneration == .metadata.generation and .spec.replicas == $replicas
      and .status.readyReplicas == $replicas and .status.updatedReplicas == $replicas' >/dev/null
  }
  budget_ready() {
    "${k[@]}" get "pdb/$1" -o json | jq -e '
      .status.observedGeneration == .metadata.generation and .spec.minAvailable == 1
      and .status.currentHealthy == 2 and .status.disruptionsAllowed >= 1' >/dev/null
  }
  listener_ready() {
    jq -e 'all(.[]; (.containers | index("api")) != null
                    and (.containers | index("media-worker-routes")) != null)' <<<"$1" >/dev/null
  }
  status() {
    local expected=$1 route=$2 actual observed rc=0
    actual=$(curl --disable --silent --show-error --max-time 3 --output /dev/null \
                  --write-out '%{http_code}' "$base$route") || rc=$?
    observed=$(date -u '+%s%3N %FT%TZ') || return 1
    printf '%s %s HTTP %s expected %s curl %s\n' "$observed" "$route" "${actual:-000}" "$expected" "$rc" &&
      [[ $rc == 0 && $actual == "$expected" ]]
  }
  signed_out() {
    local route rc=0
    status 200 / || rc=1
    for route in "${routes[@]}" /v1/formats \
      /v1/runs/run_01M7ZHNZJ2PWA8XR8K7KKWP17V/delivery \
      /v1/runs/run_01M7C5CJA7XKBCRPM0ZRP2P5RS/delivery \
      /v1/media/63dbb1e26287360ed6c4a0422dbdbfa250ad981c74e9719133d4dfe72d809d1b \
      /v1/media/0212a7de9d6b7816c4c4d3c98bfd6d8e80fc112163944152e399b3e980a6748d; do
      status 401 "$route" || rc=1
    done
    for route in /healthz /readyz /mcp /internal/v1/work/claim; do
      status 404 "$route" || rc=1
    done
    return "$rc"
  }
  first_sample() {
    status 401 /v1/me | tee "$evidence/ingress.log"
  }
  sample() {
    local i
    for ((i=1; i<samples; ++i)); do
      sleep 1 || return 1
      status 401 "${routes[i % ${#routes[@]}]}" || true
    done
  }
  verify_ingress_samples() {
    awk -v samples="$samples" -v deleted="$delete_requested_at_ms" -v ready="$ready_at_ms" \
        -v tolerance="$tolerated_502s" '
      NF != 9 || $1 !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || $4 != "HTTP" || $5 !~ /^[0-9][0-9][0-9]$/ ||
      $6 != "expected" || $7 != 401 || $8 != "curl" || $9 !~ /^[0-9]+$/ { invalid++; next }
      {
        count++
        if ($9 == 0 && $5 == 401) {
          if ($1 > ready) covered=1
        } else if ($9 == 0 && $5 == 502 && $1 >= deleted && $1 - deleted <= 5000) {
          window_502++
        } else {
          unexpected++
        }
      }
      END {
        printf "ingress samples=%d/%d window_502=%d tolerance=%d unexpected=%d invalid=%d after_ready=%d\n",
          count, samples, window_502, tolerance, unexpected, invalid, covered
        exit !(count == samples && window_502 <= tolerance && !unexpected && !invalid && covered)
      }' "$evidence/ingress.log"
  }
  api_before=
  read_api_pair() {
    api_before=$(ready_pair studio-api) && printf '%s\n' "$api_before"
  }
  pod_name() {
    jq -er --argjson i "$1" '.[$i].name' <<<"$api_before"
  }
  delete_one() {
    local current
    current=$(ready_pair studio-api) && [[ $current == "$api_before" ]] &&
      budget_ready studio-api &&
      delete_requested_at_ms=$(date -u +%s%3N) &&
      printf '%s\n' "$delete_requested_at_ms" >"$evidence/delete-start-ms" &&
      "${k[@]}" delete pod "$victim" --wait=false
  }
  replacement=
  find_replacement() {
    local after candidate deadline=$((SECONDS + 150))
    while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
      after=$(ready_pods studio-api) || return 1
      if candidate=$(jq -er --argjson before "$api_before" '
        select(length == 2 and (map(.node) | unique | length == 2))
        | select(any(.[]; .uid == $before[1].uid and .node == $before[1].node))
        | .[] | select(.uid != $before[0].uid and .uid != $before[1].uid)
        | .name' <<<"$after") && listener_ready "$after"; then
        replacement=$candidate
        printf '%s\n' "$after"
        return 0
      fi
      sleep 2
    done
    printf 'API replacement did not become Ready with both listeners within 150s\n' >&2
    return 1
  }
  idle_claims_since() {
    local count
    count=$("${k[@]}" logs "deploy/$1" -c worker --since-time="$2" |
      awk '/\/work\/claim "HTTP\/1\.1 204/ {n++} END {print n+0}') &&
      printf '%s idle claims=%s\n' "$1" "$count" &&
      (( count > 0 ))
  }

  printf 'Evidence directory %s\n' "$evidence"
  for app in studio-api studio-mcp studio-web; do
    check "$app deployment replicas" deployment_ready "$app" 2
    check "$app PDB" budget_ready "$app"
  done
  check 'API placements and identities' read_api_pair
  check 'MCP placements' ready_pair studio-mcp
  check 'web placements' ready_pair studio-web
  check 'both API listeners Ready' listener_ready "$api_before"
  for worker in "${workers[@]}"; do
    check "$worker deployment replica" deployment_ready "$worker" 1
    check "$worker placement" worker_placement "$worker"
  done
  check 'signed-out ingress routes before deletion' signed_out
  gate
  victim=$(pod_name 0) && survivor=$(pod_name 1) || exit 1
  check 'imported proxies, selections and queue baseline' timeout 45s bash "$data_probe" recovery-baseline \
    "$evidence/baseline.json" "pod/$survivor"
  check 'survivor and worker restart counts before deletion' record_restarts "$evidence/restarts-before.json"
  check 'continuity sample before deletion' first_sample
  gate
  sample >>"$evidence/ingress.log" &
  sampler=$!
  check "delete pod/$victim once" delete_one
  gate
  check 'deleted pod is gone' kubectl -n ai wait --for=delete "pod/$victim" --timeout=90s
  check 'replacement and survivor Ready on different nodes with both listeners' find_replacement
  read -r ready_at_ms ready_at < <(date -u '+%s%3N %FT%TZ') || exit 1
  if [[ -n $replacement ]]; then
    check 'unchanged data probe on replacement' timeout 45s bash "$data_probe" recovery-compare \
      "$evidence/baseline.json" "pod/$replacement"
  else
    check 'unchanged data probe requires a replacement' false
  fi
  check 'ingress sampler completed' wait "$sampler"
  sampler=
  check 'ingress continuity counts and sample after replacement readiness' verify_ingress_samples
  check 'signed-out ingress routes after replacement' signed_out
  sleep 10  # Two normal worker claim intervals after the replacement Ready timestamp.
  for worker in "${workers[@]}"; do
    check "$worker claims after replacement" idle_claims_since "$worker" "$ready_at"
  done
  check 'survivor and worker restart counts unchanged' unchanged_restarts
  gate
  printf 'PASS OP437 API recovery (evidence %s)\n' "$evidence"
)

agent-run declare-activity end "${activity_id:?Set this to the ID printed by the start command}"

docs.title: Follow-ups
docs.text:
Independent review of PR 5110 recorded four follow-ups:

  • A run submitted during a rollout can fail terminally with work.revision_mismatch when the API and claiming worker are on different Studio revisions. Keep submissions closed through postflight.
  • A browser can get HTML from one web revision and an asset 404 from the other while both revisions share the Service, leaving the Editor blank until reload.
  • The read-only command allowlist accepts calls to newly added local helpers without inspecting them.
  • Some release guards lack negative tests, including checks for receipt profiles, rollback prerequisites, encoder agreement and ingress validation.

docs.title: Preflight and merge
docs.text:
Under CR-63, the reviewed GitOps merge triggers the rollout. The queue gate includes any queued cutout.

docs.title: Roll back the pins through a reviewed PR
docs.text:
Expected. The workload rollback remains unexercised on the installed pin.

Keep submissions closed until active and held work settles. Start the revert from current Ops main. Restore release.yaml, the API, MCP, web, run, voice and image Deployment pins, all four digest-named Job manifests and their Job health-check names in ks.yaml. Apply the reverse of the original pin's patch only, so later unrelated changes remain in place. In this block FIFTH_PIN_OPS_REVISION is the original reviewed fifth-pin squash merge. If a retry added an -rN suffix, first remove that suffix from the Job name in migration/job.yaml and its matching health check in ks.yaml. Then apply this block to restore all four fourth-pin Job names.

set -o pipefail
studio=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio
git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv "${FIFTH_PIN_OPS_REVISION:?}^1" "$FIFTH_PIN_OPS_REVISION" -- \
  "$studio"/{release.yaml,ks.yaml} "$studio"/app/{api,mcp,web}.yaml \
  "$studio"/{worker/deployment,migration/job,worker-registration/job}.yaml \
  "$studio"/media-workers/{image,voice}.yaml "$studio"/media-worker-registration/{image,voice}-job.yaml |
  git apply --reverse

The fourth pin already serves schema 0013. Its migration Job will read back that head if Flux needs to recreate the Job. The render files, policy stages and listener configuration carry forward.

From the clean reviewed revert head, set MERGED_OPS_REVISION to the currently deployed fifth-pin merge, including a retry if applicable. Set new private STUDIO_OP978_RECEIPT and STUDIO_OP978_BASELINE paths.

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh op978 rollback-preflight ||
   ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh op978 admit-merge rollback; then
  printf 'FAIL rollback preflight, hold the merge\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

After the revert merges, return to the selected fifth-pin checkout. Keep MERGED_OPS_REVISION set and set ROLLBACK_OPS_REVISION to the full revert merge SHA. Set STUDIO_OP978_ROLLBACK_BASELINE to the rollback preflight snapshot. Run the same wait block and then compare. It verifies the restored workloads, schema, data and store. Record Gatus before reopening submissions.

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh op978 compare; then
  printf 'FAIL rollback read-back, keep submissions closed\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi
