docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
Under provisional coordinator ruling CR-63, merging the reviewed PR is the only action that changes the cluster. Flux receives a GitHub push event and polls Git every 30 minutes. The stages start automatically when the new artifact arrives.

Use Bash with GNU coreutils, jq, yq, Python 3.12 with PyYAML and Flux CLI 2.10. Every block can run from a session pod. Its ingress reads use kubectl exec -i into studio-mcp and connect to traefik-internal.network.svc.cluster.local:443 with studio.haynesops.com as TLS SNI and HTTP Host. The probe verifies the certificate and sends anonymous GET requests for / and /v1/me. Work from the clean reviewed PR head incorporating current Ops main. Set STUDIO_OP967_RECEIPT and STUDIO_OP967_BASELINE to new paths in a private directory outside the checkout. Keep submissions closed and offline render idle through postflight. The render pod restarts on merge. Check that each API surge replica has a free eligible node. Third pin runbook

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh preflight ||
   ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh admit-merge; then
  printf 'FAIL release preflight, hold the merge\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

The merge gate fetches Ops main and checks the reviewed commit and tree, baseline hash, predecessor Job archive digest and every required PASS. Merge within 60 minutes of starting preflight. Take a fresh preflight if the PR head changes or the receipt expires. Save the receipt, baseline and four predecessor Job logs in ${STUDIO_OP967_RECEIPT}.jobs for evidence and a possible retry. Flux prunes those Jobs and pod logs. The baseline hashes the database rows and store files and modification times.

Preflight checks the old workloads, three Ready PostgreSQL instances, LAN status and worker dependencies. It requires zero queued, running or held Studio jobs, Wan with both active jobs null, an empty shared ComfyUI queue, and at most 10% CPU and 25% memory on talosw01. The offline app must measure at most 250m CPU and run only its idle PID 1 apart from the probe, with a complete PyAV 18.1.0 venv.

docs.title: Wait for automatic deployment
docs.text:
Check out the exact Ops merge and set MERGED_OPS_REVISION to its full SHA. The script reads Flux and fetches main before each comparison. It checks that the Git source, the rendered Studio stage definitions and the trees and rendered manifests at their paths match the selected merge. An unrelated descendant passes. A rewire, a changed stage input or an observed revision missing after the fetch fails with its revision. Each live stage at the selected pin must match every reviewed spec field. The sole allowed unlisted Flux v1 API default is force: false. A spec mismatch names the field. The inventory and each stage must report Ready for the current generation and a matching applied revision. An attempted revision alone is pending. After merge the audit uses the selected SHA and live state.

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh wait; then
  printf 'FAIL automatic Flux rollout, keep submissions closed\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

Report failed pickup if the artifact still precedes the merge at 35 minutes. After observing pickup, allow up to 35 minutes for stage readiness. While pending, the script samples the API pods and reads LAN status. It checks the two image pairs as workloads advance and requires a successful migration audit before treating any advanced workload as valid.

Flux stage Added or changed automatically on merge Pruned automatically AI inventory Updates migration and the existing registration gates. studio-render Adds the pinned render environment ConfigMap and updates the HelmRelease. Recreate rolls the offline pod once at 20 CPUs. studio-migration Creates the digest-named 0013 migration Job. Third-pin migration Job and pod logs. studio Rolls API replicas, web and MCP. Both API generations use the same port-8002 listener configuration. studio-worker-registration Creates the new run registration Job. Third-pin run registration Job and pod logs. studio-worker Replaces the run worker pod. studio-media-worker-registration Creates the new voice and image registration Jobs. Third-pin voice and image registration Jobs and pod logs. studio-media-workers Replaces the voice and image worker pods.

Offline render and migration can start in parallel. API, web and MCP wait for the successful migration. The run worker waits for the API stage, its registration and the Helm-ready render worker. Voice and image wait for the API stage and their registrations. The render worker builds a new venv from the exact lock export and keeps older completed Python environments on the share. Cleanup remains unwritten. Its forwarding PID 1 reaps children and forwards termination to the startup process group.

docs.title: Migrate while the third pin serves
docs.text:
0013_matte_jobs widens the three lane checks on media_job_lanes, queue_lane_events and worker_lane_grants, and the kind, lane and board/story checks on media_jobs. It seeds the matte FIFO and adds matte_releases SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with column-scoped runtime UPDATE permission. The constraint changes and writes commit together. The migration locks grants, media lanes, pause events and media jobs in that order. PostgreSQL's 500 ms timeout applies per lock acquisition. The grant lock can queue and the other three prelocks use NOWAIT. A readiness or worker-authentication read queued behind the migration can wait for the grant lock budget plus DDL and commit, about 10 ms at the installed table sizes. The independent fixture measured a 502 ms grant read when the holder released just before timeout. The guarantee covers lock acquisition. API readiness and worker requests can take longer. A lock timeout rolls the upgrade back to 0012_release_constraints and the Job retries within its two-retry, 300-second budget. Keep sampling the old pods while the Job runs. Record when the active window is too short to sample.

Source verified. The 80975a9 readiness probe selects existing columns and tables with LIMIT 0. It doesn't require an exact Alembic revision. Old claims and pause reads use explicit run, voice and image lanes. Old media inserts and updates use named columns, and the release counter's server default covers old inserts. The widened predicates still admit the original job kinds and their original board/story associations. Old catalog, release and archive queries use the same columns and rows. The compatibility is for the original workloads. The old job provenance parser cannot display a matte job document, and the matte lane is absent from its queue controls. Retain those records for a forward recovery. Old readiness · Old queue SQL · Old job parser

Flux owns the migration and registration Jobs. The studio apply stage depends on the migration Kustomization and its successful digest-named Job. The rollout keeps maxUnavailable: 0 on the API.

The migration Job verifies the TLS login before upgrading and reports its committed head. Each migration and registration read identifies the current Job UID, requires exactly one succeeded pod owned by that Job and reads the last line starting with { from its successful container. For a registration the last JSON result identifies the worker and the earlier matching audit line confirms its status. An older failed pod is normal after a retry. A Complete Job with zero or multiple succeeded pods fails the audit.

docs.title: Retry a terminal migration with a new PR
docs.text:
Expected. The fourth-pin rollout completed on the first attempt.

Keep submissions closed. From current Ops main, change only these two files under kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio/. In migration/job.yaml, increment the terminal Job name to its next -rN suffix, starting at -r1. In ks.yaml, update the studio-migration Job health check to the same name. Keep the image and Job spec. Code or configuration recovery requires a separate review.

On the clean reviewed retry head, set STUDIO_OP967_FAILED_OPS_REVISION and STUDIO_OP967_PREVIOUS_RECEIPT to the failed Ops merge and its receipt. Use new private receipt and baseline paths.

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh retry-preflight ||
   ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh admit-merge retry; then
  printf 'FAIL retry preflight, hold the merge\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

The retry preflight checks for a Failed Job with zero active pods. It verifies the saved predecessor Job archive, the original baseline and fresh hashes. It requires Ready third-pin workloads and endpoints. Idle render may already be on PyAV 18.1.1. All other preflight checks apply.

  • Complete 0012. The primary reports 0012_release_constraints, all six original constraint definitions and both 0012 foreign keys, with the release column absent. Use the replacement Job above to apply 0013 and read it back.
  • Committed 0013. The primary reports 0013_matte_jobs, all six exact widened check definitions, both 0012 foreign keys, the SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 release column and its UPDATE grant to studio_app, and a positive matte FIFO position. The replacement Job reads back the already committed head. The workload revert below is also available.

The catalogue uses PostgreSQL 16's pg_get_constraintdef and reads the CNPG primary over its peer socket in a read-only transaction. A different catalogue state fails preflight. After the retry PR merges, use its exact merge with wait and postflight and the retry baseline.

docs.title: Serving while matte activation is pending
docs.text:
The API readiness probe requires the matte FIFO row seeded by 0013. The API and MCP start with their existing configuration, and the run, voice and image workers claim using their own lanes and existing bearer tokens. The matting profile and sidecar client are loaded only by studio-worker --lane matte. Port 8002 keeps the existing five POST routes for voice and image; only those pods use that listener. The API's worker authentication looks up a single presented token and grant per request. API readiness and startup · MCP startup · Worker startup · Worker authentication

The pinned API has no submission gate tied to matte worker registration. A valid matte request returns HTTP 202 and waits queued until a registered matte worker claims it. The queue pause controls claiming and still accepts submissions. Keep matte submissions closed operationally until story 970 activates the worker. Submit handler · Lane authorization

docs.title: Carried to story 970
docs.text:
• P2. A queued cutout can keep image submission disabled when following Generate asset from the same view. Close job view restores submission. A queued matte job also fails postflight and requires a recorded matte pause before the rollback snapshot can proceed.
  • P3. Pin the local helper entry points permitted by the read-only command scanner and inspect their payloads.
  • P3. Compare the full offline requirements list with the pinned Studio export in required CI.
  • P3. Add tests that fail when each independent release-phase and schema guard is removed, including the all-stale encoder case.

Story 970 · Independent review

docs.title: Postflight
docs.text:
Run from the selected merge with STUDIO_OP967_BASELINE set. The script reads every Flux stage, the migration and three registration Job audits, workloads, endpoints, engines, encoders, LAN and the data snapshot. The snapshot requires three existing grants, no matte grant, no queued, running or held jobs in the matte queue, idle existing lanes and unchanged archives. It rechecks Flux before the listener POST probes, which fail validation or authorization before a write. Keep submissions closed through verification.

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh postflight; then
  printf 'FAIL release verification, keep submissions closed\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

Use verify for the same audits and status probes with an optional baseline.

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh verify; then
  printf 'FAIL release verification\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

The probe reports av.__version__ and av.library_versions from both API pods, the run, voice and image workers and the offline render venv. It requires 18.1.1 and identical bundled library versions. Record the actual values and the data comparisons on both 966 and 967 from the Codex postflight session. This proof reads the installed encoders and archived data without rebuilding deliveries or runs.

The listener probes require anonymous claim to return 401, malformed or unknown-lane claims to return 422, and a known other lane (including matte) or disallowed settle_only to return 403. The port-8002 listener refuses /resume. The API refuses forwarded media requests that default to the run lane. The run worker's malformed /resume reaches API validation. Record engine reachability and Gatus before opening run, voice and image submissions. Gatus check

The static check permits kubectl get, logs, wait, and top with the reviewed read flags. Its named kubectl exec probes read PostgreSQL and the store, dependency and ingress status, the idle render process, encoder versions and worker engines. Flux renders local inputs with flux build kustomization --dry-run --in-memory-build. Direct HTTP reads use GET or HEAD. The named listener module sends only POSTs expected to fail at the listener, authentication, lane authorization or payload validation.

docs.title: Roll back workloads through a reviewed PR
docs.text:
Expected. The fourth-pin rollout completed without a workload rollback.

Keep submissions closed until active and held work settles. The snapshot allows queued matte jobs with a recorded matte pause and preserves any matte job and pause records. Keep schema 0013. Old migration images cannot resolve it.

Base a workloads-only revert on current Ops main. Under kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio/, use the verified third-pin manifests.

On the reviewed revert head, set MERGED_OPS_REVISION to the fourth-pin merge and set new private STUDIO_OP967_RECEIPT and STUDIO_OP967_BASELINE paths. The preflight checks the live Flux sequence, the idle offline environment and ingress. It checks the successful Job's log or, for a terminal Job, verifies the complete 0013 catalogue on the primary. It takes the data snapshot from a Ready API pod on either verified image, so it works during a stalled turnover.

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh rollback-preflight ||
   ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh admit-merge rollback; then

After the revert merges, return to the fourth-pin checkout. Set ROLLBACK_OPS_REVISION to the full revert merge SHA and set STUDIO_OP967_ROLLBACK_BASELINE to the revert preflight's snapshot. Run the same wait block, then compare the old images, endpoints, engine reachability and retained schema and data.

if ! bash scripts/studio-release/op967.sh compare; then
  printf 'FAIL rollback read-back, keep submissions closed\n' >&2

fi

Record the Gatus result before reopening the original lanes. A forward fix is needed to resume matte submissions and job detail.

docs.title: Studio matte worker policy
docs.text:
Story 970, part A adds the independent Flux stage ai/studio-matte-policy. It owns NetworkPolicy/ai/studio-matte-worker, which selects app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-matte-worker. It denies ingress and permits only DNS to CoreDNS in kube-system on TCP and UDP 53 and TCP 8002 to studio-api pods in ai. The parked Deployment template uses that label.

The installed Flux kustomize-controller v1.10.2 checks the live object's metadata during inventory pruning. The policy's kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/prune: disabled annotation excludes it from deletion when it drops out of the stage's render. Flux prune call · Deletion exclusions · Live object check · Annotation matching

If the parent inventory prunes the stage, deletionPolicy: Orphan skips the stage's resource deletion at finalization. The existing ai namespace has its own prune exclusion. Orphan value · Finalizer decision · Namespace manifest

docs.title: Read back the installation (Expected)
docs.text:
Run from a clean checkout of the merged Ops commit after Flux pickup and before the worker activation PR. Set MERGED_OPS_REVISION to that commit's full SHA. The block uses kubectl, jq, Flux CLI and Python with PyYAML. Capture the revision, audit output and Cilium watcher line if present.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  stage=$(kubectl -n ai get kustomization studio-matte-policy -o json)
  policy=$(kubectl -n ai get networkpolicy studio-matte-worker -o json)
  pods=$(kubectl get pods -A -l app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-matte-worker -o json)
  printf '%s\n' "$stage" "$policy" "$pods" | jq -s . |
    python3 -B scripts/tests/studio-release/check.py --audit-matte-policy "$MERGED_OPS_REVISION"

  namespaces=$(kubectl get networkpolicy -A --field-selector metadata.name=studio-matte-worker -o json |
    jq -c '[.items[].metadata.namespace]')
  agent=$(kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=cilium --field-selector spec.nodeName=talosw01 -o json |
    jq -er '.items | if length == 1 then .[0].metadata.name else error("expected one Cilium pod on talosw01") end')
  created=$(jq -er '.metadata.creationTimestamp' <<< "$policy")
  watcher=$(kubectl -n kube-system logs "$agent" -c cilium-agent --since-time="$created" --timestamps |
    awk '/NetworkPolicy successfully added/ && /(^| )k8sNetworkPolicyName=studio-matte-worker( |$)/')
  if [[ $namespaces == '["ai"]' && -n $watcher ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$watcher"
  else
    printf '%s\n' 'No unambiguous Cilium watcher receipt in the available logs.'
  fi
)

The audit compares every field in the policy spec, treats Kubernetes' omitted empty ingress list as empty, checks Flux ownership and both retention controls, and verifies the stage's current generation is Ready at the merge SHA with only this policy in inventory. The pod list includes terminating pods.

On Cilium v1.20.5, the watcher log confirms the agent parsed and queued the policy for import. The policy repository logs its completed upsert at debug level, which is disabled in the installed configuration. Kubernetes NetworkPolicy exposes no policy status, and there is no matte CiliumEndpoint to inspect before activation. Record the watcher receipt separately from enforcement. Part B must prove the expected denial from inside the matte pod before requesting its grant and keep checking it. Watcher · Importer queue · Repository upsert

docs.title: Deliberate removal (Expected)
docs.text:
1. Ensure the matte workload can no longer create pods. Read the all-namespace selector above and record zero pods, including terminating pods. In the first PR keep the policy and stage declared, remove the prune annotation, set the stage's deletion policy to MirrorPrune with prune: true, and update the guard expectations for that transition. After Flux applies it, read back the absence of the annotation, the stage's deletion policy, and zero pods again.
  2. In a second PR remove the stage and policy source and retire the guard for the policy. Confirm Flux deleted both the stage and NetworkPolicy.

docs.title: Stage Studio still matting
docs.text:
CR-33 selects BiRefNet Lite FP32 on ONNX Runtime CPU. The baseline and CPU-arena retest ran on 2026-11-25. CR-43 stages the new serving profile, with the CPU arena off, in a fresh immutable allocation. Flux owns the targeted policies and provisioner ConfigMap. The Jobs, worker sidecar and render CPU split stay staged. Launch each Job individually after its checks pass. OP459

OP459 authorizes a one-shot exception to Flux ownership for these two unprivileged Job objects. The saga coordinator runs the reviewed Git templates and waits at each health gate. Flux owns the targeted policies and provisioner ConfigMap. The provisioner leaves a verified, create-only allocation on the private Studio share, and both Job objects expire after 24 hours. Matting profile · Studio deployment

docs.title: Pin and admit the release
docs.text:
1. Merge the Studio source PR. In its successful Studio images run on main, use Publish tested Studio images to read ghcr.io/thaynes43/haynes-studio-matting@sha256:<digest> for that full commit. The synthetic build smoke proves the runtime and artifact path.
  2. Set that full reference as data.image in release.yaml. It feeds the image and profile identity of both Jobs and the staged sidecar. The release check refuses both previously installed digests and reads the resource profile from the pinned image's OCI config. Both the rendered smoke and sidecar must match its request and limit. Merge the Ops PR after its check passes. Run the following blocks from that checked-out Ops revision.
  3. Reconcile and check the policy stage and the two existing workloads. The download pod can reach only DNS and HTTPS for huggingface.co and us.aws.cdn.hf.co. The smoke pod has no permitted traffic.
(
  set -euo pipefail
  flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  flux reconcile kustomization studio-matting-policy -n ai
  kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=ready kustomization/studio-matting-policy --timeout=2m
  kubectl -n ai get ciliumnetworkpolicy studio-matting-provision studio-matting-smoke
  kubectl -n ai get deploy studio-worker studio-render -o wide
)

docs.title: Provision and read back the weight
docs.text:
The image digest and serving settings are part of the immutable profile. Provision the same pinned graph into allocation matting-op459-birefnet-lite-v1-03 for the new image. Preserve both previous allocations. Check that the jobs root has at least 33 GiB free. The provisioner checks the 1 GiB budget and 32 GiB free reserve before and during writes. CR-33 accepts a 32-inode allocation here without an NFS free-inode reading. The Job writes as 1000:1000, with only data/studio/jobs mounted read-write. One atomic mkdir claims a new private allocation. The Job hashes the file read back from its staged bytes, syncs its profile, checksum and licence, then renames within the exclusively allocated directory. The published subpath is read-only in consumers. A failed allocation is retained and never reused.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  stage=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio/matting-pending
  provision=$(kustomize build "$stage/provision" | yq -e 'select(.kind == "Job")') || exit 1
  job=$(yq -e '.metadata.name' <<< "$provision") || exit 1
  config=$(yq -e '.spec.template.spec.volumes[] |
    select(.name == "config") | .configMap.name' <<< "$provision") || exit 1
  kubectl -n ai get "configmap/$config" -o name || exit 1
  kubectl -n ai exec deploy/studio-render -c app -- sh -ec '
    test -d /studio/jobs
    df -Pk /studio/jobs | awk "NR == 2 { print; if (\$4 >= 34603008) good = 1 } END { exit !good }"
  ' || exit 1
  kubectl -n ai create -f - <<< "$provision" || exit 1
  if ! kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=complete "job/$job" --timeout=6m; then
    kubectl -n ai get "job/$job" -o wide
    kubectl -n ai logs "job/$job"
    exit 1
  fi
  report=$(kubectl -n ai logs "job/$job" | tail -n 1)
  jq -es '
    length == 1 and (.[0] |
      .graph_bytes == 224005088 and
      .graph_sha256 == "5600024376f572a557870a5eb0afb1e5961636bef4e1e22132025467d0f03333" and
      (.profile_sha256 | test("^[0-9a-f]{64}$")))
  ' <<< "$report"
  allocation=$(yq '.data.allocation' "$stage/release/release.yaml")
  profile=$(jq -er '.profile_sha256' <<< "$report")
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/studio-render -c app -- python -B - "$allocation" "$profile" <<'PY'
from hashlib import file_digest
from pathlib import Path
import json
import sys

weights = Path("/studio/jobs") / sys.argv[1] / "weights"
with (weights / "model.onnx").open("rb") as graph:
    graph_hash = file_digest(graph, "sha256").hexdigest()
with (weights / "profile.json").open("rb") as manifest:
    profile_hash = file_digest(manifest, "sha256").hexdigest()
checks = {
    "graph size": (weights / "model.onnx").stat().st_size == 224005088,
    "graph hash": graph_hash == "5600024376f572a557870a5eb0afb1e5961636bef4e1e22132025467d0f03333",
    "profile hash": profile_hash == sys.argv[2] == (weights / "profile.sha256").read_text().strip(),
}
for name, passed in checks.items():
    print(f"{'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'} {name}")
print(json.dumps({"graph_sha256": graph_hash, "profile_sha256": profile_hash}))
raise SystemExit(not all(checks.values()))
PY
)

docs.title: Run the install smoke
docs.text:
Use an exclusive heavy-job window on talosw01. Confirm the window is clear of heavy render and Foley work and review node and render pod load before running the block. It records fresh readings and gates Job creation on Wan's /v1/ready reporting readiness and both video and Foley idle, and the image engine's queue being empty. Before 2026-11-25 14:30Z, the idle gates read only /health. Run studio-matting-smoke-03 once after the new pin's read-back. The Job uses plain studio-matting smoke with the serving profile. It requests 8 GiB and limits the container to 2 CPUs and 10 GiB. It has a 300 s deadline, no retries, no network, read-only root and weights, and a 256 MiB private scratch. It runs as 10001:10001. Capture phase peaks, post-request RSS, fixture hash matches and any failure logs.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  check_json() {
    local label=$1 predicate=$2
    shift 2
    if jq -es "$@" "length == 1 and (.[0] | ($predicate))" >/dev/null; then
      printf 'PASS %s\n' "$label"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$label" >&2
      return 1
    fi
  }
  read_endpoint() {
    local pod=$1 container=$2 url=$3
    kubectl -n ai exec "$pod" -c "$container" -- python -B -c '
import sys
from urllib.request import urlopen
with urlopen(sys.argv[1], timeout=5) as response:
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(response.read())
' "$url"
  }
  wan_idle() {
    read_endpoint deploy/wan-video api http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/ready |
      check_json 'Wan idle' '.ready == true and
        has("active_video_job") and .active_video_job == null and
        has("active_foley_job") and .active_foley_job == null'
  }
  stage=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio/matting-pending
  allocation=$(yq -e '.data.allocation' "$stage/release/release.yaml") || exit 1
  provision="studio-matting-provision-${allocation##*-}"
  kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=complete "job/$provision" --timeout=5s || exit 1
  profile=$(kubectl -n ai logs "job/$provision" | tail -n 1 |
    jq -ers 'select(length == 1) | .[0].profile_sha256 | select(test("^[0-9a-f]{64}$"))') || exit 1
  pin=$(yq -e '.data.image' "$stage/release/release.yaml") || exit 1
  kubectl top node talosw01 || exit 1
  kubectl -n ai top pod --containers -l app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-render || exit 1
  wan_idle || exit 1
  read_endpoint comfyui-0 app http://127.0.0.1:8188/queue |
    check_json 'Image engine queue empty' '.queue_running == [] and .queue_pending == []' || exit 1
  smoke=$(kustomize build "$stage/smoke") || exit 1
  job=$(yq -e '.metadata.name' <<< "$smoke") || exit 1
  kubectl -n ai create -f - <<< "$smoke" || exit 1
  if ! kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=complete "job/$job" --timeout=6m; then
    kubectl -n ai get "job/$job" -o wide
    kubectl -n ai logs "job/$job"
    exit 1
  fi
  kubectl -n ai get "job/$job" -o wide
  report=$(kubectl -n ai logs "job/$job" | tail -n 1)
  printf '%s\n' "$report"
  status=0
  check_json 'Pinned serving profile and image' '
    .pinned_profile_sha256 == $profile and .profile_sha256 == $profile and .image_digest == $digest
  ' --arg profile "$profile" --arg digest "${pin##*@}" <<< "$report" || status=1
  check_json 'CPU provider with arena off' '
    .provider == "CPUExecutionProvider" and .session_settings.cpu_arena == false
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check_json '10 GiB memory limit and measured phases' '
    .memory_limit_bytes == 10737418240 and .verdicts.memory_bounded == true and
    .verdicts.memory_phases_measured == true
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check_json 'Installed source, cutout and mask hashes for every fixture and replay' '
    {source: true, cutout: true, mask: true} as $match |
    .verdicts.installed_artifacts_match == true and
    .installed_hash_matches == {bust: $match, green_eyes: $match, smaller_bust: $match, replay: $match}
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check_json 'All smoke verdicts' '.passed == true' <<< "$report" || status=1
  exit "$status"
)

Measured on 2026-11-25. The first Job was OOMKilled after 14 s under the unmeasured 6 GiB budget. Retry studio-matting-smoke-01-r2 peaked at 12,997,890,048 bytes in the worker and 13,150,916,608 bytes for the sum of process peaks. Fixture quality and replay passed. The retest studio-matting-smoke-02-r3 passed all 13 verdicts with the CPU arena disabled and byte-identical cutouts and masks. Its worker peaked at 7,538,561,024 bytes, with a 7,691,853,824-byte bound for the sum of process peaks. CR-43 sets the new request and limit from these measurements. The plain smoke with the pinned serving profile passed all 13 verdicts in 48 s with a 7,626,436,608-byte upper bound. OP459, comments 9969, 9985 and 10004

Record the Ops Git revision, both Job names and statuses, published image digest, verified graph and profile hashes, smoke JSON and deployed health on OP459. Record the private allocation in the story handoff. The synthetic result establishes installed smoke behavior. OP451 owns the private cast quality and serving integration. Tom owns acceptance.

docs.title: Run the private cast quality trial
docs.text:
Expected. The saga coordinator chooses one existing cast photo of an imported production under CR-46 and uses its read-only path and recorded SHA-256. Use the content-addressed store path /studio/productions/<prd_id>/sha256/<first-two-hex>/<sha256>.<jpg|png> or /studio/library/sha256/<first-two-hex>/<sha256>.<jpg|png> for global scope. Choose a representative still with eyes, lashes and hair visible, and use the target height for its pinned cast slot. Keep the path, asset IDs and output locator private. Mark the iris interiors and visible hair before the trial. Run in an exclusive heavy-job window as for the smoke, including no concurrent Foley or heavy render. The block checks fresh node load, render load, Wan readiness and idleness for video and Foley, and the shared image queue.

The staged template emits one Job with inline scripts. Its dedicated studio-matting-quality deny-all policy must be live before admission. The init container uses UID/GID 1000 to reserve a new group-writable /studio/jobs/<job> directory exclusively. The main container uses the smoke's UID/GID 10001, pinned image and read-only weights. Supplemental group 1000 allows it to write cutout.png, mask.png and the completed report.json under just that directory's writable subPath. The input directory has its own read-only subPath. The gate checks the canonical path, regular single-link file and SHA-256 match before opening the run window. The report identifies the input by SHA-256. The Job spec contains the store's hash-based locator and expires one hour after finishing. As in the provisioning budget, leave 32 GiB free after allowing 1 GiB and 32 filesystem entries. The NFS inode reading may be unavailable under CR-33.

The final log line reports invalid input, a hash mismatch, an existing output, unavailable readiness, a service refusal, failed verification or a timeout with distinct trial.* codes. Service refusals include the backend's adapter.* code. If output reservation fails, the report comes from the init container.

Set STUDIO_TRIAL_INPUT to the absolute Studio-share path, STUDIO_TRIAL_SOURCE_SHA256 to the pinned byte digest, STUDIO_TRIAL_ASSET_VERSION to the asv_ ID, STUDIO_TRIAL_PRODUCTION to the prd_ ID (or - for global scope), STUDIO_TRIAL_JOB_ID to the evidence's job_ ID and STUDIO_TRIAL_TARGET_HEIGHT to the slot height in pixels. Run from the checked-out Ops revision.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  : "${STUDIO_TRIAL_INPUT:?Set the private input path}"
  : "${STUDIO_TRIAL_SOURCE_SHA256:?Set the pinned byte digest}"
  : "${STUDIO_TRIAL_ASSET_VERSION:?Set the pinned asset version}"
  : "${STUDIO_TRIAL_PRODUCTION:?Set the production or - for global scope}"
  : "${STUDIO_TRIAL_JOB_ID:?Set the canonical job ID for the receipt}"
  : "${STUDIO_TRIAL_TARGET_HEIGHT:?Set the pinned slot height}"

  check() {
    local label=$1
    shift
    if "$@"; then
      printf 'PASS %s\n' "$label"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$label" >&2
      return 1
    fi
  }
  assert_json() {
    jq -es "$@" >/dev/null
  }
  is_sha256() { [[ $1 =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; }
  read_endpoint() {
    kubectl -n ai exec "$1" -c "$2" -- python -B -c '
import sys
from urllib.request import urlopen
with urlopen(sys.argv[1], timeout=5) as response:
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(response.read())
' "$3"
  }
  node_idle() {
    kubectl top node talosw01 --no-headers | awk '
      {print} $1 == "talosw01" && $3 ~ /^[0-9]+%$/ && $5 ~ /^[0-9]+%$/ &&
       $3+0 <= 10 && $5+0 <= 25 {ok=1} END {exit !ok}'
  }
  render_idle() {
    kubectl -n ai top pod --containers -l app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-render --no-headers |
      awk '{print} $2 == "app" && $3 ~ /^[0-9]+m$/ {
        seen=1; if ($3+0 > 250) busy=1
      } END {exit (!seen || busy)}'
  }
  room_on_share() {
    kubectl -n ai exec deploy/studio-render -c app -- sh -ec '
      df -Pk /studio/jobs | awk "NR == 2 { print; if (\$4 >= 34603008) ok=1 } END { exit !ok }"
      df -Pi /studio/jobs | awk "NR == 2 { print; if (\$4 == \"-\" || \$4 >= 32) ok=1 } END { exit !ok }"
    '
  }
  input_matches_store_hash() {
    local hash=$STUDIO_TRIAL_SOURCE_SHA256 root stem
    is_sha256 "$hash" || return 1
    if [[ $STUDIO_TRIAL_PRODUCTION == - ]]; then
      root=/studio/library
    else
      [[ $STUDIO_TRIAL_PRODUCTION =~ ^prd_[0-7][0-9a-hjkmnp-tv-z]{25}$ ]] || return 1
      root="/studio/productions/$STUDIO_TRIAL_PRODUCTION"
    fi
    stem="$root/sha256/${hash:0:2}/$hash"
    [[ $STUDIO_TRIAL_INPUT == "$stem.jpg" || $STUDIO_TRIAL_INPUT == "$stem.png" ]] || return 1
    kubectl -n ai exec deploy/studio-render -c app -- sh -ec '
      path=$1
      test "$(realpath -e -- "$path")" = "$path"
      test -f "$path"
      test "$(stat -c %h -- "$path")" = 1
      sum=$(sha256sum -- "$path")
      test "${sum%% *}" = "$2"
    ' sh "$STUDIO_TRIAL_INPUT" "$hash" >/dev/null 2>&1
  }
  read_profile() {
    profile=$(kubectl -n ai exec deploy/studio-render -c app -- cat \
      "/studio/jobs/$allocation/weights/profile.sha256" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    is_sha256 "$profile"
  }
  deny_all() {
    kubectl -n ai get ciliumnetworkpolicy studio-matting-quality -o json |
      assert_json 'length == 1 and .[0].spec == {
        "endpointSelector":{"matchLabels":{"app.kubernetes.io/name":"studio-matting-quality"}},
        "ingressDeny":[{"fromEntities":["all"]}], "egressDeny":[{"toEntities":["all"]}]}'
  }
  wan_idle() {
    read_endpoint deploy/wan-video api http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/ready |
      assert_json 'length == 1 and (.[0] | .ready == true and
        has("active_video_job") and .active_video_job == null and
        has("active_foley_job") and .active_foley_job == null)'
  }
  images_idle() {
    read_endpoint comfyui-0 app http://127.0.0.1:8188/queue |
      assert_json 'length == 1 and (.[0] | .queue_running == [] and .queue_pending == [])'
  }
  stage=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio/matting-pending
  allocation=$(yq -e '.data.allocation' "$stage/release/release.yaml") || exit 1
  pin=$(yq -e '.data.image' "$stage/release/release.yaml") || exit 1
  check 'Content-addressed regular single-link input matches its SHA-256' input_matches_store_hash || exit 1
  check 'Installed profile hash present' read_profile || exit 1
  check 'Share byte and inode budget' room_on_share || exit 1
  check 'Deny-all network policy' deny_all || exit 1
  check 'talosw01 CPU at most 10% and memory at most 25%' node_idle || exit 1
  check 'Render app CPU at most 250m' render_idle || exit 1
  check 'Wan idle' wan_idle || exit 1
  check 'Shared image queue empty' images_idle || exit 1
  printf 'PASS quality trial admission\n'

  private_path=${STUDIO_TRIAL_INPUT#/studio/}
  export TRIAL_INPUT_DIR="data/studio/${private_path%/*}" TRIAL_INPUT_NAME="${private_path##*/}"
  export TRIAL_PROFILE="$profile"
  export STUDIO_TRIAL_SOURCE_SHA256 STUDIO_TRIAL_ASSET_VERSION STUDIO_TRIAL_PRODUCTION
  export STUDIO_TRIAL_JOB_ID STUDIO_TRIAL_TARGET_HEIGHT
  suffix=$(openssl rand -hex 6) || exit 1
  export TRIAL_OUTPUT="studio-matting-quality-$suffix"
  manifest=$(kustomize build "$stage/quality" | yq -e '
    .metadata.name = strenv(TRIAL_OUTPUT) |
    .spec.template.spec.initContainers[0].args += [strenv(TRIAL_OUTPUT)] |
    (.spec.template.spec.containers[0].volumeMounts[] | select(.name == "input").subPath) =
      strenv(TRIAL_INPUT_DIR) |
    (.spec.template.spec.containers[0].volumeMounts[] | select(.name == "jobs").subPath) =
      ("data/studio/jobs/" + strenv(TRIAL_OUTPUT)) |
    .spec.template.spec.containers[0].args += [
      strenv(TRIAL_INPUT_NAME), strenv(STUDIO_TRIAL_SOURCE_SHA256),
      strenv(STUDIO_TRIAL_ASSET_VERSION), strenv(STUDIO_TRIAL_PRODUCTION), strenv(STUDIO_TRIAL_JOB_ID),
      strenv(STUDIO_TRIAL_TARGET_HEIGHT), strenv(TRIAL_PROFILE)
    ]') || exit 1
  kubectl -n ai create -f - <<< "$manifest" || exit 1

  wait_terminal() {
    local condition deadline=$((SECONDS + 330))
    while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
      condition=$(kubectl -n ai --request-timeout=10s get "job/$TRIAL_OUTPUT" -o json |
        jq -r '[.status.conditions[]? | select(.status == "True" and
          (.type == "Complete" or .type == "Failed" or .type == "FailureTarget"))][0].type // ""') || return 1
      case $condition in
        Complete) return 0 ;;
        Failed|FailureTarget) return 1 ;;
      esac
      sleep 5
    done
    return 1
  }
  gate=0
  check 'Job completed successfully' wait_terminal || gate=1
  report=$(kubectl -n ai --request-timeout=10s logs "job/$TRIAL_OUTPUT" -c matting 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || report=
  if [[ -z $report ]]; then
    report=$(kubectl -n ai --request-timeout=10s logs "job/$TRIAL_OUTPUT" -c reserve-output 2>/dev/null |
      tail -n 1) || report=
  fi
  final_report() {
    assert_json 'length == 1 and (.[0] | type == "object")' <<< "$report"
  }
  report_check() {
    local predicate=$1
    shift
    assert_json "$@" "length == 1 and (.[0] | ($predicate))" <<< "$report"
  }
  check 'Final log line is a JSON report' final_report || gate=1
  check 'Expected source, image and profile hashes on CPU with arena off' report_check '
    .source_sha256 == $source and .profile_sha256 == $profile and
    .image_digest == $digest and .provider == "CPUExecutionProvider" and .cpu_arena == false
  ' --arg source "$STUDIO_TRIAL_SOURCE_SHA256" --arg profile "$profile" --arg digest "${pin##*@}" || gate=1
  check 'Cold load and request within limits with both memory phases measured' report_check '
    .startup_seconds > 0 and .startup_seconds <= 120 and .request_seconds > 0 and .request_seconds <= 35 and
    .worker_memory.session_creation.peak_rss_bytes > 0 and
    (.worker_memory.requests | length) == 1 and .worker_memory.requests[0].peak_rss_bytes > 0 and
    .peak_rss_upper_bound_bytes > 0 and .peak_rss_upper_bound_bytes <= .memory_limit_bytes and
    .memory_limit_bytes == 10737418240' || gate=1
  check 'Verified cutout, mask and size ratio' report_check '
    .passed == true and .shape.alpha_threshold == 128 and
    .shape.scale.numerator == $target and .shape.scale.denominator == .shape.bbox_height_px and
    ([.artifacts.cutout, .artifacts.mask] |
      all((.sha256 | test("^[0-9a-f]{64}$")) and .bytes > 0 and .media_type == "image/png"))
  ' --argjson target "$STUDIO_TRIAL_TARGET_HEIGHT" || gate=1
  if final_report; then
    printf '%s\n' "$report"
  fi
  if (( gate != 0 )); then
    printf 'FAIL quality trial technical checks\n' >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  printf 'PASS quality trial technical checks\n'
)

Within the private Studio workflow, composite the cutout over light and dark plates and inspect both at source zoom. Record the per-eye retention, both lash lines, at least 8 of 10 premarked visible flyaways, any halo and the hand corrections that would be needed. Save the numerical report and private locator on OP451. Keep quality acceptance pending until Tom judges the private result.

docs.title: Activation, retries and rollback
docs.text:
Read-only accounting on 2026-11-25 showed 105.98 GiB allocatable and 54.29 GiB requested, including Wan (24 GiB requested, 64 GiB limit), Foley (12 GiB, 32 GiB) and their API (128 MiB, 512 MiB). Adding the dormant local-model sidecar (8 GiB, 16 GiB) and one matting instance (8 GiB, 10 GiB) leaves 35.69 GiB unrequested. Existing limits sum to 239,904 MiB. At their limits, Wan, local model, the Studio queue worker and matting alone consume 98 GiB before offline render, Foley or other workloads. The node cannot carry those peaks simultaneously. Keep heavy jobs serialized unless measured headroom shows the second fits. Follow the Wan, Foley and local-model lease rules. Matting profile

Sidecar activation after the smoke is tracked in story 970. The staged overlay below predates that story. First move the offline worker's Flux path to studio-render/matting-pending and verify its 1 GiB request and 18-CPU, 32 GiB limit. Cap offline render commands at --workers 16. Then stage the queue consumer with studio/matting-pending/activation. The worker has 4 CPUs, 2 GiB requested and an 8 GiB limit. The matting sidecar has 2 CPUs, 8 GiB requested and a 10 GiB limit. The two pods total 24 CPUs and 50 GiB. The segmentation activation overlay builds on this render split and comes after matting. The serving command uses the same arena-off profile as the plain smoke. The sidecar uses a shared, group-writable /matting emptyDir and the read-only /weights mount. Only the worker keeps its API credential and media mounts. Stage per-attempt directories with shared GID 10001, permissions 2770, and an input readable by that group. Check studio-matting ready in the activated pod before sending any dispatch.

If provisioning fails, preserve the logs and failed allocation. Investigate the code before deciding whether a fresh run is appropriate. A reviewed change to data.allocation selects the next two-digit suffix for the two Job names and their corresponding weights mount. Keep the original allocation intact. After a smoke failure, retain the exact model and any reported scores and record the coordinator's ruling before a new attempt.

After both Jobs finish, capture their evidence before the 24-hour Job TTL removes their objects and pods. The coordinator can remove the studio-matting-policy Flux object and the provision/smoke templates in a follow-up GitOps PR. Update their release guard with the removal. Pruning removes the ConfigMap and targeted policies. Preserve the immutable allocation, selected pin and staged serving overlay.

To roll back before activation, withdraw the one-shot stage in Git and stop launching Jobs. Let an existing Job reach its bound and preserve any data it wrote. After activation, disable dispatch first and revert the Studio worker's Flux path before restoring the offline 20-CPU path. Preserve the weights and artifacts regardless of the rollback. Reconcile and verify the previously authorized workloads after the Git changes.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  kubectl -n ai get kustomization studio-worker studio-render
  kubectl -n ai get deploy studio-worker studio-render -o wide
  kubectl -n ai get deploy studio-worker studio-render -o json | jq -e '
    .items | length == 2 and all(.[]; .status.availableReplicas >= 1)
  '
)

docs.title: Stage Studio segmentation
docs.text: CR-34 selects Grounding DINO Tiny followed by SAM 2.1 Hiera Tiny on CPU. One immutable allocation contains both safetensors files, their allowlisted processor and tokenizer files, and the image-bound profile. Flux installs the two policies and the provisioner script. The coordinator creates the provisioning and serving smoke Jobs individually. OP460 · Profile and fixture thresholds

docs.title: Pin and reconcile the policy
docs.text:
Merge the Studio source PR first. In its Studio images run on main, take the published ghcr.io/thaynes43/haynes-studio-segmentation@sha256:<digest> for that revision. Record the image byte size and the run's studio-segmentation-sbom-<revision> artifact. Set only data.image in release.yaml before merging the serving release for allocation segmentation-op460-dino-sam-v1-06. The release guard refuses the previous smoke digests, including the current pin from allocation 05, and verifies the published OCI config for the new digest. The serving contract pins memory-mapped loads, a 4 GiB request and a 5 GiB limit. Run the blocks below from the merged Ops revision.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  check() {
    local name=$1
    shift
    if "$@"; then printf 'PASS %s\n' "$name"; else printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$name" >&2; return 1; fi
  }
  check 'Cluster source reconciled' flux reconcile kustomization cluster-apps -n flux-system --with-source
  check 'Segmentation policy reconciled' flux reconcile kustomization studio-segmentation-policy -n ai
  check 'Segmentation policy ready' kubectl -n ai wait --for=condition=ready \
    kustomization/studio-segmentation-policy --timeout=2m
  status=0
  check 'Provision and smoke policy present' kubectl -n ai get ciliumnetworkpolicy \
    studio-segmentation-provision studio-segmentation-smoke || status=1
  check 'Offline render ready' kubectl -n ai rollout status deploy/studio-render --timeout=30s || status=1
  exit "$status"
)

Only the download Job has DNS and HTTPS to the two observed publisher hosts, huggingface.co and us.aws.cdn.hf.co. Both Job pod selectors and the CoreDNS peer use app.kubernetes.io/name. The smoke Job denies all ingress and egress. The serve process uses the local Unix socket and the image's offline runtime.

docs.title: Provision one new allocation
docs.text:
Changed (2026-11-25): the first provisioning Job refused the share. studio-segmentation-provision-01 exited in one second with free_file_reserve_too_small before creating anything. The Studio share reports a file total but -1 for free files; the provisioner treated only "no file total" as an unreported count and compared -1 with the reserve. The runbook's own df gate had passed, because df shows - there. The provisioner now treats a negative or all-ones free count as unreported (CR-34's accepted case) and still enforces a count that is reported. No allocation directory was created by the failed Job; a Job's name cannot be reused, so the measuring retry used suffix 02. The serving image gets its own allocation and profile hash.

The Job runs at 1000:1000 on talosw01 with a 1 GiB limit. The downloader syncs to NFS and drops cached pages every 64 MiB. It rehashes the staged bytes, syncs the files and publishes the manifest and both verified directories together. The only writable mount is the existing Studio jobs subtree. A failed allocation remains private and needs a fresh suffix for the next attempt. Use the 2 GiB and 64-entry budget with 32 GiB and 1,024 entries in reserve. CR-34 accepts the bounded entry budget when NFS reports the inode count as unavailable. Published files are mode 0444 and directories are 0555, readable by the smoke and sidecar at 10001:10001.

Segmentation takes its pins from the image's two-model profile and publishes both safetensors sets, their allowlisted auxiliary files and the profile in a single rename. Matting stages one ONNX graph and its bundled licence. The larger payload accounts for the 2 GiB budget and 540 s download deadline. The entry budget covers the two model directories and their auxiliary files. Segmentation allows exact same-host cache redirects for auxiliary files and releases read-back pages every 64 MiB to bound the two-model rehash. The provisioners each ship in a stage-local hashed ConfigMap. The release tests check that their directory sync and write/cache flush functions match. Before creating the provisioning Job, require Wan's /v1/ready to report ready with both video and Foley job fields present and null.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  check() {
    local name=$1
    shift
    if "$@"; then printf 'PASS %s\n' "$name"; else printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$name" >&2; return 1; fi
  }
  stage=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio/segmentation-pending
  provision=$(kustomize build "$stage/provision" | yq -e 'select(.kind == "Job")') || exit 1
  job=$(yq -e '.metadata.name' <<< "$provision") || exit 1
  config=$(yq -e '.spec.template.spec.volumes[] | select(.name == "config") | .configMap.name' <<< "$provision") || exit 1
  allocation=$(yq -e '.data.allocation' "$stage/release/release.yaml") || exit 1
  image=$(yq -e '.data.image' "$stage/release/release.yaml") || exit 1
  check 'Flux provision script present' kubectl -n ai get "configmap/$config" -o name || exit 1
  check 'Studio byte and reported inode reserve' kubectl -n ai exec deploy/studio-render -c app -- sh -ec '
    df -Pk /studio/jobs | awk "NR == 2 { print; ok = (\$4 >= 35651584) } END { exit !ok }"
    df -Pi /studio/jobs | awk "NR == 2 { print; ok = (\$4 == \"-\" || \$4 >= 1088) } END { exit !ok }"
  ' || exit 1
  check 'Wan ready and video and Foley idle' bash scripts/studio-segmentation/check-wan-idle.sh || exit 1
  check 'Provision Job created' kubectl -n ai create -f - <<< "$provision" || exit 1
  status=0
  check 'Provision Job completed' bash scripts/studio-segmentation/wait-job.sh "$job" 660 || status=1
  report=$(kubectl -n ai --request-timeout=10s logs "job/$job" -c segmentation | grep '^{' | tail -n 1) || report=
  printf '%s\n' "$report"
  check 'Provision report matches both model pins and release' jq -e --arg allocation "$allocation" \
    --arg image "${image##*@}" '
    .allocation == $allocation and .image_digest == $image and .download_bytes == 846220082 and
    (.profile_sha256 | test("^[a-f0-9]{64}$")) and
    [.models[].files[0].sha256] == [
      "1a2412ef99bd74bcd3c2a246fa1e48581f8889a1300c9051974741314fc042f3",
      "48c14467e5cf9e51870511feb72c89688e82dd74523142c0538b663e193ac2a7"
    ]
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  if (( status )); then exit "$status"; fi
  profile=$(jq -er '.profile_sha256' <<< "$report")
  kubectl -n ai exec -i deploy/studio-render -c app -- python -B - "$allocation" "$profile" "${image##*@}" <<'PY'
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path
import json
import os
import sys

os.nice(10)
root = Path("/studio/jobs") / sys.argv[1] / "weights"
manifest = (root / "profile.json").read_bytes()
pin = sha256(manifest).hexdigest()
document = json.loads(manifest)
checks = {
    "profile digest": pin == sys.argv[2] == (root / "profile.sha256").read_text().strip(),
    "serving profile identity": document["profile"] == "grounding-dino-tiny-sam2.1-tiny-cpu-v2"
        and document["image_digest"] == sys.argv[3],
    "serving load and memory": document["parameters"]["weight_load"] == "mmap"
        and document["resources"]["serving"] == {"weight_load": "mmap", "request_gib": 4, "limit_gib": 5},
}
for model in document["models"]:
    for entry in model["files"]:
        path = root / model["directory"] / entry["name"]
        digest = sha256()
        try:
            with path.open("rb", buffering=0) as source:
                while block := source.read(1024**2):
                    digest.update(block)
                    if source.tell() % (64 * 1024**2) == 0:
                        os.posix_fadvise(source.fileno(), 0, 0, os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)
                os.posix_fadvise(source.fileno(), 0, 0, os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)
            good = path.stat().st_size == entry["size_bytes"] and digest.hexdigest() == entry["sha256"]
        except OSError:
            good = False
        checks[f"{model['directory']}/{entry['name']}"] = good
for label, good in checks.items():
    print(f"{'PASS' if good else 'FAIL'} {label}")
raise SystemExit(not all(checks.values()))
PY
)

docs.title: Run the serving smoke
docs.text:
Reserve an exclusive heavy-job window on talosw01. The idle gate requires current node CPU at most 10%, node memory at most 25%, the render app at most 250m CPU, Wan ready with both video and Foley job fields present and null, and a clear shared ComfyUI queue. Record the readings and hold competing heavy render, Wan, Foley and local model work for this window.

Expected. studio-segmentation-smoke-06 requests and limits two CPUs, requests 4 GiB and has a 5 GiB limit. It runs at 10001:10001 with read-only weights. Plain studio-segmentation smoke loads the serving profile once and runs the six fixture requests three times, for eighteen fixture calls. Pass 1 warms the models. From pass 2 to pass 3, the residency check allows up to 64 MiB of growth in the maximum worker resident RSS and the maximum cgroup resident memory across all request phases. The end-of-pass cgroup sample is recorded for diagnosis. Startup and inference keep their 60 s bounds. The smoke stops starting fixture calls when fewer than 65 s remain in its 840 s run budget, leaving time to report a failure before the Job's 900 s deadline. The Job has zero retries. Allocation 03's twelve calls took about 58 s. At the same rate, eighteen calls should take about 87 s plus the cold load.

(
  set -euo pipefail
  check() {
    local name=$1
    shift
    if "$@"; then printf 'PASS %s\n' "$name"; else printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$name" >&2; return 1; fi
  }
  endpoint() {
    kubectl -n ai exec "$1" -c "$2" -- python -B -c '
import sys
from urllib.request import urlopen
with urlopen(sys.argv[1], timeout=5) as response:
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(response.read())
' "$3"
  }
  stage=kubernetes/main/apps/ai/studio/segmentation-pending
  allocation=$(yq -e '.data.allocation' "$stage/release/release.yaml") || exit 1
  image=$(yq -e '.data.image' "$stage/release/release.yaml") || exit 1
  limit_bytes=5368709120
  provision="studio-segmentation-provision-${allocation##*-}"
  check 'Provision Job complete' bash scripts/studio-segmentation/wait-job.sh "$provision" 15 || exit 1
  provision_report=$(kubectl -n ai --request-timeout=10s logs "job/$provision" -c segmentation |
    grep '^{' | tail -n 1) || exit 1
  check 'Provision profile digest matches this allocation and image' jq -e --arg allocation "$allocation" \
    --arg image "${image##*@}" '
    .allocation == $allocation and .image_digest == $image and
    (.profile_sha256 | test("^[a-f0-9]{64}$"))
  ' <<< "$provision_report" || exit 1
  profile=$(jq -er '.profile_sha256' <<< "$provision_report") || exit 1
  node=$(kubectl top node talosw01 --no-headers) || exit 1
  printf '%s\n' "$node"
  check 'Node load within smoke window' awk '
    $1 == "talosw01" && $3 ~ /^[0-9]+%$/ && $5 ~ /^[0-9]+%$/ && $3+0 <= 10 && $5+0 <= 25 { ok = 1 }
    END { exit !ok }
  ' <<< "$node" || exit 1
  render=$(kubectl -n ai top pod --containers -l app.kubernetes.io/name=studio-render --no-headers) || exit 1
  printf '%s\n' "$render"
  check 'Offline render app idle' awk '
    $2 == "app" { count++; ok = ($3 ~ /^[0-9]+m$/ && $3+0 <= 250) }
    END { exit !(count == 1 && ok) }
  ' <<< "$render" || exit 1
  check 'Wan ready and video and Foley idle' bash scripts/studio-segmentation/check-wan-idle.sh || exit 1
  endpoint comfyui-0 app http://127.0.0.1:8188/queue | check 'Shared ComfyUI queue empty' jq -es '
    length == 1 and (.[0] | .queue_running == [] and .queue_pending == [])
  ' || exit 1
  smoke=$(kustomize build "$stage/smoke") || exit 1
  job=$(yq -e '.metadata.name' <<< "$smoke") || exit 1
  check 'Smoke Job created' kubectl -n ai create -f - <<< "$smoke" || exit 1
  status=0
  check 'Smoke Job completed' bash scripts/studio-segmentation/wait-job.sh "$job" 960 || status=1
  report=$(kubectl -n ai --request-timeout=10s logs "job/$job" -c segmentation | grep '^{' | tail -n 1) || report=null
  printf '%s\n' "$report"
  check 'Smoke report JSON line' jq -es 'length == 1 and (.[0] | type == "object")' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check 'Exact image, profile and serving load setting' jq -e --arg image "${image##*@}" --arg profile "$profile" '
    .schema == "studio.segmentation-smoke/v1" and .mode == "serving" and
    .image_digest == $image and .profile_sha256 == $profile and
    .profile_id == "grounding-dino-tiny-sam2.1-tiny-cpu-v2" and [.runs[].weight_load] == ["mmap"]
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check '5 GiB cgroup limit and peak' jq -e --argjson limit "$limit_bytes" '
    .cgroup_limit_bytes == $limit and .verdicts.cgroup_allowance == true and
    (.cgroup_peak_bytes | type == "number" and . > 0 and . <= $limit)
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check 'Cold start and memory phases for all eighteen calls' jq -e --argjson limit "$limit_bytes" '
    .runs[0] |
    (.cold_load_ms | type == "number" and . >= 0 and . <= 60000) and .verdicts.phase_memory == true and
    (.memory.startup | keys == ["load_dino", "load_sam", "runtime_import", "verify_profile_and_files"]) and
    (.memory.requests | length == 18 and all(.[]; has("source_validation"))) and
    ([.memory.startup, .memory.requests[]] |
      all(.[]; all(.[]; .phase_rss_peak_reset == true and
        ([.peak_rss_bytes, .resident_rss_bytes, .cgroup_resident_bytes, .cgroup_peak_since_start_bytes] |
          all(.[]; type == "number" and . > 0 and . <= $limit)))))
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check 'Both resident memory maxima grow by at most 64 MiB from pass 2 to pass 3' jq -e --argjson limit "$limit_bytes" '
    def stable:
      type == "array" and length == 3 and
      all(.[1,2]; type == "number" and . > 0 and . <= $limit) and
      .[2] <= .[1] + 67108864;
    .runs[0] |
    .memory.passes as $passes |
    .verdicts.memory_stable == true and $passes.tolerance_bytes == 67108864 and $passes.compared_passes == [2, 3] and
    all($passes | .max_resident_rss_bytes, .max_cgroup_resident_bytes; stable)
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check 'Exact readiness before and after all three passes' jq -e --arg profile "$profile" '
    {profile_id: "grounding-dino-tiny-sam2.1-tiny-cpu-v1", profile_sha256: $profile, device: "cpu"} as $ready |
    .runs[0] | .readiness == {initial: $ready, after: $ready} and
    .verdicts.ready_initial == true and .verdicts.ready_after == true
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check 'All eighteen fixture statuses and create-only replay' jq -e '
    .runs[0] as $run |
    ($run.cases | length == 18) and $run.verdicts.create_only_replay == true and
    all(["", "_repeat", "_third"][]; . as $suffix |
      $run.verdicts["visibility" + $suffix] == true and
      $run.verdicts["hidden_prop_fails_fixture_gate" + $suffix] == true and
      $run.cases["absent_gavel" + $suffix].status == "needs_hint" and
      all(["foreground", "visible_face", "hidden_prop", "point", "grounded_ball"][];
        $run.cases[. + $suffix].status == "ready"))
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check 'Smoke report passed within its time budget' jq -e '
    .passed == true and .runs[0].verdicts.time_budget == true and
    all(.verdicts[]; . == true) and all(.runs[0].verdicts[]; . == true)
  ' <<< "$report" || status=1
  check 'Offline render ready after smoke' kubectl -n ai rollout status deploy/studio-render --timeout=30s || status=1
  exit "$status"
)

Keep the final JSON report with the story. Record the cold start, per-case wall times, per-phase worker peak and resident RSS, and container cgroup peak, limit and resident bytes. Save all three passes' phase samples, resident maxima and end-of-pass cgroup samples. The 64 MiB tolerance allows allocator and page-cache variation. The Job waits stop on Complete or Failed. A failed poll can recover at the next read. On failure or timeout, the wait prints the Job, pod termination state when available and container logs. The visible-face and hidden-prop fractions exercise the fixed synthetic arrangement. Story 452 owns real fixture quality and the adapter's build-time layout decision.
